---
# Title, subtitle and author are placeholders: the "report title" chunk after
# Set Parameters replaces them with values from config.yaml (output.report_title,
# output.report_author, dataset.id/version/target and the taxonomic level), so a
# report is named after what it actually models, whatever the data.
title: "TabFlux report"
date: today   # resolved by Quarto at render time, so every report carries its own run date
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    fig-width: 10
    fig-height: 7
    fig-dpi: 150
    out-width: "100%"
# Open as plain text in VS Code, Positron and RStudio: each cell then has its
# Run Cell controls. The visual editor also rewrites this commented header.
editor: source
always_allow_html: yes
editor_options: 
  chunk_output_type: console
---

#### Project Setup

Locates the repository root and stores it as `WORKDIR`: config.yaml, `R/` and `input/` live there, the notebook one level down in `analysis/`. Works under `quarto render`, in an IDE, and under `scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R`. Every later chunk builds its paths from `WORKDIR`. No data is read here.

```{r setting wd, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Find the repository root. The notebook lives in analysis/; config.yaml, the
# R/ helpers and the input/ data sit at the root.
# Output: WORKDIR. Every later chunk builds its paths from it, because knitr
# resets the working directory between chunks.
# Two optional environment variables steer the search, both set by
# scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R for each child render (along with
# TABFLUX_CONFIG, which the next chunk reads):
#   TABFLUX_NOTEBOOK_PATH  – this .qmd; the search starts there and walks up
#                            one parent folder at a time
#   TABFLUX_WORKDIR  – the root itself (last-resort fallback)
resolve_project_root <- function() {

  # A directory is the project root if it contains config.yaml, R/, and input/.
  # scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R has its own copy of this test that also
  # requires analysis/ (it must find the .qmd to render); this one leaves
  # analysis/ out on purpose. Keep the three shared conditions identical.
  is_project_root <- function(path) {
    file.exists(file.path(path, "config.yaml")) &&
      dir.exists(file.path(path, "R")) &&
      dir.exists(file.path(path, "input"))
  }

  # Try multiple sources to locate the current notebook file, in priority order:
  # 1. Explicit env var  2. knitr (with/without dir)  3. RStudio API
  discover_notebook_path <- function() {
    candidates <- c(
      Sys.getenv("TABFLUX_NOTEBOOK_PATH", unset = ""),
      tryCatch(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), error = function(e) ""),
      tryCatch(knitr::current_input(), error = function(e) ""),
      tryCatch({
        if (requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE) && rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
          rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path
        } else {
          ""
        }
      }, error = function(e) "")
    )

    candidates <- candidates[nzchar(candidates)]
    if (!length(candidates)) {
      return("")
    }

    normalizePath(candidates[[1]], winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  }

  notebook_path <- discover_notebook_path()

  # Walk up the directory tree from the notebook location until the root is found.
  if (nzchar(notebook_path)) {
    notebook_dir <- if (dir.exists(notebook_path)) notebook_path else dirname(notebook_path)
    search_path <- notebook_dir

    repeat {
      if (is_project_root(search_path)) {
        return(search_path)
      }

      parent_path <- dirname(search_path)
      if (identical(parent_path, search_path)) {
        # Reached the filesystem root without finding the project root.
        break
      }
      search_path <- parent_path
    }
  }

  # Fallback: check the current working directory, its parent, and the
  # TABFLUX_WORKDIR env var (useful for non-interactive rendering).
  candidate_paths <- c(
    getwd(),
    dirname(getwd()),
    file.path(getwd(), ".."),
    Sys.getenv("TABFLUX_WORKDIR", unset = "")
  )

  candidate_paths <- unique(vapply(candidate_paths[nzchar(candidate_paths)], function(path) {
    normalizePath(path, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  }, character(1)))

  for (candidate_path in candidate_paths) {
    if (is_project_root(candidate_path)) {
      return(candidate_path)
    }
  }

  stop("Could not resolve the project root. Set TABFLUX_WORKDIR before rendering.")
}

# setwd() only holds for this chunk under knitr, which restores the directory
# afterwards. That is why later chunks always write file.path(WORKDIR, ...).
WORKDIR <- resolve_project_root()
setwd(WORKDIR)
```

#### Methods and Libraries

Reads config.yaml, loads the R packages and the helpers in `R/`, and binds the Python runtime when TabPFN is picked.

TabPFN is a transformer pre-trained on synthetic tables. Its weights are not updated on your data: the training samples are passed as context at prediction time, and each prediction averages several forward passes (eight for TabPFN-3.5). It exists only as a Python package, so R must be pointed at its environment before any Python call, and the weights download on first use. The checks below fail early, with a readable message, when that setup is wrong.

No data is read here.

```{r sourcing pkgs, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# The config loader below needs the yaml package. Tell R which server to
# download packages from first, so install.packages() also works when Quarto
# renders without a console to ask.
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
if (!requireNamespace("yaml", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("yaml")

# Config helpers: load_tabflux_config() reads config.yaml and fills in defaults;
# tabflux_first_non_empty() and tabflux_resolve_hf_token() are used further down.
# TABFLUX_CONFIG is how scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R hands each child render
# its own copy of config.yaml with tax_level cut down to a single rank; an
# interactive run reads the config.yaml at the project root instead.
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_config_helpers.R"))
config_path <- Sys.getenv("TABFLUX_CONFIG", unset = "config.yaml")
# Resolve a relative config path against the project root. knitr restores the
# working directory to analysis/ between chunks, so a bare "config.yaml" would
# resolve to analysis/config.yaml and the loader would stop. Same guard as for
# the input paths further down.
# An absolute path starts with "/" (Linux/macOS) or a drive letter (Windows).
is_absolute_path <- function(path) grepl("^(/|[A-Za-z]:)", path)
if (!is_absolute_path(config_path)) config_path <- file.path(WORKDIR, config_path)
tabflux_config <- load_tabflux_config(config_path)
message("Config source: ", normalizePath(config_path, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE))

# ── Method selection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Every classifier this notebook can tune. Names are mlr3's own learner ids
# ("classif.ranger", "classif.tabpfn", ...); values are the labels used in
# plots and tables. config methods.pick lists the subset to run; the shipped
# configs pick tabpfn and ranger (random forest), and the full cFMD category
# config adds xgboost.
#
# TabPFN needs the setup that follows: it exists only as a Python package, so R
# must be pointed at a Conda environment holding it, and it downloads its model
# weights on first use (v2.x with a Hugging Face token, HF_TOKEN; 3.x after a
# one-time licence acceptance on a Prior Labs account, which a non-interactive
# run confirms with the account's API key in TABPFN_TOKEN).
# Every other classifier here is a one-line R package load.
all_methods <- list(
  glmnet = "GLM elastic net",
  kknn = "K-Nearest Neighbor",
  mlp = "Multi-layer Perceptron",
  ranger = "Random Forest",
  svm = "Support Vector Machine",
  tabpfn = "TabPFN",
  xgboost = "XGBoost"
)

pick_method <- tabflux_config$methods$pick

# Keep only the picked methods; an unknown name is a config typo, stop now.
# `methods` (named list) drives the train / benchmark / prediction chunks.
# methods.pick lists learners explicitly; mlp and tabpfn cannot share one R
# session (check below).
miss <- setdiff(pick_method, names(all_methods))
if (length(miss)) stop(sprintf("Unknown methods: %s.", paste(miss, collapse = ", ")))
methods <- all_methods[pick_method]

# Two methods need extra runtimes: mlp needs R torch (mlr3torch); TabPFN needs
# Python through reticulate (the R package that starts a Python interpreter and
# talks to it from R). Both bring their own torch/CUDA libraries and cannot
# coexist in one R session, hence the check below.
needs_mlr3torch <- "mlp" %in% names(methods)
needs_tabpfn <- "tabpfn" %in% names(methods)

if (needs_mlr3torch && needs_tabpfn) {
  stop("Conflict: 'mlp' (mlr3torch) and 'tabpfn' (reticulate/Conda) cannot run in the same R session. ",
       "Remove one from 'pick_method' and rerun.")
}

# mlr3torch needs the libtorch backend, which the torch R package downloads
# separately from itself. Without it the learner builds and then throws
# "Lantern is not loaded" the first time it trains - after the download,
# preprocessing and feature selection have already run. Check it here instead.
# No GPU check: the MLP always trains on CPU (build_classification_learners()
# in R/tabflux_training_helpers.R sets device = "cpu").
if (needs_mlr3torch && !torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  stop("'mlp' needs the libtorch backend, which is not installed. ",
       "Install it with CUDA=cpu Rscript -e 'torch::install_torch()', ",
       "or drop 'mlp' from methods.pick.")
}

cat("Methods selected:\n"); print(methods)

# Locate the Conda installation root so we can find the TabPFN environment later.
# This must run before reticulate loads: otherwise reticulate attaches itself to
# whichever Python installation it finds first (e.g. a project-local ./venv) and
# the TabPFN environment stays unreachable for the rest of the session.
detect_conda_root <- function() {
  conda_bin <- ""
  # Try reticulate's API first; fall back to env var / PATH lookup.
  if (requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE)) {
    conda_bin <- tryCatch(reticulate::conda_binary(), error = function(e) "")
  }
  if (!nzchar(conda_bin)) {
    conda_bin <- Sys.getenv("CONDA_EXE", unset = Sys.which("conda"))
  }
  if (!nzchar(conda_bin)) {
    return("")  # Conda not found; TabPFN will fail later with a clear message.
  }
  dirname(dirname(conda_bin))  # conda root = two levels above the conda binary
}

# Resolve the paths needed to launch the TabPFN Conda environment.
# Priority per field: config.yaml (runtime.tabpfn) > environment
# variable > default. The config wins because it is this project's own
# statement of what it runs with; the TABPFN_* variables in ~/.Renviron are the
# machine-wide fallback shared with other projects. To point THIS project
# elsewhere, edit config.yaml (or blank the field there).
# Returns: env_name, conda_root, env_prefix (full env path), python.
resolve_tabpfn_runtime <- function() {
  tabpfn_cfg <- tabflux_config$runtime$tabpfn
  # Conda root directory (parent of the envs/ folder)
  conda_root <- tabflux_first_non_empty(
    tabpfn_cfg$conda_root, Sys.getenv("TABPFN_CONDA_ROOT"), detect_conda_root()
  )
  # Name (or full path) of the Conda environment containing TabPFN + PyTorch.
  # The fallback is the TabPFN-3.5 environment, matching the v3.5 fallback for
  # the model version below.
  env_name <- tabflux_first_non_empty(
    tabpfn_cfg$env_name, Sys.getenv("TABPFN_ENV_NAME"), default = "tabflux-tabpfn35-gpu"
  )
  # Full path to the environment folder. If env_name is already an existing
  # directory it is used as it stands; anything else is treated as a bare
  # environment name and glued under <conda_root>/envs/. Watch out: a full path
  # that does not exist yet also lands in the second branch, so the "Python not
  # found" guard below then reports that glued-together path.
  env_prefix <- if (dir.exists(env_name)) {
    normalizePath(env_name, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  } else {
    file.path(conda_root, "envs", env_name)
  }
  # Path to the Python binary inside the environment (config > env var > env_prefix)
  python <- tabflux_first_non_empty(
    tabpfn_cfg$python, Sys.getenv("TABPFN_PYTHON"), file.path(env_prefix, "bin", "python")
  )

  list(
    env_name = env_name,
    conda_root = conda_root,
    env_prefix = env_prefix,
    python = python
  )
}

# First TabPFN step: point every Python-related environment variable at the
# Conda env BEFORE any package is loaded. Packages attached below (reticulate,
# mlr3extralearners) may initialise Python on load, and reticulate reads these
# variables only at that moment. The second step (binding + checks) follows
# after the packages are attached.
if (needs_tabpfn) {
  tabpfn_runtime <- resolve_tabpfn_runtime()
  TABPFN_MODEL_VERSION <- tabflux_first_non_empty(
    tabflux_config$runtime$tabpfn$model_version, Sys.getenv("TABPFN_MODEL_VERSION"), default = "v3.5"
  )
  # Set these *before* reticulate starts up, so every later Python import lands
  # in the same TabPFN interpreter — including imports inside the background R
  # processes used for parallel work.
  # PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF lets PyTorch reuse GPU memory more flexibly, so a long
  # run does not run out while memory is still free; the other three switch off
  # the usage statistics Hugging Face and TabPFN send to their developers.
  Sys.setenv(
    PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF = "expandable_segments:True",
    TABPFN_DISABLE_TELEMETRY = "1",
    HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY = "1",
    DO_NOT_TRACK = "1",
    TABPFN_MODEL_VERSION = TABPFN_MODEL_VERSION,
    RETICULATE_MINICONDA_PATH = tabpfn_runtime$conda_root,
    RETICULATE_PYTHON = tabpfn_runtime$python,
    PATH = paste(dirname(tabpfn_runtime$python), Sys.getenv("PATH"), sep = .Platform$path.sep)
  )
  # Prepend the env's lib/ directory to LD_LIBRARY_PATH so PyTorch's shared
  # libraries (libcuda, etc.) are found at runtime on Linux. A running process
  # cannot change its own loader path, so this reaches only the worker processes
  # started later. For the render itself scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R sets
  # LD_LIBRARY_PATH before starting quarto; a direct `quarto render` needs it
  # exported in the shell (see docs/troubleshooting.md).
  tabpfn_lib_dir <- file.path(tabpfn_runtime$env_prefix, "lib")
  if (dir.exists(tabpfn_lib_dir)) {
    ld_parts <- c(tabpfn_lib_dir, Sys.getenv("LD_LIBRARY_PATH", unset = ""))
    Sys.setenv(LD_LIBRARY_PATH = paste(ld_parts[nzchar(ld_parts)], collapse = .Platform$path.sep))
  }
  message("Using TabPFN env: ", tabpfn_runtime$env_name)
}

# ── Package loading ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# is_installed(): TRUE if the package is in the library. Works before pacman
# is available, which is why it is not pacman::p_isinstalled().
is_installed <- function(pkg) pkg %in% rownames(installed.packages())

# mlr3extralearners is not on CRAN: it holds the community learners, including
# the TabPFN wrapper (classif.tabpfn). Installed once from GitHub via remotes.
if (!is_installed("remotes")) install.packages("remotes")
if (!is_installed("mlr3extralearners")) remotes::install_github("mlr-org/mlr3extralearners@*release")

if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pacman")

# Load conflicted first and settle the 'cor' clash before anything else
# attaches: without this, loading zCompositions (whose dependencies call cor()
# on attach) errors under conflicted, and pacman then re-downloads the package
# on every single render believing it is broken.
pacman::p_load("conflicted")
conflict_prefer("cor", "stats", quiet = TRUE)

# Everything the notebook needs, grouped by role:
#   mlr3*, paradox            – tasks, tuning, filters, wrapper feature selection
#   mlr3learners, ranger, kknn – the classic learners and their mlr3 wrappers
#   compositions, zCompositions – zero replacement + CLR for the ordination plots
#   Rtsne – t-SNE; factoextra – the PCA plots (the PCA itself is base R prcomp())
#   smotefamily – SMOTE; iml – SHAP values; stabm, fastVoteR – selection stability
#   future, future.apply, callr, progressr – parallel workers and progress bars
#   tidyverse, data.table, magrittr – data handling; patchwork – multi-panel figures
base_pkgs <- c(
  "callr","compositions","data.table","emoa",
  "factoextra","fastVoteR","FSelectorRcpp","future",
  "future.apply","jsonlite","kknn","iml","magrittr","mlr3filters","mlr3fselect","mlr3hyperband",
  "mlr3learners","mlr3pipelines","mlr3tuning",
  "mlr3viz","paradox","parallel","patchwork",
  "progressr","ranger","scales","smotefamily","stabm","tidyverse","Rtsne",
  "zCompositions"
)

# mlr3fairness is loaded ONLY when a protected attribute is configured. It is
# not a passive dependency: on load it registers an extra 'pta' column role on
# every mlr3 task. Parallel tuning workers that have not loaded it then reject
# those tasks ("extra elements {'pta'}"), so keeping it out of sessions that
# don't use fairness metrics avoids the mismatch entirely.
pta_setting <- tabflux_config$dataset$pta
pta_configured <- length(pta_setting) > 0 && nzchar(trimws(as.character(pta_setting[[1]])))
if (pta_configured) base_pkgs <- c(base_pkgs, "mlr3fairness")

# Installed but deliberately not attached with library(); called as
# package::function() instead:
#   R.utils – lets data.table::fread() read .csv.gz input directly. Attaching
#             it would mask many base R functions of the same name.
#   digest  – md5 hashes for the sequence-based feature IDs
#             (tabflux_data_helpers.R).
for (ns_pkg in c("R.utils", "digest")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(ns_pkg, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(ns_pkg)
}

# Method-dependent extras. mlr3extralearners is attached either way (of the
# methods above only tabpfn lives there); reticulate only when TabPFN
# must talk to Python; mlr3torch only for the MLP.
torch_pkgs   <- if (needs_mlr3torch) c("mlr3torch") else character()
tabpfn_pkgs  <- if (needs_tabpfn) c("reticulate","mlr3extralearners") else "mlr3extralearners"

# Attach everything in one go; p_load installs from CRAN whatever is missing.
pkgs <- unique(c(base_pkgs, torch_pkgs, tabpfn_pkgs))
do.call(pacman::p_load, c(as.list(pkgs), install = TRUE))

# Several attached packages define functions with the same name; state once
# which one wins when the name is used unqualified. dplyr's verbs clash with
# stats (filter) and data.table (first); compositions::var beats stats::var.
conflict_prefer("select", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("rename", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("mutate", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("first", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("var", "compositions")

# ── TabPFN: bind R to the Conda Python and verify it ──────────────────────────
# Second TabPFN step, after the packages are attached. Nothing here touches the
# data: it checks that the Python side is the one we configured and stops with a
# readable message if not. TabPFN downloads its pretrained weights on first use:
# v2.x weights need a Hugging Face token (HF_TOKEN), 3.x weights need a
# one-time licence acceptance on a Prior Labs account (a non-interactive run
# confirms it with the account's API key in TABPFN_TOKEN).
if (needs_tabpfn) {
  # Hugging Face access token, required per TabPFN generation, not always:
  #   v2.x  – the weights come from Hugging Face with an access token
  #           (HF_TOKEN). Without one the notebook stops here with a readable
  #           message, before any data work.
  #   v3.x  – the repository is public. The download is gated instead on a
  #           one-time licence acceptance on a Prior Labs account (made in the
  #           browser; a non-interactive run confirms it with the account's
  #           API key in TABPFN_TOKEN). tabpfn checks this only when it must
  #           download, so a cached checkpoint needs neither. Demanding a HF
  #           token would block runs that can proceed.
  tabpfn_version_key <- tolower(TABPFN_MODEL_VERSION)
  hf_token_required <- !grepl("^v?3", tabpfn_version_key)
  token <- tabflux_resolve_hf_token(
    tabpfn_cfg = tabflux_config$runtime$tabpfn,
    project_dir = WORKDIR
  )
  if (hf_token_required && !nzchar(token)) {
    stop(
      paste(
        "HF_TOKEN missing.",
        paste0("TabPFN v2.x weights (model_version ", TABPFN_MODEL_VERSION, ") need a Hugging Face access token."),
        "Define the token in ~/.Renviron, the project .Renviron, the system environment,",
        "or runtime.tabpfn.hf_token in config.yaml before running TabPFN.",
        "TabPFN 3.x (model_version v3.5) needs no Hugging Face token."
      )
    )
  }
  if (!hf_token_required && !nzchar(token)) {
    message("TabPFN ", TABPFN_MODEL_VERSION,
            ": no Hugging Face token needed. The weights download after a one-time ",
            "licence acceptance on a Prior Labs account (a non-interactive run needs ",
            "the account's API key in TABPFN_TOKEN), or come from ",
            "the model cache if they are already there.")
  }
  
  # Configure Conda / reticulate environment: resolve paths and export to global vars
  # for easy inspection in later chunks.
  tabpfn_runtime <- resolve_tabpfn_runtime()
  TABPFN_ENV_NAME   <- tabpfn_runtime$env_name    # Conda env name (e.g. "tabflux-tabpfn35-gpu")
  TABPFN_CONDA_ROOT <- tabpfn_runtime$conda_root  # Conda installation root
  TABPFN_ENV_PREFIX <- tabpfn_runtime$env_prefix  # Full path to the env directory
  TABPFN_PYTHON     <- tabpfn_runtime$python       # Python binary path inside the env

  # Guard 1: The Python binary must physically exist before reticulate tries to load it.
  if (!file.exists(TABPFN_PYTHON)) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "TabPFN Python not found at '%s'. Set TABPFN_PYTHON or TABPFN_CONDA_ROOT/TABPFN_ENV_NAME correctly.",
      TABPFN_PYTHON
    ))
  }

  # Guard 2: If reticulate already loaded a different Python (e.g. from a previous
  # chunk or a stale session), any use_python() call below will be silently ignored
  # and we would end up with the wrong interpreter. Catch this before it causes
  # cryptic import errors later.
  if (reticulate::py_available(initialize = FALSE)) {
    current_cfg <- reticulate::py_config()
    current_python <- normalizePath(current_cfg$python, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
    requested_python <- normalizePath(TABPFN_PYTHON, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
    if (!identical(current_python, requested_python)) {
      stop(sprintf(
        paste(
          "reticulate is already initialized to '%s' instead of '%s'.",
          "Restart the R session and rerun the notebook from the first setup chunk."
        ),
        current_python,
        requested_python
      ))
    }
  }

  # Bind reticulate to the TabPFN Python and then verify the binding took effect.
  use_python(TABPFN_PYTHON, required = TRUE)
  py_cfg <- reticulate::py_config()
  bound_python    <- normalizePath(py_cfg$python,   winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  requested_python <- normalizePath(TABPFN_PYTHON, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  if (!identical(bound_python, requested_python)) {
    stop(sprintf(
      paste(
        "reticulate bound to '%s' instead of '%s'.",
        "Restart the R session and rerun the notebook from the first setup chunk."
      ),
      bound_python,
      requested_python
    ))
  }

  # Guard 3: Verify that the four Python packages mlr3's TabPFN learner depends on
  # can be imported. Fail here with a clear message rather than letting
  # the first predict() call crash inside the tuning loop.
  import_error <- tryCatch({
    reticulate::py_run_string("import ssl, tabpfn, torch, sklearn")
    NULL
  }, error = function(e) {
    e
  })
  if (inherits(import_error, "error")) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Python '%s' failed the TabPFN import check: %s",
      bound_python,
      conditionMessage(import_error)
    ))
  }

  # Record the Python side in the report: which interpreter and numpy
  # reticulate bound to (py_cfg, read above), then the TabPFN package version
  # and the model version it will load. print() is needed because inside an
  # if-block R shows nothing it is not told to print.
  print(py_cfg)
  reticulate::py_run_string("
import tabpfn
from tabpfn.settings import settings
print('tabpfn package:', tabpfn.__version__)
print('model version:', settings.tabpfn.model_version)
")
}

# Load the project's own helper functions (plain R files under R/).
# tabflux_training_helpers.R: build_classification_learners(), train_methods(), ...
#                            → used by the "Train models" and "Benchmark" chunks
# tabflux_scoring_helpers.R:  collect_benchmark_scores(), score_prediction_metrics()
#                            → used from "Benchmark" through "External Test Set"
# tabflux_data_helpers.R:     taxon_assignments_at_rank(), aggregate_counts_by_taxon(),
#                            sequence_based_feature_ids(), normalize_abundance(),
#                            align_features_to_reference() → used by the import,
#                            normalize, and external-test chunks.
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_training_helpers.R"))
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_scoring_helpers.R"))
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_data_helpers.R"))
# tabflux_selection_helpers.R:  select_features() — wrapper feature selection,
#                              run for the final model and inside outer folds
# tabflux_evaluation_helpers.R: build_outer_resampling(), run_outer_evaluation()
#                              — the outer evaluation loop (nested resampling)
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_selection_helpers.R"))
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_evaluation_helpers.R"))
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_prediction_helpers.R"))   # prediction-set summaries, bootstrap intervals, dumbbells
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_cfmd_helpers.R"))
# tabflux_figure_helpers.R: show_and_save_figure() (PNG + SVG copies of the
#                           report figures), and shap_class_summary() +
#                           plot_shap_by_class() for the per-class SHAP figure
#                           in the Feature Importance chunk.
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_figure_helpers.R"))
source(file.path(WORKDIR, "R", "tabflux_summary_helpers.R"))    # lodo_chance_level(), shorten_heldout_label() — the per-group figure below draws chance and its axis labels exactly as the multi-level wrapper does
```

#### Set Parameters

Turns every config value into a validated R variable. Validation happens here on purpose: a typo should stop the run now, not after hours of tuning. This chunk also builds the run-folder name (date, id, version, target, taxonomic level) and the report title, so runs never overwrite each other and an interrupted one can be resumed.

```{r settings, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ── Execution settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Verbosity of mlr3 and bbotk (optimizer) loggers: "warn", "info", "debug", etc.
log_threshold <- as.character(tabflux_config$execution$log_threshold[[1]])
lgr::get_logger("mlr3")$set_threshold(log_threshold)
lgr::get_logger("bbotk")$set_threshold(log_threshold)

seed <- as.integer(tabflux_config$execution$seed[[1]])   # global RNG seed for reproducibility
set.seed(seed)

# num_threads: cores used *inside* a single learner (e.g. ranger/xgboost internal parallelism).
# Set to "auto" to use all detected cores, or an integer to cap usage.
num_threads_cfg <- tabflux_config$execution$num_threads[[1]]
if (is.character(num_threads_cfg) && identical(num_threads_cfg, "auto")) {
  num_threads <- parallel::detectCores()
} else {
  num_threads <- as.integer(num_threads_cfg)
}

# num_jobs: parallel R worker processes inside one tuning, i.e. how many inner
# folds / model fits run at the same time. The methods themselves are not
# parallel: train_methods() (R/tabflux_training_helpers.R) tunes them in a loop.
# "auto" = one worker per inner fold, capped by num_threads, resolved in the
# Define Task chunk once the fold count is known; an integer pins it. With
# TabPFN in the run the notebook stays single-process (see the training chunk),
# but train_methods() still tunes the R learners with this many workers.
num_jobs_cfg <- tabflux_config$execution$num_jobs[[1]]
num_jobs <- if (is.character(num_jobs_cfg) && tolower(num_jobs_cfg) %in% c("auto", "kfold")) {
  "auto"
} else {
  as.integer(num_jobs_cfg)
}

# Cap the size of objects that future is allowed to copy to worker processes.
# Increase this if large data objects cause "globals too large" errors.
future_globals_max_gb <- as.numeric(tabflux_config$execution$future_globals_max_gb[[1]])
options(future.globals.maxSize = future_globals_max_gb * 1024^3)

# Register progressr progress bars so long loops print updates to the console.
# Falls back to a plain text bar if the global handler is unavailable
# (e.g. when rendering non-interactively via Quarto CLI).
enable_progress_handlers <- function() {
  tryCatch({
    progressr::handlers(global = TRUE)
    invisible(TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(
      "Skipping global progressr handlers in this render context: ",
      conditionMessage(e)
    )
    tryCatch({
      progressr::handlers("txtprogressbar")
    }, error = function(e2) {
      message("Could not register local progressr handlers either: ", conditionMessage(e2))
    })
    invisible(FALSE)
  })
}

enable_progress_handlers()

# Turn the dataset.tax_level config value into a plain character vector.
# config.yaml may give one string ("genus") or a list of levels (the batch
# script renders one notebook per level; here more than one is an error).
# Same helper as in scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R — keep the two in sync.
normalize_tax_levels_input <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) {
    return("")
  }

  if (is.list(x)) {
    x <- unlist(x, recursive = TRUE, use.names = FALSE)
  }

  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) {
    return("")
  }

  x
}

# Validate a taxonomy-level string and return it lowercased. Empty or missing
# gives "" (nothing configured); "ASV" gives "asv" — different strings, hence
# the nzchar(tax_level_key) && !(tax_level_key %in% c("asv", "sgb")) test in the
# import chunk and the external-test guard before aggregating to a rank.
#
# "sgb" names the same thing again: the finest level the input provides, no
# aggregation. A shotgun profile's finest unit is a species-level genome bin,
# not an amplicon variant, so "ASV" in a report title would be wrong. Code that
# decides whether to aggregate treats "asv" and "sgb" alike; the list below is
# the only place that knows about both.
canonical_tax_level_value <- function(x = "") {
  valid_tax_levels <- c("", "asv", "sgb", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")

  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) {
    return("")
  }

  tax_level_value <- trimws(as.character(x[[1]]))
  if (is.na(tax_level_value) || !nzchar(tax_level_value)) {
    return("")
  }

  tax_level_key <- tolower(tax_level_value)
  if (!(tax_level_key %in% valid_tax_levels)) {
    stop(
      "Parameter 'tax_level' must be one of: \"\", \"ASV\", \"SGB\", \"phylum\", ",
      "\"class\", \"order\", \"family\", \"genus\", or \"species\"."
    )
  }

  tax_level_key
}

# Return a display label for the taxonomy level ("ASV", "genus", etc.) for use in plot titles.
format_tax_level_label <- function(x = "") {
  tax_level_key <- canonical_tax_level_value(x)
  if (identical(tax_level_key, "sgb")) {
    return("SGB")
  }
  if (!nzchar(tax_level_key) || identical(tax_level_key, "asv")) {
    return("ASV")
  }

  tax_level_key
}

# Lowercase version of the tax level label used in directory and file names
# (a "slug" = a short form of a name that is safe in file and folder names:
# letters, digits and dashes only). Must match the copy in
# scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R, which recomputes the folder names.
make_tax_level_slug <- function(x = "") {
  tolower(format_tax_level_label(x))
}

# Turn the outcome column name into a file-name-safe version (letters, digits
# and dashes only, lowercase) so it can be used in output folder names.
make_target_slug <- function(x = "") {
  value <- trimws(as.character(x[[1]] %||% ""))
  if (!nzchar(value)) {
    value <- "unspecified"
  }
  value <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", value)
  value <- gsub("^-+|-+$", "", value)
  tolower(value)
}

# `x %||% y` reads "x, or y if x is NULL/empty". make_target_slug() above uses
# it; R only looks the operator up when that function is called, so
# defining it here, after the function, is fine.
`%||%` <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) y else x
}

# Assemble the output folder name for this run:
#   <run_date>_<dataset.id>_<dataset.version>_target_<target>_tax_<level>_saved_learners
# e.g. 2026-09-24_TabFlux_demo_target_category_tax_sgb_saved_learners for the
# cFMD demo. Date + dataset + version + target + rank make each run
# self-describing and stop runs from overwriting each other. Same helper as in
# the batch script.
build_tax_level_save_dir <- function(run_date, ds, ver, tax_level = "", target = "") {
  paste(
    run_date,
    ds,
    ver,
    paste0("target_", make_target_slug(target)),
    paste0("tax_", make_tax_level_slug(tax_level)),
    "saved_learners",
    sep = "_"
  )
}

# Rename taxa to names R accepts as column names, unquoted and unique. mlr3's
# feature selection uses column names as its own setting names, so a taxon like
# "Candidatus [Brocadia] sp. 1", or one starting with a digit, breaks it.
# Input: the columns of asv_df (import chunk, called once).
# Output: a tibble of original name → model name plus a 'renamed' flag. It stays
# in memory as feature_name_map, which the external-test chunk uses to translate
# back; the feature_name_map.csv copy is for use outside this notebook and
# nothing here reads it back.
sanitize_feature_names <- function(feature_names,
                                   tax_level = "feature",
                                   reserved_names = c(
                                     "Sample", "target", "group", "pta",
                                     ".row_id", ".class_count_tmp", "n"
                                   )) {
  original_feature_names <- as.character(feature_names)
  original_feature_names[is.na(original_feature_names)] <- ""

  # Build a prefix (e.g. "tax_genus_") put in front of names that would
  # otherwise clash with the notebook's own columns (reserved_names above).
  tax_slug <- make_tax_level_slug(tax_level)
  tax_prefix <- paste0("tax_", tax_slug, "_")

  # Step 1 – replace accented or non-Latin letters (é, µ, Greek symbols) with
  # the nearest plain letter, so later R tools don't choke on them.
  transliterated_names <- suppressWarnings(iconv(
    original_feature_names,
    from = "",
    to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT",
    sub = ""
  ))
  # iconv returns NA when transliteration fails completely; keep the original in that case.
  transliterated_names[is.na(transliterated_names)] <- original_feature_names[is.na(transliterated_names)]

  # Step 2 – strip surrounding whitespace and quotes, collapse runs of
  # punctuation/whitespace into a single dot, and remove leading/trailing dots.
  cleaned_names <- trimws(transliterated_names)
  cleaned_names <- gsub("^['\"`]+|['\"`]+$", "", cleaned_names)
  cleaned_names <- gsub("[[:space:][:punct:]]+", ".", cleaned_names)
  cleaned_names <- gsub("\\.+", ".", cleaned_names)
  cleaned_names <- gsub("^\\.+|\\.+$", "", cleaned_names)

  # Step 3 – replace empty strings or uninformative placeholders (NA, unknown…)
  # with a generic prefixed name so nothing is truly anonymous.
  placeholder_idx <- !nzchar(cleaned_names) |
    tolower(cleaned_names) %in% c("na", "nan", "null", "none", "unknown")
  cleaned_names[placeholder_idx] <- paste0(tax_prefix, "feature")

  # Step 4 – apply make.names() to guarantee syntactic validity (no leading digits, etc.)
  model_feature_names <- make.names(cleaned_names, unique = FALSE)

  # Step 5 – prefix any name that collides with internal modeling columns
  # (Sample, target, group_col, pta, …) to prevent accidental overwriting.
  reserved_idx <- tolower(model_feature_names) %in% tolower(reserved_names)
  model_feature_names[reserved_idx] <- paste0(tax_prefix, model_feature_names[reserved_idx])

  empty_idx <- !nzchar(model_feature_names)
  model_feature_names[empty_idx] <- paste0(tax_prefix, "feature")

  # Step 6 – enforce global uniqueness so every feature has a distinct column name.
  model_feature_names <- make.names(model_feature_names, unique = TRUE)

  tibble(
    feature_original = original_feature_names,
    feature_model = model_feature_names,
    renamed = feature_original != model_feature_names  # TRUE = name was changed
  )
}

# Wall-clock tuning cap in minutes (config execution.term_min, 20 min).
# get_terminator_for_method() applies it to the SVM only, whose training time
# grows steeply with sample size; the search stops when the time is gone and
# keeps the best setting found by then. The random searches (xgboost, mlp) stop
# after a fixed number of settings (40 with fast_tuning, 80 without); the other
# learners stop when their own grid or Hyperband schedule is exhausted.
term_min <- as.integer(tabflux_config$execution$term_min[[1]])  # wall-clock tuning cap in minutes, SVM only

# How the final hyperparameter setting is picked from the tuning results.
# Tuning scores every setting on two measures (balanced accuracy, logloss),
# which yields a set of equally "best" trade-offs; this rule chooses one:
#   "one_se"   – lowest logloss among the settings within one standard error
#                of the best balanced accuracy (default; see train_methods())
#   "max_bacc" – highest balanced accuracy, logloss breaks ties
tuning_selection <- as.character(tabflux_config$execution$tuning_selection[[1]])
if (!tuning_selection %in% c("one_se", "max_bacc")) {
  stop("execution.tuning_selection must be 'one_se' or 'max_bacc' (got '", tuning_selection, "').")
}

# ── Preprocessing settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The first three act in the "Preprocess Data" chunk; smote, filtering and
# selecting are consumed in "Prepare Modeling Inputs" / "Feature Selection";
# fast_tuning and learner_fallback in "Train models".
min_samples_per_class <- as.integer(tabflux_config$preprocessing$min_samples_per_class[[1]])  # drop classes with fewer samples than this
samples_to_keep  <- as.numeric(tabflux_config$preprocessing$samples_to_keep[[1]])   # random subsample fraction per class (1.0 = keep all)
feat_to_keep     <- as.numeric(tabflux_config$preprocessing$feat_to_keep[[1]])      # top-abundance feature fraction to retain (1.0 = keep all)
# smote: "" is not off, it means "decide later" — "Prepare Modeling Inputs"
# switches SMOTE on only when the majority/minority ratio exceeds
# smote_imbalance_threshold (below) and every class is big enough. The variants
# differ in where the synthetic minority samples go: "smote" anywhere in the
# minority class, "blsmote" only near the border with the majority class,
# "adasyn" mostly where the minority is hardest to tell apart. "none" = never.
smote            <- as.character(tabflux_config$preprocessing$smote[[1]])            # "smote" | "blsmote" | "adasyn" | "balance" | "none" | "" (auto-decide)
# Checked here because an unrecognised value is not an error later: "Prepare
# Modeling Inputs" builds no balancing step for it, so a typo (smote: true, say)
# silently trains on the imbalanced data while the report claims balancing ran.
if (!smote %in% c("", "none", "smote", "blsmote", "adasyn", "balance")) {
  stop("preprocessing.smote must be one of: '' (auto), none, smote, blsmote, adasyn, balance (got '", smote, "').")
}
# filtering: how hard the unsupervised feature filter is. TRUE behaves exactly
# like "minimal", FALSE = no filter at all. Careful: whatever is set here is
# overridden to "minimal" in "Prepare Modeling Inputs" when selecting = TRUE, so
# that the model-based selection gets to see every candidate feature.
filtering        <- tabflux_config$preprocessing$filtering[[1]]                      # "varcor" | "infogain" | "minimal" | TRUE | FALSE
# Same reason: an unrecognised value leaves preprocessing_pipe NULL and drops
# the whole robustify stage (constant-column removal, type harmonisation)
# without saying so.
if (!(isTRUE(filtering) || isFALSE(filtering) ||
      (is.character(filtering) && filtering %in% c("minimal", "varcor", "infogain")))) {
  stop("preprocessing.filtering must be TRUE, FALSE, or one of: minimal, varcor, infogain (got '", filtering, "').")
}
# selecting: run model-based ("wrapper") feature selection in the "Feature
# Selection" chunk — refit the model on ever smaller feature sets and keep what
# still works (RFE), and/or combine several such runs into one ranking
# (ensemble) — instead of trusting the plain filter above.
selecting        <- isTRUE(tabflux_config$preprocessing$selecting[[1]])              # run wrapper feature selection (RFE / ensemble FS)?
# fast_tuning: cheaper tuners (get_tuner_for_method) — successive halving on
# row subsamples instead of the full grid for glmnet/kknn/svm, 1 Hyperband
# repetition instead of 3 for ranger, and 40 random-search settings instead of
# 80 for xgboost/mlp. The Define Task chunk switches it OFF whenever there are
# < 500 samples or < 25 features, so on a few hundred samples the flag has no
# effect.
fast_tuning      <- isTRUE(tabflux_config$preprocessing$fast_tuning[[1]])           # cheaper tuners (see above); auto-off on small data
# learner_fallback: run each fit in a separate R process. If a fit errors, a
# majority-class stand-in answers in its place and a warning counts the failed
# tuning evaluations (TabPFN stops instead), so one bad setting does not cost
# hours of tuning. If every evaluation of a learner fails, the run stops.
learner_fallback <- isTRUE(tabflux_config$preprocessing$learner_fallback[[1]])      # encapsulate each learner so one failure doesn't abort the whole run

# Per-sample depth normalization ("none" | "tss" | "tss_log" | "tss_clr"; TSS
# = total-sum scaling, each sample's counts divided by that sample's total,
# i.e. relative abundance) and the fixed pseudocount used before log
# transforms. Validated here so a typo in the config stops the run
# immediately instead of silently changing behaviour.
normalization <- as.character(tabflux_config$preprocessing$normalization[[1]])
if (!normalization %in% c("none", "tss", "tss_log", "tss_clr")) {
  stop("preprocessing.normalization must be one of: none, tss, tss_log, tss_clr (got '",
       normalization, "').")
}
pseudocount <- as.numeric(tabflux_config$preprocessing$pseudocount[[1]])
if (!is.finite(pseudocount) || pseudocount <= 0) {
  stop("preprocessing.pseudocount must be a positive number (got '", pseudocount, "').")
}

# Probability calibration ("platt" | "none"): fitted on out-of-fold benchmark
# probabilities in the Benchmark chunk, applied to the external test set.
calibration <- as.character(tabflux_config$preprocessing$calibration[[1]])
if (!calibration %in% c("platt", "none")) {
  stop("preprocessing.calibration must be 'platt' or 'none' (got '", calibration, "').")
}

# ── Importance settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# "shap" | "perm" | "none". "none" skips the whole feature-importance chunk —
# validated here because an unrecognized value would skip the plots silently
# while still paying for the explainer setup and a model retrain.
importance_method <- as.character(tabflux_config$importance$method[[1]])
if (!importance_method %in% c("shap", "perm", "none")) {
  stop("importance.method must be one of: shap, perm, none (got '",
       importance_method, "').")
}

# ── Dataset settings ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ds     <- as.character(tabflux_config$dataset$id[[1]])       # dataset identifier used in output folder names
ver    <- as.character(tabflux_config$dataset$version[[1]])  # dataset version tag (e.g. "v1")
target <- as.character(tabflux_config$dataset$target[[1]])   # metadata column name used as the outcome variable
# The grouping column (site, study, batch, ...): every sample of one group stays
# on the same side of every split. Under leave-one-dataset-out (LODO) each group
# is held out in turn, so the metrics measure transfer to an unseen group rather
# than fit within one.
# group_col and pta must not name the same column (checked below): a group held out
# of training has no samples in that fold to compute fairness gaps from.
group_col <- as.character(tabflux_config$dataset$group[[1]])  # grouping column: site / study / batch (empty = no grouping)
pta    <- as.character(tabflux_config$dataset$pta[[1]])      # protected attribute column for fairness metrics (empty = disabled)
if (nzchar(trimws(group_col)) && identical(trimws(group_col), trimws(pta))) {
  stop("dataset.group and dataset.pta both name '", trimws(group_col), "'. They cannot be the same column: ",
       "a group held out of training has no samples left in that fold to compute fairness gaps from. ",
       "Use a different protected attribute, or leave dataset.pta empty.")
}

# Taxonomic resolution: "asv" (default) or a rank name ("genus", "species", etc.).
# Only one level per notebook run; use run_multi_tax_levels.R for batch runs.
tax_levels <- normalize_tax_levels_input(tabflux_config$dataset$tax_level)
if (length(tax_levels) > 1) {
  stop(
    "Multiple taxonomic levels detected in 'dataset.tax_level'. ",
    "Run 'Rscript scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R' instead of rendering this notebook directly."
  )
}
# Three spellings of the same setting. The display label ("ASV", "SGB" or the
# rank name) is built in the import chunk as feature_level.
tax_level       <- tax_levels[[1]]                        # raw value from config (e.g. "genus")
tax_level_key   <- canonical_tax_level_value(tax_level)  # lowercase validated key  (e.g. "genus")
tax_level_slug  <- make_tax_level_slug(tax_level)        # file-name-safe form      (e.g. "genus")

positive_class <- as.character(tabflux_config$dataset$positive_class[[1]])  # class treated as positive in binary tasks (empty = auto-select minority)

# ── Input paths ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two input layouts are supported (see the import chunk for the details):
#   Three-file (recommended): counts_path + taxa_path + meta_path
#   Legacy single-file:       asv_path + meta_path
counts_path <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$counts_path[[1]])  # feature_id + raw counts per sample
taxa_path   <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$taxa_path[[1]])    # feature_id + sequence/ranks/taxonomy
asv_path    <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$asv_path[[1]])     # legacy combined feature table
meta_path   <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$meta_path[[1]])    # sample metadata CSV

# Optional external test set (three-file layout). Predictions and per-group
# metrics are produced after the internal evaluation when these are set.
test_counts_path <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$test_counts_path[[1]])
test_taxa_path   <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$test_taxa_path[[1]])
test_meta_path   <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$test_meta_path[[1]])
test_group       <- as.character(tabflux_config$input$test_group[[1]])  # metadata column for per-group test metrics ("" = overall only)

# Resolve relative input paths against the project root so knitr's working-directory
# restoration between chunks does not cause file-not-found errors.
resolve_input_path <- function(path) {
  if (nzchar(path) && !is_absolute_path(path)) file.path(WORKDIR, path) else path
}

# ── Input source: your own files, or a public cFMD release ────────────────────
# input.source = "cfmd" replaces the three training paths with files built from
# a release of the curated Food Metagenomic Data (SegataLab/cFMD): profiles are
# downloaded, cached by content hash and rewritten in the same counts / taxa /
# metadata layout, so everything below runs unchanged. Settings under
# input.cfmd, details in R/tabflux_cfmd_helpers.R. input.test_* is untouched.
input_source <- tolower(as.character(tabflux_config$input$source[[1]]))
if (!input_source %in% c("files", "cfmd")) {
  stop("input.source must be 'files' or 'cfmd' (got '", input_source, "').")
}
if (input_source == "cfmd") {
  cfmd_cfg <- tabflux_config$input$cfmd
  cfmd_datasets <- unlist(cfmd_cfg$datasets, use.names = FALSE)
  cfmd_files <- cfmd_prepare_inputs(
    repo = as.character(cfmd_cfg$repo[[1]]),
    ref = as.character(cfmd_cfg$ref[[1]]),
    data_path = as.character(cfmd_cfg$data_path[[1]]),
    datasets = if (length(cfmd_datasets)) as.character(cfmd_datasets) else NULL,
    completeness_threshold = as.numeric(cfmd_cfg$completeness_threshold[[1]]),
    min_samples_per_dataset = as.integer(cfmd_cfg$min_samples_per_dataset[[1]]),
    cache_dir = resolve_input_path(as.character(cfmd_cfg$cache_dir[[1]]))
  )
  counts_path <- cfmd_files$counts_path
  taxa_path   <- cfmd_files$taxa_path
  meta_path   <- cfmd_files$meta_path
  asv_path    <- ""
  cat(sprintf("Input source: cFMD %s, %d samples x %d taxa from %d datasets\n",
              as.character(cfmd_cfg$ref[[1]]), cfmd_files$n_samples, cfmd_files$n_features, cfmd_files$n_datasets))
}
counts_path      <- resolve_input_path(counts_path)
taxa_path        <- resolve_input_path(taxa_path)
asv_path         <- resolve_input_path(asv_path)
meta_path        <- resolve_input_path(meta_path)
test_counts_path <- resolve_input_path(test_counts_path)
test_taxa_path   <- resolve_input_path(test_taxa_path)
test_meta_path   <- resolve_input_path(test_meta_path)

# Exactly one training input layout must be configured.
three_file_input <- nzchar(counts_path) && nzchar(taxa_path)
if (!three_file_input && !nzchar(asv_path)) {
  stop("No training input configured: set input.counts_path + input.taxa_path ",
       "(recommended) or the legacy input.asv_path.")
}
if (three_file_input && nzchar(asv_path)) {
  stop("Both input layouts are configured. Set either counts_path + taxa_path ",
       "or asv_path, not both.")
}

# The external test set is optional, but half-configured is an error — caught
# here, at the start, not hours later when the external chunk finally runs.
external_test_configured <- nzchar(test_counts_path)
if (external_test_configured && !nzchar(test_meta_path)) {
  stop("input.test_counts_path is set but input.test_meta_path is not. ",
       "The external test set needs both.")
}
if (external_test_configured && !nzchar(test_taxa_path) &&
    nzchar(tax_level_key) && !(tax_level_key %in% c("asv", "sgb"))) {
  stop("The external test set must be aggregated to the '", tax_level_key,
       "' level, which needs its taxonomy: set input.test_taxa_path.")
}

# ── Output / run settings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
run_date <- as.character(tabflux_config$output$run_date[[1]])   # date prefix for the output folder (empty = today)
# Where the run folder and the report are written. Empty means the project
# root, the usual case. A container mounts a volume and points this at it, so
# results survive the container; the code stays read-only in the image.
output_dir <- as.character(tabflux_config$output$dir[[1]] %||% "")
output_dir <- if (nzchar(output_dir)) resolve_input_path(output_dir) else WORKDIR
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Stop here if results cannot be written, rather than hours later. file.access()
# mode 2 tests write permission (0 = allowed). A common cause: a folder that
# Docker created as root for a bind mount, used by a container that runs as you.
if (file.access(output_dir, 2) != 0) {
  stop("Cannot write to the output folder '", output_dir, "' (output.dir). ",
       "Check that it exists and belongs to the user running TabFlux.")
}

# ── Evaluation design ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# How the reported performance is estimated (config `evaluation`; terms defined
# at the top of R/tabflux_evaluation_helpers.R). Two independent decisions:
# test_split reserves an internal test set before anything learns (0 = none);
# outer/nested/inner say how the training-data estimate is made. The outer folds
# are what gets reported; nested = TRUE repeats feature selection and tuning
# inside every fold. The reserved and external test sets are scored once by the
# final models, in Prediction and External Test.
eval_test_split    <- as.numeric(tabflux_config$evaluation$test_split[[1]])
eval_outer         <- tolower(as.character(tabflux_config$evaluation$outer[[1]]))
eval_outer_folds   <- as.integer(tabflux_config$evaluation$outer_folds[[1]])
eval_outer_repeats <- as.integer(tabflux_config$evaluation$outer_repeats[[1]])
eval_nested        <- isTRUE(tabflux_config$evaluation$nested[[1]])
# evaluation.prior_correction: every learner's predicted category is the largest
# probability divided by the class's training frequency (apply_prior_correction(),
# training helpers) - the decision rule balanced accuracy rewards. Default TRUE.
eval_prior_correction <- !isFALSE(tabflux_config$evaluation$prior_correction[[1]])
eval_inner         <- tolower(as.character(tabflux_config$evaluation$inner[[1]]))
eval_inner_folds   <- as.integer(tabflux_config$evaluation$inner_folds[[1]])
eval_inner_repeats <- as.integer(tabflux_config$evaluation$inner_repeats[[1]])
if (is.na(eval_test_split) || eval_test_split < 0 || eval_test_split >= 0.5) {
  stop("evaluation.test_split must be 0 (no internal test set) or a fraction below 0.5 (got ", eval_test_split, ").")
}
if (!eval_outer %in% c("subsampling", "cv", "repeated_cv", "loo", "lodo")) {
  stop("evaluation.outer must be one of: subsampling, cv, repeated_cv, loo, lodo (got '", eval_outer, "').")
}
if (!eval_inner %in% c("auto", "cv", "repeated_cv", "loo")) {
  stop("evaluation.inner must be one of: auto, cv, repeated_cv, loo (got '", eval_inner, "').")
}
if (eval_outer == "lodo" && !nzchar(trimws(group_col))) {
  stop("evaluation.outer = 'lodo' needs dataset.group set to the grouping column (study, site, ...).")
}

# ── Visualization settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
viz_downsample_threshold <- as.integer(tabflux_config$visualization$downsample_threshold[[1]])  # max samples before PCA/t-SNE downsampling kicks in
viz_downsample_size      <- as.integer(tabflux_config$visualization$downsample_size[[1]])       # number of samples to keep after downsampling
viz_prevalence_threshold <- as.numeric(tabflux_config$visualization$prevalence_threshold[[1]])  # min feature prevalence (fraction of samples > 0) for ordination plots

# ── SMOTE settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One class-size rule for everything: the same
# min_samples_per_class that drops tiny classes also guards SMOTE.
smote_min_samples_per_class <- min_samples_per_class                                                  # minimum class size required to apply SMOTE safely
smote_imbalance_threshold   <- as.numeric(tabflux_config$preprocessing$smote_imbalance_threshold[[1]])  # majority/minority ratio above which SMOTE is triggered

# ── SHAP settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SHAP splits one prediction into a contribution per feature, estimated by
# querying the model again and again with feature values swapped in from other
# samples. shap_sample_size = how many such draws per Shapley value; more =
# steadier numbers, proportionally slower. TabPFN re-runs the whole model for
# every draw, so it gets a smaller number (tabpfn_shap_sample_size) and SHAP is
# computed for at most tabpfn_shap_max_rows training samples.
shap_max_rows            <- as.integer(tabflux_config$importance$shap_max_rows[[1]])        # training rows explained, any learner
shap_sample_size_default <- as.integer(tabflux_config$importance$shap_sample_size[[1]])     # draws per Shapley value, see above (all models except TabPFN)
tabpfn_shap_sample_size  <- as.integer(tabflux_config$importance$tabpfn_shap_sample_size[[1]])  # reduced sample size for TabPFN (very slow per-query)
tabpfn_shap_max_rows     <- as.integer(tabflux_config$importance$tabpfn_shap_max_rows[[1]])     # max training rows to compute SHAP for in TabPFN mode

# ── Output folder for this run ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Everything a later reader or an external prediction needs lands here:
# <method>_tuned_learner.rds / _tuned_instance.rds (train models chunk),
# feature_name_map.csv (import), normalization.json + reference_features.csv
# (normalize), and metrics/ with every exported CSV. The batch script passes a
# fixed run_date so all taxonomic levels of one batch share the same date.
if (run_date == "" || is.na(run_date)) {
  run_date <- as.character(Sys.Date())
}
# Save each run in its own dated folder so old results are not overwritten and finished tuning can be picked up again
save_dir <- file.path(output_dir, build_tax_level_save_dir(
  run_date = run_date,
  ds = ds,
  ver = ver,
  tax_level = tax_level,
  target = target
))
metrics_dir <- file.path(save_dir, "metrics")

if (!dir.exists(save_dir)) {
  dir.create(save_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  if (!dir.exists(save_dir)) stop("Could not create the run folder '", save_dir, "'.")
  message("Created new directory: ", save_dir)
} else {
  message("Using existing directory: ", save_dir)
}
# Create the metrics folder up front: several chunks before "Save Metrics"
# already export CSVs into it (selected features, predictions, LODO metrics),
# and on a fresh run the folder would otherwise not exist yet.
dir.create(metrics_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r report title, echo=FALSE}
#| output: asis
# Name the HTML report after the run. Quarto merges the YAML block printed here
# with the header at the top of the file, so title/subtitle/author come from
# config.yaml rather than being typed into the notebook:
#   output.report_title   "" = "Predicting <target> from <tax_level>-level profiles"
#   output.report_author  "" = no author line
# The default title says what the run does. The subtitle carries the run label
# (id, version) and, when a custom title is set, the target and taxonomic level
# too, so two reports of the same batch can always be told apart.
yaml_quote <- function(x) paste0('"', gsub('"', '\\"', x, fixed = TRUE), '"')
report_title  <- as.character(tabflux_config$output$report_title[[1]])
report_author <- as.character(tabflux_config$output$report_author[[1]])
default_title <- !nzchar(trimws(report_title))
if (default_title) {
  report_title <- sprintf("Predicting %s from %s-level profiles", target, tax_levels[[1]])
  report_subtitle <- sprintf("%s \u00b7 run %s", ds, ver)
} else {
  report_subtitle <- sprintf("Target: %s \u00b7 Taxonomic level: %s \u00b7 run %s", target, tax_levels[[1]], ver)
}
cat("---\n",
    "title: ", yaml_quote(report_title), "\n",
    "subtitle: ", yaml_quote(report_subtitle), "\n",
    if (nzchar(trimws(report_author))) paste0("author: ", yaml_quote(report_author), "\n") else "",
    "---\n", sep = "")
```

#### Import Data

Reads metadata, counts and taxonomy, and builds the samples × features matrix. A feature is either an ASV, named by a hash of its sequence so the same ASV keeps its name in any dataset, or a taxon at the rank in `tax_level`, summing the reads of every ASV assigned to it. Reads unassigned at that rank are dropped and the loss reported. `build_feature_matrix()`, defined here, is reused unchanged for the external test set.

```{r import, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Sample metadata (config input.meta_path). One row per sample; the first
# column holds the sample IDs, which must match the sample columns of the count
# table. Also carries the outcome column named in `target` (the class labels)
# and, if set, the grouping column named in `group_col` (site, study, ...).
# meta_df is keyed by sample ID so it can be lined up with the feature matrix.
meta_dt <- fread(meta_path, check.names = FALSE, showProgress = TRUE)
id_meta <- names(meta_dt)[1]
meta_df <- as.data.frame(meta_dt)
rownames(meta_df) <- make.unique(as.character(meta_df[[id_meta]]))
meta_df[[id_meta]] <- NULL

# Is aggregation to a rank requested? (tax_level empty, "asv" or "sgb" = stay
# at the finest level the input provides.)
# feature_level is the human label ("ASV", "SGB" or the rank name), used from
# here on in messages, the feature-name prefix (sanitize_feature_names) and the
# tax_level column of the exported metrics (Save Metrics chunk).
aggregate_requested <- nzchar(tax_level_key) && !(tax_level_key %in% c("asv", "sgb"))
feature_level <- format_tax_level_label(tax_level)

# Turns a features × samples count table plus its taxon table into the modeling
# matrix (rows = samples, cols = features), aggregated to the requested rank or
# kept at ASV level with stable feature names. Used by both input layouts below
# and, unchanged, for the external test set, so training and test data are
# prepared identically.
#
# Input:  feature_counts – data.frame, rows = features, cols = samples (raw counts)
#         feature_ids    – character, one ID per feature row
#         taxa_info      – data.frame with taxonomy for those features (rank
#                          columns and/or 'taxonomy' string; may have a
#                          'sequence' column), or NULL at ASV level without one
#         label          – "training" / "external test", for messages only
# Output: data.frame, rows = samples, cols = features:
#         aggregated: taxon names at tax_level_key (reads of unassigned
#                     features are dropped and reported)
#         ASV level:  sequence-derived hash IDs when sequences are available
#                     (comparable across datasets), else the input IDs
#                     (dataset-local — a warning says so).
# Helpers used (all from R/tabflux_data_helpers.R): taxon_assignments_at_rank(),
# aggregate_counts_by_taxon(), looks_like_sequences(), sequence_based_feature_ids().
# Consumers: asv_df here, ext_matrix in the "External Test Set" chunk.
build_feature_matrix <- function(feature_counts, feature_ids, taxa_info, label) {
  feature_counts <- as.data.frame(feature_counts)

  if (aggregate_requested) {
    if (is.null(taxa_info)) {
      stop(sprintf(
        "Taxonomic aggregation at '%s' requested for the %s data, but no taxonomy was provided.",
        tax_level_key, label
      ))
    }
    taxon <- taxon_assignments_at_rank(taxa_info, tax_level_key)

    # Report how many reads the rank filter costs: features not assigned at
    # this rank are dropped, and deep ranks can lose a lot (species keeps only
    # a few percent of reads with typical 16S assignments).
    reads_before <- sum(colSums(feature_counts, na.rm = TRUE))
    aggregated <- aggregate_counts_by_taxon(feature_counts, taxon)
    reads_after <- sum(colSums(aggregated$counts, na.rm = TRUE))
    message(sprintf(
      "%s data at '%s' level: %d of %d features assigned; %.1f%% of reads retained.",
      label, tax_level_key, aggregated$n_features_used,
      aggregated$n_features_used + aggregated$n_features_dropped,
      100 * reads_after / max(reads_before, 1)
    ))
    counts_out <- aggregated$counts
    feature_names <- rownames(aggregated$counts)
  } else {
    # ASV level. IDs like "ASV_12" are assigned per dataset in input order, so
    # the same ID means different organisms in different datasets. With
    # sequences we name the feature by an md5 hash of the sequence, identical
    # for the same ASV anywhere. Without them the input IDs are kept, and they
    # mean something only inside this dataset.
    sequences <- NULL
    if (!is.null(taxa_info)) {
      seq_col <- which(tolower(names(taxa_info)) == "sequence")
      if (length(seq_col)) sequences <- as.character(taxa_info[[seq_col[1]]])
    }
    if (is.null(sequences) && looks_like_sequences(feature_ids)) {
      # Canonical DADA2 output: the feature name IS the sequence.
      sequences <- feature_ids
    }

    if (!is.null(sequences)) {
      feature_names <- sequence_based_feature_ids(sequences)
      message(sprintf(
        "%s data at ASV level: feature IDs derived from sequences (stable across datasets).",
        label
      ))
    } else if (identical(input_source, "cfmd")) {
      # cFMD features are species-level genome bins (SGBs), MetaPhlAn 4's
      # finest unit. An SGB code is comparable across datasets, so nothing
      # needs warning about here: this is the native resolution of the
      # profiles, and aggregating to a rank would throw it away.
      feature_names <- make.unique(as.character(feature_ids))
      message(sprintf(
        "%s data at SGB level: %d species-level genome bins, stable identifiers from the MetaPhlAn database.",
        label, length(feature_names)
      ))
    } else {
      feature_names <- make.unique(as.character(feature_ids))
      warning(sprintf(
        paste0(
          "%s data at ASV level has no sequences: keeping the input feature IDs. ",
          "These are dataset-local — do NOT combine or compare with other ASV tables."
        ),
        label
      ))
    }
    counts_out <- feature_counts
  }

  # Transpose to the modeling layout: rows = samples, cols = features.
  out <- as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(counts_out)), check.names = FALSE)
  colnames(out) <- feature_names
  out
}

if (three_file_input) {
  # ── Three-file layout (recommended; mirrors MetaFlux output) ────────────────
  #   counts: feature_id + one raw-count column per sample
  #   taxa:   feature_id, optional sequence, rank columns and/or taxonomy string
  # fread() reads .csv and .csv.gz transparently. integer64 = "double" keeps
  # very large counts as ordinary numbers; the integer64 type would be
  # silently misread by rowsum()/as.matrix() downstream.
  counts_dt <- fread(counts_path, check.names = FALSE, showProgress = TRUE, integer64 = "double")
  taxa_dt   <- fread(taxa_path,   check.names = FALSE, showProgress = TRUE)

  counts_df <- as.data.frame(counts_dt)
  feature_ids <- make.unique(as.character(counts_df[[1]]))
  counts_df[[1]] <- NULL
  rownames(counts_df) <- feature_ids

  taxa_df <- as.data.frame(taxa_dt)
  taxa_id_col <- names(taxa_df)[1]

  # The taxon table must describe at LEAST every feature in the counts table.
  # match() puts its rows into counts order, so a shuffled taxon table is fine
  # and extra rows are dropped; a counts feature with no taxonomy row stops the
  # run instead of being silently discarded.
  taxa_match <- match(feature_ids, make.unique(as.character(taxa_df[[taxa_id_col]])))
  if (anyNA(taxa_match)) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "%d feature(s) in '%s' have no row in the taxon table '%s'. First missing: %s",
      sum(is.na(taxa_match)), basename(counts_path), basename(taxa_path),
      feature_ids[which(is.na(taxa_match))[1]]
    ))
  }
  taxa_df <- taxa_df[taxa_match, , drop = FALSE]

  asv_df <- build_feature_matrix(
    feature_counts = counts_df,
    feature_ids = feature_ids,
    taxa_info = taxa_df,
    label = "Training"
  )
} else {
  # ── Legacy single-file layouts ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  asv_dt <- fread(asv_path, check.names = FALSE, showProgress = TRUE, integer64 = "double")
  id_asv <- names(asv_dt)[1]

  # Detect the layout by checking whether a 'taxonomy' column is present:
  #   Format 1 – regular sample × ASV table (rows = samples, cols = ASVs)
  #   Format 2 – BIOM-style ASV × sample table with a trailing 'taxonomy'
  #              column; supports aggregation to a higher rank.
  taxonomy_col <- names(asv_dt)[tolower(names(asv_dt)) == "taxonomy"][1]
  has_taxonomy_col <- !is.na(taxonomy_col)

  if (has_taxonomy_col) {
    # --- Format 2: BIOM-style (ASV × sample + taxonomy column) ---
    asv_tbl <- as.data.frame(asv_dt)
    feature_ids <- make.unique(as.character(asv_tbl[[id_asv]]))
    taxonomy_strings <- as.character(asv_tbl[[taxonomy_col]])

    sample_cols <- setdiff(names(asv_tbl), c(id_asv, taxonomy_col))
    if (!length(sample_cols)) {
      stop("Taxonomy-formatted input does not contain any sample columns.")
    }
    counts_df <- asv_tbl[, sample_cols, drop = FALSE]
    counts_df[] <- lapply(counts_df, function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)))
    rownames(counts_df) <- feature_ids

    asv_df <- build_feature_matrix(
      feature_counts = counts_df,
      feature_ids = feature_ids,
      taxa_info = data.frame(taxonomy = taxonomy_strings, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
      label = "Training"
    )
  } else {
    # --- Format 1: regular sample × ASV table (no taxonomy column) ---
    if (aggregate_requested) {
      stop(sprintf(
        paste0(
          "Taxonomic aggregation requested at '%s', but no 'taxonomy' column was found in '%s'. ",
          "Use the three-file input layout (counts_path + taxa_path), point `asv_path` at a ",
          "taxonomy-bearing table, or set `tax_level` to 'ASV'."
        ),
        tax_level_key,
        asv_path
      ))
    }

    asv_df <- as.data.frame(asv_dt)
    rownames(asv_df) <- make.unique(as.character(asv_df[[id_asv]]))
    asv_df[[id_asv]] <- NULL
  }
}

# The outcome column (config dataset.target) must exist in the metadata.
# Checked now, before anything is built on it.
if (!exists("target") || length(target) != 1 || !is.character(target)) {
  stop("Parameter 'target' must be defined in 'Set Parameters' as a single character string.")
}
if (!(target %in% colnames(meta_df))) {
  stop(sprintf("Target '%s' not found in metadata. Available: %s",
               target, paste(colnames(meta_df), collapse = ", ")))
}

# Check the optional LODO and PTA columns before later code depends on them.
# PTA = protected attribute: a grouping column (site, country, soil type) across
# which the model's error rates are compared, to see whether it works equally
# well for every group. Nothing to do with `target`, which everywhere else means
# the outcome being predicted.
grouping_active <- is.character(group_col) && length(group_col) == 1 && nzchar(trimws(group_col))
if (grouping_active && !(group_col %in% colnames(meta_df))) {
  stop(sprintf("Grouping column (dataset.group) '%s' not found in metadata. Available: %s",
               group_col, paste(colnames(meta_df), collapse = ", ")))
}

pta_active <- is.character(pta) && length(pta) == 1 && nzchar(trimws(pta))
if (pta_active && !(pta %in% colnames(meta_df))) {
  stop(sprintf("PTA column '%s' not found in metadata. Available: %s",
               pta, paste(colnames(meta_df), collapse = ", ")))
}

# Keep only samples present in BOTH the feature matrix and the metadata, and
# put both tables in the same (sorted) sample order. Sorting makes the row
# order reproducible before the seeded shuffle in the pre-process chunk.
common_ids <- intersect(rownames(asv_df), rownames(meta_df))
if (!length(common_ids)) stop("No overlapping sample IDs between ASV and metadata.")
common_ids <- sort(common_ids)
asv_df  <- asv_df[common_ids, , drop = FALSE]
meta_df <- meta_df[common_ids, , drop = FALSE]

# Counts read from CSV can arrive as text (e.g. quoted numbers). Convert; a
# column that still is not numeric afterwards means a malformed input file.
non_num <- !vapply(asv_df, is.numeric, logical(1))
if (any(non_num)) {
  for (cn in names(asv_df)[non_num]) {
    suppressWarnings({ asv_df[[cn]] <- as.numeric(asv_df[[cn]]) })
  }
}
if (any(!vapply(asv_df, is.numeric, logical(1)))) {
  stop("Feature table contains non-numeric columns after coercion. Clean inputs.")
}

# Make the feature names safe R column names (see sanitize_feature_names above).
# feature_name_map stays in memory for the external-test chunk, which aligns a
# new dataset by its original taxon names; the CSV is a copy for outside use.
feature_name_map <- sanitize_feature_names(
  feature_names = colnames(asv_df),
  tax_level = feature_level
)
safe_feature_names <- feature_name_map$feature_model

if (any(feature_name_map$renamed)) {
  colnames(asv_df) <- safe_feature_names
  n_renamed_features <- sum(feature_name_map$renamed)
  message(
    "Renamed ",
    n_renamed_features,
    " feature columns to syntactically valid names for modeling and feature selection."
  )
} else {
  colnames(asv_df) <- safe_feature_names
}
readr::write_csv(feature_name_map, file.path(save_dir, "feature_name_map.csv"))

# Outcome vector y: the class label of every sample. Samples without a label
# cannot be used for supervised training, so they are dropped from both tables.
y <- meta_df[[target]]
y[y == ""] <- NA
keep <- !is.na(y)
if (sum(!keep)) {
  message(sprintf("Dropping %d samples with missing '%s'.", sum(!keep), target))
  asv_df  <- asv_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  meta_df <- meta_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  y <- y[keep]
}

# Make target factor by default
if (!is.numeric(y)) y <- as.factor(y)

# tab_raw is the output of this chunk: rows = samples, cols = features (raw
# counts) + the outcome column, plus group_col / pta below when configured.
# → consumed by the "Preprocess Data" chunk.
tab_raw <- cbind(asv_df, y)
colnames(tab_raw)[ncol(tab_raw)] <- target

# Add the optional grouping columns to the modeling table so they stay aligned with the same filtered samples
if (grouping_active) {
  group_values <- meta_df[[group_col]]
  group_values[group_values == ""] <- NA
  if (anyNA(group_values)) {
    stop(sprintf("Grouping column '%s' contains missing values after filtering. Fill them or leave 'dataset.group' empty.", group_col))
  }
  tab_raw$group <- as.factor(group_values)
}

if (pta_active) {
  pta_values <- meta_df[[pta]]
  pta_values[pta_values == ""] <- NA
  if (anyNA(pta_values)) {
    stop(sprintf("PTA column '%s' contains missing values after filtering. Fill them or leave 'pta' empty.", pta))
  }
  tab_raw$pta <- as.factor(pta_values)
}

# Quick report
message(sprintf("Samples: %d, features: %d, feature level: %s, target: %s",
                nrow(asv_df), ncol(asv_df), feature_level, target))
if (is.factor(y)) message(sprintf("Levels: %s", paste(levels(y), collapse = ", ")))
if (grouping_active) message(sprintf("LODO enabled with metadata column: %s", group_col))
if (pta_active) message(sprintf("PTA enabled with metadata column: %s", pta))
```

#### Preprocess Data

Builds the working table `tab`: drops samples with no reads at this rank and classes below `min_samples_per_class`, optionally keeps a fraction of samples and features for quick runs, and shuffles the sample order. Fixes, once, the metric set (binary or multi-class) and the positive class. The printed diagnostics say which steps changed anything.

```{r pre-process, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Input: tab_raw from the import chunk (raw counts + outcome [+ group_col, pta]).
# dplyr verbs below drop row names, so the sample IDs move into a "Sample"
# column. It stays a bookkeeping column (never a feature) all the way to the
# task chunk, where it becomes the row-id → sample-name lookup.
tab_raw$Sample <- rownames(tab_raw)
rownames(tab_raw) <- NULL

# From here on the outcome column is always called "target", so no later
# chunk needs to know the metadata column name.
names(tab_raw)[names(tab_raw) == target] <- "target"

# Drop samples with zero reads at the modelled rank before anything looks at the
# sample set. At deep ranks (species) a sample can lose every read to the
# "unassigned" filter, leaving no community information (0/0 relative
# abundance). Dropping here means the class-distribution decisions, the
# ordination plots and the normalization all see the same samples.
pre_feature_cols <- setdiff(names(tab_raw), c("Sample", "target",
                                              if (grouping_active) "group",
                                              if (pta_active) "pta"))
pre_sample_reads <- rowSums(tab_raw[, pre_feature_cols, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
if (any(pre_sample_reads == 0)) {
  message(sprintf(
    "Dropping %d sample(s) with zero reads at the '%s' level: %s",
    sum(pre_sample_reads == 0), feature_level,
    paste(head(tab_raw$Sample[pre_sample_reads == 0], 10), collapse = ", ")
  ))
  tab_raw <- tab_raw[pre_sample_reads > 0, , drop = FALSE]
}

# Drop classes with fewer than min_samples_per_class samples (config, 5): such a
# class cannot be spread over CV folds. Then keep a random fraction
# samples_to_keep of each remaining class (1 = keep all; < 1 for quick test
# runs). droplevels() forgets the removed classes so they do not linger as empty
# factor levels in the mlr3 task. With every class at or above the minimum and
# samples_to_keep = 1 both steps are pass-throughs.
class_count_col <- ".class_count_tmp"

tab <- tab_raw %>%
  group_by(target) %>%
  mutate(!!class_count_col := dplyr::n()) %>%
  filter(.data[[class_count_col]] >= min_samples_per_class) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = samples_to_keep) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-all_of(class_count_col)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  droplevels()

# Sanity check on the config value only: feat_to_keep must be a number greater
# than 0 and at most 1. The abundance filter itself runs about 20 lines further
# down, in the `if (feat_to_keep < 1)` block after the PTA check.
stopifnot(is.numeric(feat_to_keep), feat_to_keep > 0, feat_to_keep <= 1)

# Fairness metrics compare groups of the protected attribute; after the class
# filter at least two groups must remain, otherwise there is nothing to compare.
if ("pta" %in% names(tab)) {
  tab$pta <- droplevels(as.factor(tab$pta))
  if (nlevels(tab$pta) < 2) {
    stop(sprintf("PTA column '%s' has fewer than two groups after filtering.", pta))
  }
}

# Separate metadata columns from taxa columns before abundance-based filtering
non_feature_cols <- c("Sample", "target", if (grouping_active) "group", if (pta_active) "pta")
feat_cols <- setdiff(names(tab), non_feature_cols)
p0 <- length(feat_cols)

if (feat_to_keep< 1) {
  # Keep only the top-abundance fraction of features. This is a fast pre-filter
  # before any model-based feature selection later.
  for (cn in feat_cols) {
    if (!is.numeric(tab[[cn]])) {
      suppressWarnings(tab[[cn]] <- as.numeric(tab[[cn]]))
    }
  }
  # Rank features by summed RELATIVE abundance (each sample's counts divided by
  # its total) rather than raw counts. With raw counts a deeply sequenced
  # sample contributes more to every feature's total, so the ranking would
  # partly reflect sequencing depth instead of community composition.
  feat_mat <- as.matrix(tab[, feat_cols, drop = FALSE])
  sample_reads <- rowSums(feat_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
  feat_props <- sweep(feat_mat, 1, pmax(sample_reads, 1), "/")  # pmax guards empty samples
  totals <- colSums(feat_props, na.rm = TRUE)
  k <- max(1, floor(p0 * feat_to_keep))
  ord <- order(totals, decreasing = TRUE)
  sel <- feat_cols[ord][seq_len(k)]
} else {
  # feat_to_keep == 1: keep all features (no abundance pre-filter)
  sel <- feat_cols
  k <- p0
}

# `tab` now holds the working sample set and feature set; every later chunk
# (ordination, normalization, task) starts from it.
tab <- tab[, c(non_feature_cols, sel), drop = FALSE]

# Diagnostics
cat(sprintf("\nAfter feature cap: kept %d of %d features (%.1f%%) by total abundance.\n",
            k, p0, 100 * k / p0))


# Pick the metric set for the number of classes. Binary tasks get the full
# suite, including area under the ROC curve (AUC) and under the precision-recall
# curve (PR-AUC, more informative when one class is rare). Multi-class tasks get
# accuracy, balanced accuracy (mean of the per-class recalls, so guessing the
# big class does not flatter the score) and log-loss; most other measures are
# defined for two classes only.
# Fairness metrics are added only for a binary task with a protected-attribute
# column: how far false-positive rate, true-positive rate and balanced accuracy
# differ between that column's groups.
```
