```{r pre-process, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
fairness_active <- FALSE
fairness_metric_ids <- character()

# Decided once, so every later stage reports the same things ("bmr" = benchmark
# result):
#   bmr_measures   → benchmark, prediction and external-test scoring
#   train_measures → what the tuner optimises ("Train models"): balanced
#                    accuracy and log-loss at once, keeping every setting no
#                    other setting beats on both — the Pareto front.
#                    train_methods() (R/tabflux_training_helpers.R) then picks
#                    one row from it by execution.tuning_selection: by default
#                    "one_se", the lowest log-loss among the settings within one
#                    paired standard error of the best balanced accuracy
#                    (paired = compared with the best setting fold by fold);
#                    "max_bacc" takes the highest balanced accuracy instead.
#   positive_class → task$positive in the task chunk; orients AUC / PR-AUC and
#                    the "prob.<class>" column in the prediction exports
if (length(levels(as.factor(tab$target))) > 2) {
  dataset_attr <- "multi-class"
  bmr_measure_ids <- c("classif.acc", "classif.bacc", "classif.logloss")
  train_measures <- c("classif.bacc", "classif.logloss")
} else if (length(levels(as.factor(tab$target))) == 2) {
  dataset_attr <- "binary"
  bmr_measure_ids <- c("classif.acc", "classif.bacc", "classif.logloss",
                       "classif.precision", "classif.recall", "classif.specificity",
                       "classif.fbeta", "classif.auc", "classif.prauc")
  train_measures <- c("classif.bacc", "classif.logloss")

  # No positive class in the config: take the minority class. With perfectly
  # balanced classes which.min() picks the first name alphabetically, which is
  # why dataset.positive_class should be stated whenever the classes are even.
  if (positive_class == "") {
    counts <- table(tab$target)
    positive_class <- names(which.min(counts))
  }
} else {
  # One class left (or none). Almost always the class filter, not the data:
  # preprocessing.min_samples_per_class drops any class smaller than its value,
  # and on a subset that can remove everything but the largest class. The
  # message below names the survivors and the threshold.
  surviving <- table(tab$target)
  stop(
    "Only ", length(surviving), " class left in the target column '", target, "' — ",
    "a classifier needs at least two.\n",
    "  Surviving: ", paste(names(surviving), surviving, sep = " = ", collapse = ", "), "\n",
    "  preprocessing.min_samples_per_class is ", min_samples_per_class,
    "; lower it, or widen the data, if classes were dropped by that filter."
  )
}

if (dataset_attr == "binary" && pta_active) {
  fairness_active <- TRUE
  fairness_metric_ids <- c("fairness.fpr", "fairness.tpr", "fairness.bacc")
} else if (pta_active) {
  message("PTA is set, but fairness metrics are skipped because the target is not binary.")
}

# msr() turns each measure id into an mlr3 Measure object. bmr = benchmark
# result: this is the list of measures the "Benchmark" chunk, the prediction
# chunk and the external test set are all scored with.
bmr_measures <- lapply(bmr_measure_ids, msr) # Measure objects

cat("\nDataset type:", dataset_attr, "\n")
cat("Selected metrics:", paste(train_measures, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Positive class:", positive_class, "\n")
if (pta_active) cat("PTA source column:", pta, "\n")
if (fairness_active) {
  cat("Fairness metrics:",
      paste(fairness_metric_ids, collapse = ", "),
      "\n")
}

# Print how samples spread over the groups of one metadata column (LODO group or
# protected attribute), plus a group × class table. Called here on the full table
# and again in the task chunk on the train / test halves: a group contributing
# only one class makes a poor LODO fold, and that shows up here. Prints only.
print_group_diagnostics <- function(data, col_name, label, target_col = "target") {
  if (!(col_name %in% names(data)) || !(target_col %in% names(data))) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  group_vals <- as.character(data[[col_name]])
  target_vals <- as.character(data[[target_col]])
  keep <- !is.na(group_vals) & nzchar(group_vals)
  if (!any(keep)) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  group_vals <- group_vals[keep]
  target_vals <- target_vals[keep]
  
  cat("\n", label, " distribution:\n", sep = "")
  print(sort(table(group_vals), decreasing = TRUE))
  cat(label, " x target:\n", sep = "")
  print(table(group_vals, target_vals))
}

# Shuffle the rows. They are ordered by CLASS at this point: the
# group_by(target) + slice_sample() step above returns all samples of one class,
# then all of the other, so anything splitting by position would get
# single-class folds. (The import chunk sorted by accession ID, not by study.)
# Reproducible via set.seed(seed) in the settings chunk.
tab %<>% dplyr::sample_frac(size = 1)

# Final size of the working table, printed for the record. Later stages
# recompute their own sizes from the mlr3 task (the feature-selection chunk
# even reuses the name n_features for its minimum feature count).
n_samples  <- nrow(tab)
n_features <- length(sel)
cat("\nAfter filtering: ", n_samples, "samples and", n_features, "features.\n")
table_summary <- table(tab$target)
cat("Class distribution:\n")
print(table_summary)
if ("group" %in% names(tab)) print_group_diagnostics(tab, "group", "Groups")
if ("pta" %in% names(tab)) print_group_diagnostics(tab, "pta", "PTA groups")
```

#### Inspect Data

A look at the data before any model: do the classes separate at all, and in how many dimensions? Rare taxa dropped, zeros replaced, counts put on the centred log-ratio scale, then PCA and t-SNE coloured by class. Diagnostic only — the models get their own depth normalisation in the next section.

```{r inspecting data, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Ordination plots for a first look at the data.
# Input: `tab` (raw counts) from the pre-process chunk.
# Steps: drop rare and constant taxa, replace zeros, CLR-transform, then PCA
# and t-SNE coloured by class.
# Output: plots only. df, X, X_clr, pca and ts are used nowhere else; the
# feature-selection chunk repeats these plots on the training split after
# selection.
# `y` is reused here for the class labels and may be subsampled for the t-SNE,
# overwriting the import chunk's `y`. Harmless: those values already sit in
# tab_raw$target and nothing reads the import `y` again.
df <- as_tibble(tab)

# Split into the abundance matrix X (samples × taxa, numeric) and the class
# labels y for colouring. Factor columns go through character first so factor
# level codes are never mistaken for counts.
y  <- df$target
metadata_cols <- c("target", "Sample", "group", "pta")
X <- df[, !(names(df) %in% metadata_cols), drop = FALSE]
X[] <- lapply(X, function(col) {
  if (is.factor(col)) col <- as.character(col)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(col))
})

# Optional downsample for speed (t-SNE is slow on thousands of samples):
# above viz_downsample_threshold samples keep a random viz_downsample_size.
# Rows of X and entries of y are subset together so colours stay aligned.
if (nrow(X) > viz_downsample_threshold) {
  idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(X)), viz_downsample_size)
  X <- X[idx, , drop = FALSE]
  y <- y[idx]
}

# 1) Remove taxa that are almost always zero or have no variation.
# prev = fraction of samples in which a taxon is present. Taxa seen in fewer
# than viz_prevalence_threshold (5%) of samples add noise to the CLR and can
# dominate a PCA; zero-variance columns cannot be scaled by prcomp().
if (any(vapply(X, anyNA, logical(1)))) {
  stop("Feature matrix contains non-numeric or missing values after preprocessing; check taxa columns for invalid entries.")
}
prev <- colMeans(X > 0)
X <- X[, prev >= viz_prevalence_threshold, drop = FALSE]
if (ncol(X) == 0) stop("All features filtered out; lower the prevalence threshold.")
X <- X[, apply(X, 2, var) > 0, drop = FALSE]

# 2) Zero replacement. The CLR below takes logs and log(0) is undefined, so each
# zero is replaced by a small value that depends on how deeply that sample was
# sequenced — a zero in a shallow sample says much less than a zero in a deep
# one (the "count zero multiplicative" method, CZM). It needs raw COUNTS as
# input, which is why the ordination runs here, before the normalization chunk
# transforms `tab`.
X0 <- zCompositions::cmultRepl(as.matrix(X),
                               label = 0,
                               method = "CZM",
                               z.warning = 1, # silence high-zero warnings
                               z.delete  = FALSE) # do not drop rows/cols

# 3) CLR (centred log-ratio): log of each taxon divided by the sample's
# geometric mean. Sequencing gives relative amounts only, so one taxon can look
# higher just because another dropped. After the CLR, ordinary Euclidean
# distances — and therefore PCA — are meaningful.
X_clr <- compositions::clr(X0)

# PCA on the CLR values, each taxon scaled to unit variance so abundant taxa
# do not dominate the axes. Plots: scree, PC1 vs PC2 by class, top loadings.
pca <- prcomp(X_clr, scale. = TRUE)

# Scree plot of PCA variance
fviz_eig(pca, addlabels = TRUE)

# PCA plot  
scores <- data.frame(PC1 = pca$x[,1], PC2 = pca$x[,2], target = y)

ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, fill = target)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "target") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "PCA on CLR-transformed abundances",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(100*summary(pca)$importance[2,1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(100*summary(pca)$importance[2,2], 1), "%)"))

# Loadings contributions (top 10)
fviz_contrib(pca, choice = "var", axes = 1:2, top = 10)

# Elbow plot: how many principal components are needed to reach 90% of the
# variance, i.e. roughly how many independent directions carry the signal.
# Printed and drawn as a diagnostic only — num_components is not used by
# anything downstream.
cumulative_prop_var <- cumsum(pca$sdev ^ 2 / sum(pca$sdev ^ 2))

# Find number of components explaining 90% of variance
num_components <- which(cumulative_prop_var >= 0.9)[1]

# Print number of components
cat("Number of components explaining 90% of variance:",
    num_components,
    "\n")

# Create a data frame with the number of components and their cumulative proportion of variance explained
elbow_df <-
  data.frame(
    Num_Components = 1:length(cumulative_prop_var),
    Cumulative_Proportion_Var_Explained = cumulative_prop_var
  )

# Plot the elbow plot
ggplot(elbow_df,
       aes(x = Num_Components, y = Cumulative_Proportion_Var_Explained)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = num_components,
    color = "dodgerblue3",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, length(cumulative_prop_var), 1)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Elbow plot of PCA components",
    subtitle = "Reference line: components explaining up to 90% variance",
    x = "Number of components",
    y = "Cumulative proportion of variance explained"
  )

# Get the PCA loading matrix
loadings <- pca$rotation

# Find the variable with highest absolute loading for each principal component
variables <- rownames(loadings)  # Get the variable names
max_loadings <-
  apply(abs(loadings), 2, function(x)
    variables[which.max(x)])

# Output the results
for (i in 1:ncol(loadings)) {
  cat(paste0("Most important variable for PC", i, ": ", max_loadings[i]),
      "\n")
}

# t-SNE on the same CLR values: a non-linear map that keeps close neighbours
# close, useful when classes separate only locally. Perplexity ≈ how many
# neighbours each sample "considers"; Rtsne requires it below (n - 1) / 3, so
# it is capped for small sample sets.
perplexity <- pmin(30, floor((nrow(X_clr) - 1) / 3))  # safe, within 5–30 typical
ts <- Rtsne(X_clr,
            pca = FALSE,
            check_duplicates = FALSE,
            perplexity = perplexity,
            theta = 0.5)

ts_df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = ts$Y[,1], tSNE2 = ts$Y[,2], target = y)

ggplot(ts_df, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, fill = target)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "target") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "t-SNE on CLR-transformed abundances")
```

#### Normalize Abundances

Converts the counts in `tab` to depth-corrected values (default: log10 relative abundance with a fixed pseudocount). Last change to the table before the task is built. The raw counts are kept for the SHAP export; the settings and the full feature list are written next to the models, so new data can be prepared identically.

```{r normalize, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Correct for sequencing depth before the modeling task is built.
#
# Placed here because `tab` still holds the raw counts the ordination chunk
# above needs. From the task definition onward everything must see
# depth-corrected values: library size varies ~30x between samples and
# systematically between studies, so a model on raw counts can identify the
# study from its depth instead of learning biology.
#
# The transform (default tss_log = log10 relative abundance) is per-sample and
# estimates nothing from the data, so the same function is applied to the
# external test set. Options in normalize_abundance() (R/tabflux_data_helpers.R).

# Identify the feature columns; everything else is bookkeeping metadata.
norm_meta_cols <- c("Sample", "target", if (grouping_active) "group", if (pta_active) "pta")
norm_feat_cols <- setdiff(names(tab), norm_meta_cols)

# Zero-read samples were already dropped in the pre-process chunk, before the
# class-distribution decisions and the ordination plots. This guard only fires
# if the chunks were run out of order. Careful when reading the message: the
# pre-process chunk removed `tab`'s row names, so find_empty_samples() reports
# row POSITIONS ("1", "5", ...), not sample IDs — look them up in tab$Sample.
empty_samples <- find_empty_samples(tab[, norm_feat_cols, drop = FALSE])
if (length(empty_samples)) {
  stop("Sample(s) with zero reads reached the normalization step: ",
       paste(empty_samples, collapse = ", "),
       ". Rerun the notebook from the pre-process chunk onward.")
}

# Keep the raw counts: the importance chunk's SHAP export reports the raw
# count and proportion next to the value the model saw, and library size is a
# QC quantity worth showing per sample. tab_counts must stay row-aligned with
# tab, which nothing after this point reorders.
tab_counts <- tab

normalized <- normalize_abundance(
  tab[, norm_feat_cols, drop = FALSE],
  method = normalization,
  pseudocount = pseudocount
)
# From here on `tab` holds normalized values → "Define Task" builds the mlr3 task
# from it. library_sizes = total reads per sample, used by the SHAP export and
# the external-test QC flag below_training_min_depth. It is UNNAMED and in `tab`
# row order (the pre-process chunk dropped the row names), so map an entry back
# to a sample via tab$Sample at the same position, or via sample_lookup.
tab[, norm_feat_cols] <- normalized$data
library_sizes <- normalized$library_sizes

# Report the depth spread — the size of the problem the normalization removes.
cat(sprintf(
  "\nNormalization: %s (pseudocount %g)\nLibrary size: min %s | median %s | max %s reads (%.0fx spread)\n",
  normalization, pseudocount,
  format(min(library_sizes), big.mark = ","),
  format(round(stats::median(library_sizes)), big.mark = ","),
  format(max(library_sizes), big.mark = ","),
  max(library_sizes) / max(min(library_sizes), 1)
))
if (grouping_active) {
  # Median depth per study group: large differences here are exactly the batch
  # signal that would leak into a model trained on raw counts.
  depth_by_group <- tapply(library_sizes, tab$group, stats::median)
  cat("Median library size per LODO group:\n")
  print(round(sort(depth_by_group, decreasing = TRUE)))
}

# Record the settings and the full pre-selection feature space next to the saved
# learners. With feature_name_map.csv, that is everything needed to prepare a
# future dataset the same way. The "External Test Set" chunk uses the in-memory
# versions (norm_feat_cols, normalization, pseudocount); the files are for
# reusing the saved learners outside the notebook.
jsonlite::write_json(
  list(
    normalization = normalization,
    pseudocount = pseudocount,
    tax_level = tax_level_key,
    n_features = length(norm_feat_cols),
    n_samples = nrow(tab)
  ),
  file.path(save_dir, "normalization.json"),
  auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE
)
readr::write_csv(
  data.frame(feature_model = norm_feat_cols),
  file.path(save_dir, "reference_features.csv")
)
```

#### Define Task

Builds the mlr3 task, reserves the internal test set when `evaluation.test_split` asks for one (whole groups under a grouping column, class-stratified otherwise), and builds the outer folds from `evaluation.outer`: cross-validation, repeated random splits, or one fold per group. Nothing that learns sees the reserved samples. The fold table printed here is the design every later section reports against.

```{r task, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Turn the normalized abundance table into an mlr3 classification task and
# split it into training and test parts.
#
# Input: `tab` from the normalize chunk — one row per sample, columns Sample,
#        target (the class labels), optional group_col (study/group) and pta (protected
#        attribute), plus one depth-normalized column per taxon.
# Output, used by every later chunk:
#   task             – the full task (all samples)
#   task_train       – what feature selection, tuning and benchmarking see
#   task_test        – the internal test set scored in the Prediction chunk
#                      (NULL unless evaluation.test_split > 0)
#   task_*_base      – frozen copies the feature-selection chunk restarts from
#   sample_lookup, pta_lookup, group_lookup – row id -> sample / group tables
#                      used by the metric exports
#
# Sanity checks: the task needs a sample id and a class label per row.
stopifnot(all(c("Sample", "target") %in% names(tab)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(tab$Sample), !anyNA(tab$Sample))

# Ensure factor target
if (!is.factor(tab$target)) tab$target <- as.factor(tab$target)

# Identify task rows by a plain row number (1..n), not by sample name: SMOTE
# invents new rows later and gives them new numeric ids, which sample-name ids
# could not carry. sample_lookup keeps the row number -> sample name mapping,
# used by the Benchmark chunk to label predictions.csv.
row_ids <- seq_len(nrow(tab))
sample_lookup <- data.frame(
  row_id = row_ids,
  Sample = tab$Sample,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
# Row id -> protected attribute (PTA) group. The PTA column is a metadata
# variable such as country or crop on which the fairness gaps are computed
# (does the model do equally well in every group?). Used by the scoring
# helpers in the benchmark and prediction chunks; NULL when no PTA is set.
pta_lookup <- if ("pta" %in% names(tab)) {
  stats::setNames(as.character(tab$pta), as.character(row_ids))
} else {
  NULL
}

# Row-id → LODO group lookup. The benchmark shuffles fold order, so this is
# how each LODO fold is traced back to the study/group it held out when the
# per-group metrics are exported later.
group_lookup <- if ("group" %in% names(tab)) {
  stats::setNames(as.character(tab$group), as.character(row_ids))
} else {
  NULL
}

# Drop the two reporting-only columns before the table goes into the task.
# Sample is character data, which the learners and feature-selection pipeops
# cannot handle. pta would be accepted (it is a factor) but must never become a
# feature, and mlr3 only knows a "pta" column role while mlr3fairness is
# attached (see sanitize_task_col_roles below), so it stays out and pta_lookup
# does the job. group_col stays: it becomes the grouping variable for
# leave-one-dataset-out resampling.
backend_tab <- tab[, setdiff(names(tab), c("Sample", "pta")), drop = FALSE]

# The backend is the data store behind an mlr3 task. Rows are addressed by
# the integer row ids created above, not by a column of the table.
backend <- mlr3::as_data_backend(backend_tab, primary_key = row_ids)

# mlr3 tags every task column with a "role": feature, target, group, stratum,
# weight... Extension packages can add roles (mlr3fairness adds "pta"). This
# helper drops any role the currently loaded mlr3 does not recognise — e.g. a
# leftover "pta" role on a task built while mlr3fairness was attached, which
# would make every pipeop fail its role check. The allowed set is read from mlr3
# itself, so it matches this session's extensions.
# Applied to `task` at creation and to every clone/filter building task_train /
# task_test below; no later chunk calls it.
# local({...}) gives the function a private cache (allowed_roles), so the probe
# task is built only once.
sanitize_task_col_roles <- local({
  allowed_roles <- NULL
  function(task) {
    if (is.null(allowed_roles)) {
      # Ask mlr3 itself which roles exist right now: build a minimal throwaway
      # task and read its role slots. Computed once, then reused.
      probe <- mlr3::as_task_classif(
        data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3, 4), y = factor(c("a", "b", "a", "b"))),
        target = "y"
      )
      allowed_roles <<- names(probe$col_roles)
    }
    keep_roles <- intersect(names(task[["col_roles"]]), allowed_roles)
    task$.__enclos_env__$private$.col_roles <- task[["col_roles"]][keep_roles]
    task
  }
})

# Create the classification task: target = the class labels, every other
# backend column is a feature for now.
task <- mlr3::as_task_classif(backend, target = "target")
task <- sanitize_task_col_roles(task)

# Assign the non-feature roles.
#   group_col -> "group": resampling keeps all samples of a study together, so a
#           study is either entirely in a fold's training part or entirely
#           in its test part. This is what turns rsmp("loo") into
#           leave-one-group-out: the outer "lodo" folds, and the inner tuning
#           folds when there are few groups.
#   target -> "stratum" (only without a grouping column): folds keep the
#           class ratio of the whole data. mlr3 cannot combine grouping and
#           stratification.
# set_col_roles() already moved group_col out of the feature role; the direct write
# into the private role slot below is a guard against an extension package
# re-registering roles. In a normal session it changes nothing.
if ("group" %in% names(tab)) task$set_col_roles("group", "group")
if ("group" %in% names(tab)) {
  task$set_col_roles("target", "target")
} else {
  task$set_col_roles("target", c("target", "stratum"))
}
task$.__enclos_env__$private$.col_roles$feature <- setdiff(
  task$.__enclos_env__$private$.col_roles$feature,
  intersect("group", task$backend$colnames)
)
task <- sanitize_task_col_roles(task)

# Last guard: a character column that slipped through would crash the
# pipeline much later with a cryptic error, so stop here with a clear one.
unsupported_feature_types <- task$feature_types[type == "character", id]
if (length(unsupported_feature_types)) {
  stop(
    "Unsupported character feature columns reached the modeling task: ",
    paste(unsupported_feature_types, collapse = ", "),
    ". Convert or remove them before feature selection."
  )
}

# ── Internal test set (evaluation.test_split) ────────────────────────────────
# Reserved first, before feature selection, tuning, the outer folds and the
# final model see anything. With test_split > 0 the reserved samples are whole
# groups (group role, dataset.group) or a class-stratified draw, scored once by
# the final models in the Prediction section. With test_split = 0 (the default)
# nothing is reserved: the final model uses all samples, and generalisation comes
# from the outer folds below plus the external set.
#   task_train – what selection, tuning, the outer folds and the final model see
#   task_test  – the reserved part, or NULL
test_split_ids <- build_test_split(task, eval_test_split, seed)
if (!is.null(test_split_ids)) {
  task_train <- sanitize_task_col_roles(task$clone(deep = TRUE)$filter(test_split_ids$train_ids))
  task_test  <- sanitize_task_col_roles(task$clone(deep = TRUE)$filter(test_split_ids$test_ids))
  cat(sprintf("\nInternal test set: %d of %d samples reserved (test_split = %s%s)\n",
              task_test$nrow, task$nrow, eval_test_split,
              if ("group" %in% names(tab)) ", whole groups" else ", stratified by class"))
} else {
  task_train <- sanitize_task_col_roles(task$clone(deep = TRUE))
  task_test  <- NULL
}

# ── Outer evaluation folds ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The outer resampling decides which TRAINING samples are tested in each
# fold and is instantiated here, once, on task_train, so every learner meets
# the same folds. With dataset.group set, the task carries the "group" role
# and mlr3 makes every strategy work on whole groups: "lodo" = one fold per
# group, "cv" = whole groups per fold. The rarest class caps the fold count
# (build_outer_resampling).
min_class_count <- min(table(task_train$truth()))
outer_resampling <- build_outer_resampling(
  outer = eval_outer,
  outer_folds = eval_outer_folds,
  outer_repeats = eval_outer_repeats,
  min_count = min_class_count,
  task = task_train
)

# The inner (tuning) resampling: NULL = "auto" (train_methods() picks per
# method), otherwise the explicit choice from the config, grouped like the task.
inner_resampling <- if (eval_inner == "auto") NULL else build_inner_resampling(
  inner = eval_inner, inner_folds = eval_inner_folds, inner_repeats = eval_inner_repeats,
  min_count = min_class_count, task = task_train
)

# num_jobs "auto": one parallel worker per inner fold, never more than cores.
# With a grouping column the fold count is taken as the number of groups: the
# inner resampling is leave-one-group-out up to max(inner_folds, 10) groups
# (choose_tuning_resampling()). Above that it is k-fold over the groups
# (evaluation.inner_folds folds), so the group count overstates the folds and
# the worker count can exceed them. Without groups it is evaluation.inner_folds.
if (identical(num_jobs, "auto")) {
  inner_iterations <- if ("group" %in% names(tab)) length(unique(as.character(tab$group))) else eval_inner_folds
  num_jobs <- max(1L, min(as.integer(num_threads), as.integer(inner_iterations)))
}
cat("Parallel workers for tuning the R learners (num_jobs):", num_jobs, "\n")

outer_fold_table <- describe_outer_folds(outer_resampling, group_lookup = group_lookup)
cat(sprintf("\nEvaluation design: test_split = %s, outer = %s (%d fold%s), nested = %s, inner = %s\n",
            eval_test_split, eval_outer, outer_resampling$iters, if (outer_resampling$iters > 1) "s" else "",
            eval_nested, eval_inner))
print(outer_fold_table)

# Binary tasks: tell mlr3 which class is "positive". This orients AUC, PR-AUC,
# precision, recall, specificity and F1, and the prob.<class> column the
# Benchmark chunk averages. positive_class comes from the config, or was set to
# the minority class in the pre-process chunk.
if (exists("dataset_attr") && dataset_attr == "binary" &&
    exists("positive_class") && positive_class %in% levels(task$truth())) {
  task$positive       <- positive_class
  task_train$positive <- positive_class
  if (!is.null(task_test)) task_test$positive <- positive_class
}

# Freeze the untouched post-split tasks. Feature selection shrinks task_train
# and task_test in place, so a rerun of that chunk would otherwise start from
# the already-reduced tasks; it restarts from these copies instead.
task_train_base <- task_train$clone(deep = TRUE)

# Resolve fast_tuning ONCE, here, from the task before feature selection.
# Each outer fold selects its own taxa; if the rule were applied to each fold's
# post-selection task, a fold that kept 20 taxa would tune under a different
# protocol than a fold that kept 125. Resolved here, every fold and the final
# model tune the same way.
if (fast_tuning && (length(task_train_base$feature_names) < 25 || task_train_base$nrow < 500)) {
  message("preprocessing.fast_tuning is off: ", length(task_train_base$feature_names),
          " features and ", task_train_base$nrow,
          " samples are below the 25 / 500 the shortcuts need to pay off.")
  fast_tuning <- FALSE
}
task_test_base <- if (!is.null(task_test)) task_test$clone(deep = TRUE) else NULL

# Diagnostics: sizes, classes and the class-by-study tables for each split. A
# study with only one class cannot be scored meaningfully when held out under
# LODO, so this is worth a look before training.
# Unquoted `group_col` and `pta` are the settings-chunk variables holding the NAME of
# the metadata columns copied into tab$group / tab$pta, printed so the report
# records which columns were used. print_group_diagnostics() comes from the
# Preprocess Data chunk and prints only.
cat("\nTask summary:\n")
cat("  Samples:", task$nrow, "\n")
cat("  Features:", length(task$feature_names), "\n")
cat("  Target:", task$target_names, "\n")
cat("  Classes:", paste(levels(task$truth()), collapse = ", "), "\n")
if ("group" %in% names(tab)) {
  cat("  LODO column:", group_col, "\n")
  cat("  Datasets:", length(unique(as.character(tab$group))), "\n")
}
if ("pta" %in% names(tab)) {
  cat("  PTA source column:", pta, "\n")
  cat("  PTA groups:", length(unique(as.character(tab$pta))), "\n")
}
if ("group" %in% task_train$backend$colnames) {
  print_group_diagnostics(task_train$data(cols = c("target", "group")), "group", "Training groups")
}
if (!is.null(pta_lookup)) {
  train_pta <- tab[match(task_train$row_ids, row_ids), c("target", "pta"), drop = FALSE]
  print_group_diagnostics(train_pta, "pta", "Training PTA groups")
}
if (!is.null(task_test) && "group" %in% task_test$backend$colnames) {
  print_group_diagnostics(task_test$data(cols = c("target", "group")), "group", "Test groups")
}
if (!is.null(task_test) && !is.null(pta_lookup)) {
  test_pta <- tab[match(task_test$row_ids, row_ids), c("target", "pta"), drop = FALSE]
  print_group_diagnostics(test_pta, "pta", "Test PTA groups")
}
```

#### Prepare Modeling Inputs

Defines the preprocessing in front of every learner: drop constant and redundant taxa, scale, and oversample the minority class when the imbalance rule asks for it. Packaged as an mlr3 graph and attached to each learner, so every step is refitted inside each fold instead of once on all the data.

```{r preprocess, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Define the preprocessing that sits in front of every learner: constant and
# redundant-taxa filters, scaling, and SMOTE oversampling when needed. Decided
# from the training split only.
#
# Input: task_train from the task chunk; config values smote, filtering,
#        selecting and the smote_* thresholds from the settings chunk.
# Output: training_preprocessing_pipe (an mlr3pipelines graph) and
#         training_preproc_params (its tunable settings), both handed to
#         train_methods() in "Train models", which puts the graph in front of
#         each learner. The graph being part of the learner, its filters are
#         re-fitted inside every fold, so a fold's test part never shapes them.

# Class balance of the training split: the majority/minority ratio decides
# whether SMOTE is switched on below.
class_counts <- table(task_train$data()$target)
majority_class <- names(which.max(class_counts))
minority_class <- names(which.min(class_counts))
imbalance_ratio <- class_counts[majority_class] / class_counts[minority_class]

# Print class distribution information
cat("\nClass Distribution Analysis:\n")
print(class_counts)
cat("\nMajority Class:", majority_class, "with", class_counts[majority_class], "instances\n")
cat("Minority Class:", minority_class, "with", class_counts[minority_class], "instances\n")
cat("Imbalance Ratio:", round(imbalance_ratio, 2), ":", "1\n")

# Plot Class Distribution

# Create dataframe for plotting
class_counts_df <- as.data.frame(class_counts)
colnames(class_counts_df) <- c("target", "count")

# Plot class distribution
ggplot(class_counts_df, aes(x = target, y = count, fill = target)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +  
  geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -0.5, size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Class Distribution",
    x = "Target Class",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

# Decide on SMOTE (synthetic minority oversampling): it invents extra
# minority-class samples by interpolating between a sample and its K nearest
# minority neighbours, so the learner does not just vote for the majority class.
# It runs inside the pipeline, so only on the training part of each fold.
# Switched on only when the imbalance exceeds the threshold AND every class has
# enough samples for the K-nearest-neighbour interpolation — a heavily
# imbalanced but tiny minority class cannot be safely oversampled.
apply_smote <- imbalance_ratio > smote_imbalance_threshold &&
  all(class_counts >= smote_min_samples_per_class)

# The SMOTE family interpolates towards ONE minority class, so on a multi-class
# target it closes the biggest gap and leaves the smaller classes as they were:
# the balance it produces is not the balance you asked for. "balance" is the
# multi-class-safe option - po("classbalancing") resamples every class towards
# the same size by drawing rows, inventing nothing.
smote_is_binary_only <- smote %in% c("smote", "blsmote", "adasyn")
smote_was_auto <- identical(smote, "")   # read below, against evaluation.prior_correction
if (smote == "") {
  # Automatic: pick the method that suits the target, not only whether to act.
  smote <- if (!apply_smote) "none" else if (dataset_attr == "binary") "smote" else "balance"
} else if (smote_is_binary_only && dataset_attr != "binary") {
  message(sprintf(
    "preprocessing.smote = '%s' oversamples towards a single minority class and mis-balances a %s target. Using 'balance' (classbalancing) instead.",
    smote, dataset_attr
  ))
  smote <- "balance"
}

# Every method is off when the classes are already even enough, or when a class
# is too small to resample safely.
if (!apply_smote) {
  smote <- "none"
}

# Balancing the training rows (SMOTE, classbalancing) and correcting the
# decision for the class frequencies (evaluation.prior_correction) both aim at
# balanced accuracy. Applied together they correct the imbalance twice and
# over-predict the small classes: on an 80/20 binary task balanced accuracy fell
# from 0.69 to 0.57, with the minority class predicted for 88 % of samples. The
# automatic choice defers to the correction; an explicit choice of both stops.
if (eval_prior_correction && smote != "none") {
  if (smote_was_auto) {
    message("Class imbalance ratio ", round(imbalance_ratio, 1), ": class balancing is left off, because ",
            "evaluation.prior_correction already corrects the decision for the class frequencies.")
    smote <- "none"
  } else {
    stop("preprocessing.smote = '", smote, "' and evaluation.prior_correction = true both correct for ",
         "class imbalance, and together they over-predict the small classes. Set one of them off.", call. = FALSE)
  }
}

# Print final decision on SMOTE
cat("\nFinal SMOTE decision:", smote, "\n")

# Initialize SMOTE pipeline as NULL
smote_pipe <- NULL

# Build the mlr3pipelines preprocessing graph: a chain of "pipeops" (pipeline
# operators) linked by %>>%, each fitted on training data and then applied the
# same way to new data. ppl("robustify") is a ready-made preset — impute missing
# values, encode factors, drop constant columns. The colapply step turns
# whole-number and TRUE/FALSE columns into decimals so every learner sees the
# same column types. Modes (config `filtering`):
#   "varcor"   – robustify + drop zero-variance + drop highly correlated taxa (Spearman)
#   "minimal"  – robustify only (forced when wrapper feature selection follows)
#   TRUE       – same as "minimal"
#   "infogain" – robustify + keep the taxa whose abundance says most about the
#                class (information gain, the score the Feature Selection chunk
#                uses as prefilter); the fraction kept is tuned
#   FALSE      – no-op (data passes through unchanged)
# Every mode but FALSE appends scaling: each taxon shifted to mean 0 and divided
# by its standard deviation, so abundant taxa do not dominate.
preprocessing_pipe <- NULL

# Switch to minimal filtering when wrapper feature selection is active,
# otherwise the variance / correlation filters would throw away taxa the wrapper
# deliberately kept. This graph is not in front of the wrapper: the Feature
# Selection chunk runs its learners directly on task_train, and the graph is
# attached to learners only in Train models, after selection.
if (selecting && !identical(filtering, "minimal")) {
  message(sprintf("preprocessing.filtering = '%s' is ignored because selecting is true: wrapper selection replaces filtering (forced to 'minimal').", filtering))
}
if (selecting) filtering <- "minimal"

if (filtering == "varcor") {
  preprocessing_pipe <- ppl("robustify") %>>%
    po("filter", filter = flt("variance"), id = "variance_filter") %>>%
    po("filter", filter = flt("find_correlation"), method = "spearman", id = "correlation_filter") %>>%
    po("colapply", applicator = as.numeric, affect_columns = selector_type(c("integer", "logical", "numeric")))
} else if (filtering == TRUE || filtering == "minimal" || selecting == TRUE) {
  preprocessing_pipe <- ppl("robustify") %>>%
    po("colapply", applicator = as.numeric, affect_columns = selector_type(c("integer", "logical", "numeric")))
} else if (filtering == "infogain") {
  preprocessing_pipe <- ppl("robustify") %>>%
    po("filter", filter = flt("information_gain"), id = "infogain_filter") %>>%
    po("colapply", applicator = as.numeric, affect_columns = selector_type(c("integer", "logical", "numeric")))
} else if (filtering == FALSE) {
  preprocessing_pipe <- po("nop")
} else {
  # Unreachable: the settings chunk already rejected anything else. Here so the
  # accepted list and the branches cannot drift apart without someone noticing.
  stop("preprocessing.filtering = '", filtering, "' has no branch in the preprocessing graph.")
}

# Add scaling for filtered pipelines
if (filtering != FALSE) {
  preprocessing_pipe <- preprocessing_pipe %>>% po("scale", center = TRUE)
}

# SMOTE variants: "smote" oversamples everywhere in the minority class,
# "blsmote" (borderline) only near the class boundary, "adasyn" adds more
# synthetic samples where the minority class is sparse.
smote_pipe <- NULL
if (apply_smote && smote %in% c("smote", "blsmote", "adasyn", "balance")) {
  smote_pipe <- switch(smote,
    smote   = po("smote"),
    blsmote = po("blsmote"),
    adasyn  = po("adas"),
    # classbalancing resamples rows so every class reaches the size of the
    # largest one: it copies existing samples rather than interpolating new
    # ones, so it works for any number of classes and cannot invent a
    # community that could not exist.
    balance = po("classbalancing", adjust = "all", reference = "major", shuffle = FALSE),
    NULL)
}

# Add SMOTE if needed.
# On a grouped task (dataset.group set) the grouping column travels with the task
# and SMOTE refuses to invent values for it — rightly, a synthetic sample belongs
# to no study. The folds were drawn before training, so the grouping has already
# done its job: the role is stripped from the copy flowing through the graph and
# SMOTE sees only features and target.
if (!is.null(smote_pipe)) {
  if ("group" %in% names(tab)) {
    preprocessing_pipe <- preprocessing_pipe %>>%
      po("colroles", new_role = list(group = character(0))) %>>% smote_pipe
    message("Class balancing on a grouped task: the grouping column is dropped inside the learner graph, where it is not a feature.")
  } else {
    preprocessing_pipe <- preprocessing_pipe %>>% smote_pipe
  }
}

# mlr3torch (loaded for the MLP learner) registers an extra feature type,
# "lazy_tensor" ("lt"), on every pipeop. On our plain numeric tables that
# tag makes some pipeops fail their type checks, so strip it from each
# pipeop's private feature-type list; the graph then behaves like a plain
# mlr3 graph for every learner.
for (po_name in names(preprocessing_pipe$pipeops)) {
  po <- preprocessing_pipe$pipeops[[po_name]]
  if (!is.null(po$.__enclos_env__$private$.feature_types)) {
    if ("lt" %in% names(po$.__enclos_env__$private$.feature_types)) {
      cat(sprintf("Removing 'lazy_tensor' from %s\n", po_name))
      po$.__enclos_env__$private$.feature_types <-
        po$.__enclos_env__$private$.feature_types[
          names(po$.__enclos_env__$private$.feature_types) != "lt"
        ]
    }
  }
}

cat("\nFinal preprocessing pipeline:\n")
print(preprocessing_pipe)

# Preprocessing settings tuned jointly with each learner's own hyperparameters —
# the knobs chosen by trying values (number of trees, SMOTE K, filter fraction),
# not learned from the data. The trying happens in the inner cross-validation
# inside train_methods(), separate from the benchmark folds, so each learner
# gets its own best filter fraction or SMOTE K.
# Names are "<pipeop id>.<parameter>", e.g. variance_filter.filter.frac = the
# fraction of taxa that filter keeps. p_dbl()/p_int() give the search range
# (paradox syntax). logscale = TRUE has the tuner work on log(value), spacing
# candidates evenly in ratio terms rather than equal steps (0.5, 0.59, 0.71,
# 0.84, 1 over 0.5-1); it matters more for the wider 0.2-1 infogain range.
preproc_params <- list()

if (filtering == "varcor") {
  preproc_params <- c(preproc_params, list(
    variance_filter.filter.frac = p_dbl(0.5, 1, logscale = TRUE),
    correlation_filter.filter.frac = p_dbl(0.5, 1, logscale = TRUE)
  ))
} else if (filtering == "infogain") {
  preproc_params <- c(preproc_params,
    list(
      infogain_filter.filter.frac = p_dbl(0.2, 1.0, logscale = TRUE)
    )
  )
}

if (!is.null(smote_pipe)) {
  # Cap K (minority neighbours SMOTE interpolates between) to what any inner CV
  # training fold can supply. With folds = min_count each fold has min_count-1
  # minority samples and SMOTE needs K+1, so K <= min_count-2. The max(2L, ...)
  # floors K at 2: harmless at the default min_samples_per_class = 5, but lower
  # that and a rarest class of 3 gives K = 2 > min_count-2 = 1, so SMOTE can
  # fail inside a fold.
  # Also tuned: dup_size = synthetic samples per real minority sample (1-5);
  # blsmote.C = neighbours from BOTH classes used to decide whether a minority
  # sample sits on the class border (only those are oversampled).
  smote_k_max <- max(2L, min(5L, as.integer(min(class_counts)) - 2L))
  if (smote == "smote") {
    preproc_params <- c(preproc_params, list(
      smote.K = p_int(2L, smote_k_max),
      smote.dup_size = p_int(1, 5)
    ))
  } else if (smote == "blsmote") {
    preproc_params <- c(preproc_params, list(
      blsmote.K = p_int(2L, smote_k_max),
      blsmote.dup_size = p_int(1, 5),
      blsmote.C = p_int(1, 5)
    ))
  } else if (smote == "adasyn") {
    preproc_params <- c(preproc_params, list(
      adas.K = p_int(2L, smote_k_max)
    ))
  }
}

# The two objects the "Train models" chunk hands to train_methods().
training_preprocessing_pipe <- preprocessing_pipe
training_preproc_params <- preproc_params
```

#### Feature Selection

Optional (`preprocessing.selecting`). A random forest is refit on shrinking subsets of taxa and the smallest subset scoring about as well as the best one is kept: recursive elimination with the one-standard-error rule. At ten samples or fewer, four learners vote instead. The kept taxa replace the full set in both tasks and go to `metrics/selected_features.csv`.

```{r feature selection, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# The selection lives in R/tabflux_selection_helpers.R (select_features), so the
# same code runs here — once, on all training data, for the final model — and
# again inside every outer evaluation fold when evaluation.nested is TRUE.
# Skipped when the config flag `selecting` is FALSE.
#
# Input:  task_train_base / task_test_base (frozen in the task chunk).
# Output: task_train and task_test reduced to `selected_feats`, plus
#         metrics/selected_features.csv (a record of the selected taxa) and, in
#         ensemble mode, feature_selection_stability.csv. The reduced
#         task_train is what the final tuning then works on.
if (selecting) {
  if (!exists("task_train_base")) {
    stop("Feature selection requires saved base tasks. Rerun the task-definition chunk first.")
  }

  # Always restart from the frozen copies, so rerunning this chunk does not
  # select from an already-reduced task.
  set.seed(seed + 100L, kind = "Mersenne-Twister", normal.kind = "Inversion", sample.kind = "Rejection")   # own seed AND generator kind, independent of what ran before
fs_result <- select_features(
    task_train = task_train_base$clone(deep = TRUE),
    task_test = if (!is.null(task_test_base)) task_test_base$clone(deep = TRUE) else NULL,
    seed = seed,
    num_threads = num_threads,
    out_dir = metrics_dir,
    prior_correction = eval_prior_correction
  )
  selected_feats <- fs_result$selected_feats
  task_train <- fs_result$task_train
  task_test <- fs_result$task_test
}
```

#### Visualize Model Results

Runs only when feature selection was on: the PCA and t-SNE of the Inspect Data section, repeated on the selected taxa alone. A visual check of whether the reduced set separates the classes better than the full table did. Nothing here feeds the models.

```{r final look, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
if (selecting) {
  # Visual check after feature selection: repeat the PCA and t-SNE
  # ordinations from the "Inspect Data" section on the selected taxa only,
  # to see whether the reduced set separates the classes better than the
  # full table did. Input: task_train (already reduced). Nothing here feeds
  # the models.
  df <- as_tibble(task_train$data())

  # y = class labels, X = numeric taxa matrix. Only "target" is actually
  # present in task data; the other metadata names are listed defensively.
  y  <- df$target
  metadata_cols <- c("target", "Sample", "group", "pta")
  X <- df[, !(names(df) %in% metadata_cols), drop = FALSE]
  X[] <- lapply(X, function(col) {
    if (is.factor(col)) col <- as.character(col)
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(col))
  })
  
  # Optional downsample for speed: t-SNE is slow on thousands of samples.
  # Both thresholds come from the visualization section of config.yaml
  # (settings chunk). y is subset with X so the labels stay aligned.
  if (nrow(X) > viz_downsample_threshold) {
    idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(X)), viz_downsample_size)
    X <- X[idx, , drop = FALSE]
    y <- y[idx]
  }

  # 1) Stop on missing values (non-numeric cells were coerced to NA above).
  if (any(vapply(X, anyNA, logical(1)))) {
    stop("Feature matrix contains non-numeric or missing values after preprocessing; check taxa columns for invalid entries.")
  }

  # Two ordination paths, depending on what the normalization chunk produced:
  #   normalization == "none": the task still holds raw counts, so take the
  #     compositional route (prevalence filter -> zero replacement -> CLR), as
  #     in the pre-modeling ordination above.
  #   otherwise: the values are already depth-corrected and log-scaled
  #     (tss/tss_log/tss_clr). Zero replacement and CLR would be wrong —
  #     cmultRepl() expects counts and no true zeros are left — so ordinate the
  #     normalized values directly. No prevalence filter either: only the
  #     features that survived selection are present.
  if (normalization == "none") {
    prev <- colMeans(X > 0)
    X <- X[, prev >= viz_prevalence_threshold, drop = FALSE]
    if (ncol(X) == 0)
      stop("All features filtered out; lower the prevalence threshold.")
    X <- X[, apply(X, 2, var) > 0, drop = FALSE]

    # 2) Zero replacement WITHOUT deletions
    X0 <- zCompositions::cmultRepl(
      as.matrix(X),
      label = 0,
      method = "CZM",
      z.warning = 1,
      # silence high-zero warnings
      z.delete  = FALSE
    ) # do not drop rows/cols

    # 3) CLR transform
    X_clr <- compositions::clr(X0)
    ordination_label <- "CLR-transformed abundances"
  } else {
    X <- X[, apply(X, 2, var) > 0, drop = FALSE]
    if (ncol(X) == 0)
      stop("All selected features have zero variance; cannot draw ordinations.")
    X_clr <- as.matrix(X)   # name kept for the shared PCA/t-SNE code below
    ordination_label <- paste0(normalization, "-normalized abundances")
  }
  
  # PCA on X_clr. CLR-transformed only when normalization == "none"; with
  # tss / tss_log / tss_clr these are the normalized values as they are (see
  # ordination_label, which the plot titles use).
  pca <- prcomp(X_clr, scale. = TRUE)
  
  # Scree plot of PCA variance, as in Inspect Data. print() is needed inside
  # this if-block, where R shows nothing it is not told to print.
  print(fviz_eig(pca, addlabels = TRUE))
  
  # PCA plot
  scores <- data.frame(PC1 = pca$x[, 1],
                       PC2 = pca$x[, 2],
                       target = y)
  
  print(
    ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, fill = target)) +
      geom_point(
        shape = 21,
        size = 5,
        colour = "white",
        stroke = 0.8
      ) +
      scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo", name = "target") +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(
        title = paste("PCA on", ordination_label),
        x = paste0("PC1 (", round(100 * summary(pca)$importance[2, 1], 1), "%)"),
        y = paste0("PC2 (", round(100 * summary(pca)$importance[2, 2], 1), "%)")
      )
  )
  
  # Loadings contributions (top 10)
  print(fviz_contrib(
    pca,
    choice = "var",
    axes = 1:2,
    top = 10
  ))
  
  # Elbow plot: how many PCs are needed to reach 90% cumulative variance — a
  # rough measure of how many independent axes of variation the selected
  # taxa carry.
  cumulative_prop_var <- cumsum(pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2))
  
  # Find number of components explaining 90% of variance
  num_components <- which(cumulative_prop_var >= 0.9)[1]
  
  # Print number of components
  cat("Number of components explaining 90% of variance:",
      num_components,
      "\n")
  
  # Create a data frame with the number of components and their cumulative proportion of variance explained
  elbow_df <-
    data.frame(
      Num_Components = 1:length(cumulative_prop_var),
      Cumulative_Proportion_Var_Explained = cumulative_prop_var
    )
  
  # Plot the elbow plot
  print(
    ggplot(
      elbow_df,
      aes(x = Num_Components, y = Cumulative_Proportion_Var_Explained)
    ) +
      geom_line() +
      geom_point() +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = num_components,
        color = "dodgerblue3",
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, length(
        cumulative_prop_var
      ), 1)) +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(
        title = "Elbow plot of PCA components",
        subtitle = "Reference line: components explaining up to 90% variance",
        x = "Number of components",
        y = "Cumulative proportion of variance explained"
      )
  )
  
  # Get the PCA loading matrix
  loadings <- pca$rotation
  
  # Find the variable with highest absolute loading for each principal component
  variables <- rownames(loadings)  # Get the variable names
  max_loadings <-
    apply(abs(loadings), 2, function(x)
      variables[which.max(x)])
  
  # Output the results
  for (i in 1:ncol(loadings)) {
    cat(paste0("Most important variable for PC", i, ": ", max_loadings[i]),
        "\n")
  }
  
  # t-SNE on the same X_clr matrix as the PCA (CLR only when
  # normalization == "none", see above).
  perplexity <- pmin(30, floor((nrow(X_clr) - 1) / 3))  # safe, within 5–30 typical
  ts <- Rtsne(
    X_clr,
    pca = FALSE,
    check_duplicates = FALSE,
    perplexity = perplexity,
    theta = 0.5
  )
  
  ts_df <- data.frame(tSNE1 = ts$Y[, 1],
                      tSNE2 = ts$Y[, 2],
                      target = y)
  
  print(
    ggplot(ts_df, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, fill = target)) +
      geom_point(
        shape = 21,
        size = 5,
        colour = "white",
        stroke = 0.8
      ) +
      scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo", name = "target") +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(title = paste("t-SNE on", ordination_label))
  )
    }
```

#### Train models

Each picked method gets a graph — the preprocessing above, then the learner — and both are tuned together, scored by inner resampling on balanced accuracy and log-loss (a penalty for confident wrong probabilities; lower is better).

The tuner depends on the learner: grid search for glmnet, kknn and SVM, Hyperband for the random forest, random search for XGBoost and the MLP, one fixed setting for TabPFN. `fast_tuning` switches glmnet, kknn and SVM to successive halving, runs one Hyperband round instead of three and halves the random searches; the Define Task section turns it off below 25 features or 500 samples. Under a grouping column, inner resampling is leave-one-group-out up to max(inner_folds, 10) groups and k-fold over the groups above that; without one, it is k-fold or repeated k-fold.

Tuned learners are saved as `<method>_tuned_learner.rds` and reused on a re-render. Details in `R/tabflux_training_helpers.R`.

**Reading the printouts below:** the scores in this section are each learner's *internal* search results — its own settings on its own tuning folds. They are not comparable between learners (one learner's search maximum against another's single fixed setting), and the printed values are inflated the way any best-of-many is. The fair model-to-model comparison is the Benchmark section, where all learners face the same folds.

```{r classification, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Tune and fit one model per selected method (config `methods`: random forest,
# xgboost, TabPFN, ...).
#
# Input:  task_train (reduced by feature selection if it ran),
#         training_preprocessing_pipe + training_preproc_params from the
#         "Prepare Modeling Inputs" chunk, and the execution settings.
# Per method, train_methods() (R/tabflux_training_helpers.R) joins the
# preprocessing graph and the learner into one graph learner and searches its
# hyperparameters — filter fractions, SMOTE K, the learner's own. The tuner
# comes from get_tuner_for_method(): grid search for glmnet, kknn and svm;
# Hyperband (many configurations get a small budget, the promising ones get
# more) for ranger; random search (80 settings) for xgboost and mlp; a grid of
# one fixed setting for tabpfn. fast_tuning switches glmnet/kknn/svm to
# successive halving (one Hyperband round), ranger to 1 Hyperband repetition
# instead of 3, and xgboost/mlp to 40 settings. The Define Task chunk already
# turned it off below 25 features or 500 samples.
# Inner resampling per configuration (choose_tuning_resampling()):
# with a grouping column, leave-one-group-out up to max(inner_folds, 10)
# groups and k-fold over the groups above that; otherwise CV with as many folds
# as the rarest class has samples (at least 2) when that class is no bigger
# than inner_folds; plain k-fold for >= 500 samples or for mlp / tabpfn /
# xgboost; repeated k-fold (inner_repeats x inner_folds) otherwise. Measures:
# balanced accuracy and log-loss (train_measures; log-loss penalises confident
# wrong probabilities).
# Output: <method>_tuned_learner.rds in save_dir, a <method>_tuned_learner
#         object in the global environment, and the list learners_best, which
#         the benchmark chunk reloads so a re-render skips finished methods.

# future = R's parallel backend. Reset to sequential first; below we switch
# to multisession (separate R processes) only when num_jobs > 1.
future::plan(sequential)

# Base learner objects for every method (untuned, predict_type = "prob").
# The helper also decides whether parallel tuning is allowed: TabPFN runs
# through Python (reticulate) and is forced to a single process.
learner_setup <- build_classification_learners(
  methods = methods,
  seed = seed,
  num_jobs = num_jobs
)
learners <- learner_setup$learners
# Workers for tuning the R learners inside train_methods(): the value asked
# for in the config, kept BEFORE the TabPFN override on the next line, which
# only concerns this notebook's own plan and TabPFN itself.
tuning_workers <- num_jobs
num_jobs <- learner_setup$num_jobs

if (learner_setup$force_sequential || num_jobs <= 1) {
  future::plan(sequential)
} else {
  future::plan(multisession, workers = num_jobs)
}

# Metrics xgboost watches for early stopping: error/logloss for binary,
# merror/mlogloss for multi-class.
eval_metrics <- get_eval_metrics(dataset_attr)

# Training-set numbers the helpers use. min_count (smallest class size) decides
# the inner CV fold count in choose_tuning_resampling(). num_feat and num_obs
# size the hyperparameter ranges, and num_obs >= 500 also picks plain k-fold
# over repeated k-fold. The SMOTE K cap came from class_counts in the
# preprocess chunk.
training_stats <- get_training_task_stats(task_train)
min_count <- training_stats$min_count
num_feat <- training_stats$num_feat
num_obs <- training_stats$num_obs

# Run the tuning loop. assign_env = .GlobalEnv puts each <method>_tuned_learner
# into the workspace for the benchmark chunk to find.
# Arguments not covered above:
#   tab              – read only to check for a "group" column and switch the
#                      inner resampling to whole groups (leave-one-group-out,
#                      or k-fold over the groups when there are many).
#   term_min         – wall-clock tuning cap in minutes, SVM only; the random
#                      searches stop after a fixed number of settings, the
#                      others when their grid or Hyperband schedule is done.
#   inner_folds / inner_repeats – the (repeated) k-fold inner resampling used
#                      when tuning is not leave-one-group-out
#                      (evaluation.inner_folds / inner_repeats).
#   learner_fallback – run each fit in a separate R process and fall back to a
#                      majority-class model when it errors, so one bad setting
#                      does not abort hours of tuning.
set.seed(seed + 200L, kind = "Mersenne-Twister", normal.kind = "Inversion", sample.kind = "Rejection")   # own seed AND generator kind, independent of what ran before
learners_best <- train_methods(
  methods = methods,
  learners = learners,
  preprocessing_pipe = training_preprocessing_pipe,
  task_train = task_train,
  tab = tab,
  preproc_params = training_preproc_params,
  save_dir = save_dir,
  train_measures = train_measures,
  fast_tuning = fast_tuning,
  learner_fallback = learner_fallback,
  num_threads = num_threads,
  tuning_workers = tuning_workers,     # parallel workers for the R learners (TabPFN stays sequential)
  inner_folds = eval_inner_folds,      # tuning folds when the inner resampling is k-fold (settings chunk)
  inner_repeats = eval_inner_repeats,
  term_min = term_min,
  selection_rule = tuning_selection,   # which Pareto-front setting to refit (settings chunk)
  prior_correction = eval_prior_correction,   # tune on the corrected balanced accuracy
  eval_metrics = eval_metrics,
  min_count = min_count,
  num_feat = num_feat,
  num_obs = num_obs,
  assign_env = .GlobalEnv
)
```

#### Benchmark

Compares the learners on the outer folds built in Define Task. With `evaluation.nested` on, feature selection and tuning are repeated inside every fold, on its training part alone and over the full feature space; with it off, the final learners are only refit and scored.

Reports the mean per method, the per-fold scores (`fold_metrics.csv`) and, under a grouping column, the score per held-out group (`lodo_metrics.csv`). The best method is chosen here on the resampling, never on a test set.

```{r benchmarking, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Compare the tuned learners on equal footing, pick the best, and look at its
# cross-validated predictions.
#
# Input:  the tuned learners (from memory or save_dir), task_train and
#         task_train_base, the outer folds (outer_resampling, Define Task
#         chunk), the metric set bmr_measures from the pre-process chunk, the
#         group_col/pta lookups from the task chunk and the evaluation settings.
# Output: outer_results (one row per learner x outer fold, from
#         run_outer_evaluation()), bench_df (mean metrics per method, written
#         to benchmark_metrics.csv in the Save Metrics chunk), fold_metrics
#         (metrics/fold_metrics.csv), metrics/lodo_metrics.csv (grouped designs
#         only), metrics/predictions.csv, learners_best (the fitted learners the
#         Prediction and External Test chunks loop over) and best_model_id /
#         best_method, used for the prediction plots below and by the
#         importance/SHAP chunk. Prediction and External Test score every
#         learner, not just the best one.

# Measure for the per-fold boxplot only; the tables use the full bmr_measures.
measure = c('accuracy' = "classif.acc")

# Inspect what the preprocessing pipeline produced after training — a sanity
# check before reading the benchmark results. Two outcomes:
#   - the pipeop named by `after` (the SMOTE step by default) has a Task
#     output: return the taxa the learner saw and the class counts after
#     oversampling; the filters are not reported.
#   - no such pipeop, or no Task output (filtering is FALSE, so there is no
#     scale step either, or the learner ran in a separate R process with the
#     fallback model): warn, print a per-filter table (taxa considered / kept)
#     and return it with NA for the rest. That table is empty whenever the
#     graph is robustify-only, i.e. with filtering "minimal" or selecting TRUE.
# Reads the pipeop outputs kept by keep_results = TRUE in
# configure_final_learner(); learner$train() below refreshes them.
get_final_preproc_summary <- function(graph_learner, after = smote) {
  stopifnot(inherits(graph_learner, "GraphLearner"))

  # `after` arrives as the SMOTE setting from the config, not as a pipeop id.
  # Map it to the id of the last preprocessing step in the graph:
  # no SMOTE -> the scaling step is last; "adasyn" was built as po("adas") and
  # "balance" as po("classbalancing"). Without this mapping, "none" (the usual
  # case) would match no pipeop and the feature summary would be skipped silently.
  after <- switch(after, none = "scale", adasyn = "adas", balance = "classbalancing", after)

  po_out <- graph_learner$graph_model$pipeops[[after]]$.result$output
  features_summary <- NULL
  class_counts <- NULL
  
  if (is.null(po_out) || !("Task" %in% class(po_out))) {
    warning(
      sprintf(
        "The specified pipeop '%s' has no valid Task output. Was the graph learner trained with fallback encapsulation or did training fail? Only filter summary will be shown.",
        after
      )
    )
    # Always print filter summary regardless of po_out
    pipeops_out <- graph_learner$graph_model$pipeops
    filter_summary <- data.frame(
      filter_id = character(),
      considered = integer(),
      selected = integer(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    features_per_filter <- list()
    for (id in names(pipeops_out)) {
      po = pipeops_out[[id]]
      if (inherits(po, "PipeOpFilter")) {
        considered = length(po$state$affected_cols)
        selected   = length(po$state$features)
        filter_summary <- rbind(
          filter_summary,
          data.frame(
            filter_id = id,
            considered = considered,
            selected = selected,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
          )
        )
        features_per_filter[[id]] <- po$state$features
      }
    }
    print(filter_summary)
    return(list(
      features = NA,
      n_features = NA,
      class_distribution = NA,
      filter_summary = filter_summary,
      features_per_filter = features_per_filter
    ))
  }
  
  # If po_out is a Task, proceed as normal
  features_summary <- po_out$feature_names
  class_data <- po_out$data(cols = "target")
  class_counts <- if ("target" %in% colnames(class_data)) table(class_data$target) else NA
  
  list(
    features = features_summary,
    n_features = length(features_summary),
    class_distribution = class_counts
  )
}

# Benchmarking setup: folds run in parallel via future when num_jobs > 1.
future::plan(sequential)

if (num_jobs > 1) {
  future::plan(multisession, workers = num_jobs)
}

# The folds every learner is scored on (outer_resampling) were built and
# instantiated in the Define Task chunk from config `evaluation`, so all
# methods meet exactly the same folds and the design is printed there.

# Load each tuned learner in priority order: (1) in memory from the training
# chunk, (2) saved .rds on disk, (3) skip with a warning. They come back already
# fitted (train_methods() refits the best setting on all of task_train before
# saving), and every fold refits them anyway. The learner$train(task_train)
# below is for get_final_preproc_summary(): it refreshes the pipeop outputs so
# the filter / SMOTE summary reflects this run. learners_best is rebuilt here on
# purpose — in a fresh session only the .rds files exist.
learners_best <- list()
for (method in names(methods)) {
  obj_name <- paste(method, "tuned", "learner", sep = "_")
  learner_name <- paste0(method, "_tuned_learner.rds")
  learner_path <- file.path(save_dir, learner_name)

  # Priority 1: already in memory from this session's training chunk
  if (exists(obj_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
    cat("\nMethod:", method, "| found in memory (", obj_name, ")\n")
    learner <- get(obj_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  } else if (file.exists(learner_path)) {
    # Priority 2: .rds file from a previous session
    cat("\nMethod:", method, "->", learner_path, "| file exists, loading from disk\n")
    learner <- tryCatch(
      readRDS(learner_path),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("  !!! Error loading", learner_name, ":", e$message, "\n")
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
    if (is.null(learner)) next
  } else {
    cat("\nMethod:", method, "| SKIP: No tuned model found in memory or disk.\n")
    next
  }
  
  # Torch (MLP) models are saved in a "marshalled" form — converted to plain
  # R objects so they survive saveRDS — and must be unpacked before use.
  # For every other learner this call does nothing.
  learner$unmarshal()
  
  # One thread per learner: the folds run in parallel via future, so
  # internal multithreading would only start more threads than there are
  # cores and slow all of them down.
  learner <- tryCatch(
    set_threads(learner, n = 1),
    error = function(e) {
      cat("  !!! Error setting threads for", method, ":", e$message, "\n")
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  if (is.null(learner)) next

  cat("  --> Training learner:", method, "\n")
  tryCatch({
    learner$train(task_train)
    learners_best[[method]] <- learner
    cat("  --> SUCCESS: Trained and stored learner for", method, "\n")
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error training", method, ":", e$message, "\n")
  })
}

# For each fitted learner, print the taxa that survived its preprocessing
# filters and the class counts after SMOTE, so the benchmark results below
# can be read knowing what each model saw.
for (method in names(learners_best)) {
  summary <- suppressWarnings(get_final_preproc_summary(learners_best[[method]]))
  if (!is.null(summary)) {
    cat(sprintf("\n--- [%s] ---\n", method))
    if (!is.na(summary$n_features)) {
      cat(sprintf("Final features (%d):\n", summary$n_features))
      print(summary$features)
      cat("Class distribution:\n")
      print(summary$class_distribution)
    } else {
      cat("No Task output; see filter summary above.\n")
    }
  }
}

# ── The outer evaluation loop ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One row per learner x outer fold, each holding that fold's prediction on its
# test part (run_outer_evaluation(), R/tabflux_evaluation_helpers.R):
#   nested = TRUE  – feature selection and tuning repeated inside every fold on
#                    its training part; that fold's tuned learners predict its
#                    test part. The honest estimate.
#   nested = FALSE – the final learners above (tuned once on all training data,
#                    features selected once, so selection saw every fold's test
#                    samples) are refit on each fold's training part and predict
#                    its test part.
# The loop runs over task_train_base (the training samples before feature
# selection), on which the outer folds were instantiated; a reserved internal
# test set never enters it. Per-fold files land in
# <save_dir>/outer_fold_<i>/ and are reused on rerun. outer_results has the same
# columns as as.data.table(<BenchmarkResult>).
start_time <- Sys.time()
cat(" Start time: ", format(start_time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")

outer_evaluation <- run_outer_evaluation(
  # task_train_base, NOT task_train: the Feature Selection chunk above replaced
  # task_train with the reduced task, and handing that to the outer loop would
  # have every fold select from a shortlist drawn with the held-out samples in
  # view - selection leakage, and the one thing a nested design exists to stop.
  # On the cFMD category run the one-shot selection keeps 15 of 7,847 SGBs;
  # starting the folds from those 15 would make every per-fold selection a
  # subset of them. The final model still uses task_train; only the estimate
  # has to start from the full feature space.
  #   nested = TRUE  - each fold selects from all features, on its own training part
  #   nested = FALSE - each fold is reduced to selected_feats, the one-shot
  #                    selection, which is what that (optimistic) mode means
  task = task_train_base,
  outer_resampling = outer_resampling,
  methods = methods,
  nested = eval_nested,
  selecting = selecting,
  learners_best = learners_best,
  selected_feats = if (selecting) selected_feats else NULL,
  train_args = list(
    methods = methods, learners = learners,
    preprocessing_pipe = training_preprocessing_pipe, preproc_params = training_preproc_params,
    tab = tab, train_measures = train_measures, fast_tuning = fast_tuning,
    learner_fallback = learner_fallback, num_threads = num_threads, tuning_workers = tuning_workers,
    inner_folds = eval_inner_folds, inner_repeats = eval_inner_repeats, term_min = term_min,
    selection_rule = tuning_selection,
    eval_metrics = eval_metrics, inner_resampling = inner_resampling,
    prior_correction = eval_prior_correction
  ),
  fs_args = list(seed = seed, num_threads = num_threads, prior_correction = eval_prior_correction),
  save_dir = save_dir,
  prior_correction = eval_prior_correction
)
outer_results <- outer_evaluation$results
cat("\nOuter folds:\n"); print(outer_evaluation$fold_info)

end_time <- Sys.time()
cat(" End time: ", format(end_time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")

# Report duration
time_diff <- difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "secs")

# Collect the per-learner timings into one table: the final models (run root)
# and each outer fold, plus the outer loop as a whole. This is the source for
# any statement about what a run costs.
timing_files <- c(
  file.path(save_dir, "timings.csv"),
  list.files(save_dir, pattern = "^timings\\.csv$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
)
timing_files <- unique(timing_files[file.exists(timing_files)])
timings <- do.call(rbind, lapply(timing_files, function(f) {
  d <- readr::read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
  where <- basename(dirname(f))
  d$stage <- if (grepl("^outer_fold_", where)) sub("^outer_fold_0*", "fold ", where) else "final model"
  d
}))
timings <- rbind(
  timings[, c("stage", "method", "seconds", "started", "finished")],
  data.frame(stage = "outer loop, all folds", method = "all",
             seconds = round(as.numeric(time_diff), 1),
             started = format(start_time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
             finished = format(end_time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"))
)
timings$minutes <- round(timings$seconds / 60, 1)
readr::write_csv(timings, file.path(metrics_dir, "timings.csv"))
if (time_diff < 60) {
  cat(" Time taken for benchmarking:", time_diff, " seconds\n")
} else {
  time_diff <- difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "mins")
  cat(" Time taken for benchmarking: ", time_diff, " minutes\n")
}

# Boxplot of accuracy per fold and method (one row per learner x fold).
# The spread across folds is what a single mean hides.
bmr_scores <- collect_benchmark_scores(
  bmr = outer_results,
  measures = list(msr(measure[[1]])),
  task = task_train,
  positive_class = positive_class,
  fairness_active = FALSE,
  pta_lookup = pta_lookup
)

bmr_scores %<>%
  mutate(
    method = recode_method_labels(learner_id)
  )

ggplot(bmr_scores, aes(x = method, y = .data[[measure[[1]]]])) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue3", alpha = 0.8, outlier.alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Method", y = paste(names(measure[1]), "measure")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# bench_df: the full metric set averaged over folds, one row per method.
# Fairness gaps (best-vs-worst PTA group) are added when fairness_active.
# Consumed by the barplot and best-model choice below, and later by the
# Performance Comparison and Save Metrics chunks.
bench_df <- aggregate_benchmark_scores(
  bmr = outer_results,
  measures = bmr_measures,
  task = task_train,
  positive_class = positive_class,
  fairness_active = fairness_active,
  pta_lookup = pta_lookup
)

# Tidy for display: readable method names in the first column, metric ids
# turned into plain labels ("classif.bacc" -> "balanced accuracy"), 4 decimals.
bench_df %<>%
  mutate(
    method = recode_method_labels(learner_id)
  ) %>%
  relocate(tail(names(.), 1), .before = names(.)[1]) %>%
  rename_with(~ label_measure_name(.x)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4)))

print(bench_df %>% select(-learner_id))

# ── Per-fold benchmark metrics ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# bench_df above is the average over folds; these fold-level scores show how
# much performance varies. Exported for every resampling mode, one row per
# method x fold, full metric set. Under LODO each fold is one held-out study, so
# the table also names it (heldout_group, via group_lookup from the task chunk):
# mlr3 shuffles fold order, so the iteration number alone would not tell.
fold_scores <- collect_benchmark_scores(
  bmr = outer_results,
  measures = bmr_measures,
  task = task_train,
  positive_class = positive_class,
  fairness_active = FALSE,   # PTA gaps are not meaningful within a single fold
  pta_lookup = NULL,
  group_lookup = group_lookup # NULL in plain CV mode -> no heldout_group column
)

# How many samples of each class each fold's test set held: a fold of 4 + 4
# supports much weaker conclusions than one of 30 + 30, so the class balance
# belongs next to the scores.
bmr_pred_dt <- outer_results
fold_class_counts <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(bmr_pred_dt)), function(i) {
  truth_counts <- table(bmr_pred_dt$prediction[[i]]$truth)
  tibble::tibble(
    learner_id = bmr_pred_dt$learner_id[[i]],
    iteration = bmr_pred_dt$iteration[[i]],
    n_test = length(bmr_pred_dt$prediction[[i]]$row_ids),
    class_counts = paste(names(truth_counts), truth_counts, sep = "=", collapse = "; ")
  )
})
# n_test already exists when a group lookup was used; keep one copy.
if ("n_test" %in% names(fold_scores)) fold_class_counts$n_test <- NULL

fold_metrics <- fold_scores %>%
  left_join(fold_class_counts, by = c("learner_id", "iteration")) %>%
  mutate(method = recode_method_labels(learner_id)) %>%
  rename_with(~ label_measure_name(.x)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) %>%
  relocate(method, iteration, n_test, class_counts) %>%
  arrange(method, iteration)
readr::write_csv(fold_metrics, file.path(metrics_dir, "fold_metrics.csv"))

# Mean and SD of every metric across the outer folds: the spread behind
# bench_df. Reported as "SD across folds" (groups under LODO), not as a
# standard error — folds share training data, so a proper confidence
# interval does not exist for cross-validation (see fold_metric_spread()).
# Read by the dumbbell plots (error bars) and the Save Metrics export.
bench_spread <- fold_metric_spread(fold_metrics)
readr::write_csv(bench_spread, file.path(metrics_dir, "benchmark_metrics_spread.csv"))
cat("\nSpread across outer folds (SD) of balanced accuracy and AUC:\n")
print(bench_spread %>% filter(metric %in% c("balanced accuracy", "auc", "logloss")) %>%
        mutate(across(c(mean, sd), ~ round(., 3))))

# ── Metrics per held-out group ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Runs for every grouped design, not only LODO. Under leave-one-dataset-out a
# fold holds out exactly one study, so the fold-wise scores ARE the per-study
# generalisation results: "how does the model do on a study it has never seen?",
# answered once per study. Under grouped k-fold (outer: cv with dataset.group
# set) a fold holds out a slice of the groups, so the same question is answered
# per fold instead. Same rows as fold_metrics, labelled by held-out group,
# printed, exported to lodo_metrics.csv (the filename is the convention for both
# designs), and plotted.
#
# How to report these numbers, depending on config evaluation.nested:
#   nested = TRUE  – feature selection and tuning were repeated inside every
#                    fold on its training part, so each held-out group was
#                    genuinely unseen by everything that learned from data:
#                    these are honest nested-resampling estimates.
#   nested = FALSE – selection and tuning ran once on task_train, which
#                    includes every group; only the fold's model fit excluded
#                    the held-out group. Mildly optimistic. Either way, the
#                    external test set is the evaluation no part of the
#                    pipeline ever saw.
if ("group" %in% names(tab)) {
  lodo_metrics <- fold_metrics %>%
    rename(heldout_dataset = heldout_group) %>%
    relocate(method, heldout_dataset, n_test, class_counts) %>%
    arrange(method, heldout_dataset)

  # "LODO" is literally true only when a fold holds out one group. With
  # outer: cv + dataset.group a fold holds out several, so heading, title and
  # axis follow the strategy that was actually configured.
  is_lodo    <- eval_outer == "lodo"
  group_unit <- if (is_lodo) "datasets" else "groups"
  fold_axis  <- if (is_lodo) "Held-out dataset" else "Held-out groups (per fold)"
  fold_title <- if (is_lodo) "LODO: balanced accuracy per held-out dataset"
                else sprintf("Balanced accuracy per outer fold (%s grouped by '%s')", eval_outer, group_col)
  heading    <- if (is_lodo) "LODO performance per held-out dataset:"
                else sprintf("Outer-fold performance per held-out group of '%s':", group_col)

  cat("\n", heading, "\n", sep = "")
  print(lodo_metrics %>% select(-learner_id, -task_id, -resampling_id, -iteration))
  readr::write_csv(lodo_metrics, file.path(metrics_dir, "lodo_metrics.csv"))
```
