```{r benchmarking, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
  # One panel per method: balanced accuracy per held-out group, with the
  # across-group mean as a dashed reference line. The spread across groups is
  # the honest picture of transferability that a single averaged number hides.
  #
  # Two things the raw table cannot be plotted with (both shared with the
  # multi-level wrapper, hence the helpers):
  #   shorten_heldout_label() – a grouped fold is labelled with every group in
  #     it, joined by ";", which runs to a couple of hundred characters and
  #     leaves no canvas for the bars; it becomes "fold i (k groups)" and the
  #     full membership stays in lodo_metrics.csv.
  #   lodo_chance_level()     – balanced accuracy averages the per-class
  #     recalls, so guessing scores 1 / number of classes: 0.5 only when the
  #     target is binary, and much lower on a multi-class one. Read off the
  #     class_counts column written above, not hard-coded.
  chance <- lodo_chance_level(lodo_metrics)
  lodo_plot_df <- lodo_metrics %>%
    mutate(heldout_dataset = shorten_heldout_label(heldout_dataset, iteration)) %>%
    mutate(heldout_dataset = reorder(heldout_dataset, `balanced accuracy`))
  lodo_means <- lodo_plot_df %>%
    group_by(method) %>%
    summarise(mean_bacc = mean(`balanced accuracy`, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  lodo_plot <- ggplot(lodo_plot_df, aes(x = heldout_dataset, y = `balanced accuracy`)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue4", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("n=%d", n_test)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
    geom_hline(data = lodo_means, aes(yintercept = mean_bacc),
               linetype = "dashed", color = "tomato3") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = chance, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
    facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 1) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
    labs(
      title = fold_title,
      subtitle = paste(
        sprintf("Dashed red = mean across %s; dotted grey = chance (%.2f).", group_unit, chance),
        if (eval_nested) "Nested: feature selection and tuning repeated inside every fold."
        else sprintf("Internal estimates: feature selection and tuning used all %s.", group_unit)
      ),
      x = fold_axis, y = "Balanced accuracy"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  show_and_save_figure(lodo_plot, "per_group_balanced_accuracy", save_dir)
}

# Side-by-side bars per method for accuracy, balanced accuracy and logloss
# (from bench_df above), with custom colors.
bench_long <- bench_df %>%
  select(method, accuracy, `balanced accuracy`, logloss) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(accuracy, `balanced accuracy`, logloss), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value")

# Define the color palette
metric_colors <- c("accuracy" = "skyblue3", "balanced accuracy" = "dodgerblue3", "logloss" = "tomato3")

ggplot(bench_long, aes(x = method, y = value, fill = measure)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metric_colors) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
            vjust = 1.5, 
            color = "white", 
            size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Model performance measures",
       x = "Method",
       y = "Value") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# Pick the best model from the benchmark (training CV), not from the test split:
# choosing the winner on the same data whose score you report inflates it. Sort
# by balanced accuracy (desc), ties broken by logloss (asc). best_model_id pulls
# this model's cross-validated predictions below and drives the importance/SHAP
# chunk; best_method only labels the prediction plots. Prediction and External
# Test score every learner in learners_best, not just this one.
best_row <- bench_df %>%
  arrange(desc(`balanced accuracy`), logloss) %>%
  slice(1)

best_model_id <- best_row$learner_id
best_method <- best_row$method

# Say the outcome plainly in the report, so nobody has to reconstruct the
# winner from the table: this is the model every later section uses.
cat(sprintf(
  "\n>>> Best model by balanced accuracy: %s (%.3f). This model is used for the prediction overview and the SHAP analysis; the external test set is scored with every tuned model.\n",
  best_method, best_row$`balanced accuracy`
))

# Take the best model's fold-wise predictions and average the predicted
# probabilities across folds, so each sample ends with one score however often
# it was in a test fold. With plain CV or LODO a sample is tested exactly once,
# so that average is its single out-of-fold prediction; averaging only matters
# for repeated CV.
pred_dt <- outer_results
best_preds <- pred_dt[str_detect(learner_id, best_model_id)]

# best_preds$prediction is a table column whose cells each hold one whole
# mlr3 prediction object (one per fold). Expand it into a flat tibble with
# one row per (fold × sample) combination.
all_preds <- best_preds$prediction %>%
  map_dfr(~ as.data.table(.x) %>% as_tibble())

# Detect probability columns (one per class, named "prob.<classname>")
prob_cols <- grep("^prob\\.", names(all_preds), value = TRUE)

# One row per sample. Without the class-prior correction the label is decided
# again from the fold-averaged probabilities (threshold 0.5, or the largest
# mean probability). With it, each sample keeps the label its fold decided under
# that rule - the one oof_predictions.csv and the per-class table use - so this
# overview agrees with them; under plain cross-validation a sample has exactly one
# fold. prob_positive is kept either way for the Platt calibration below.
# Binary: average P(positive class) across folds.
if (length(prob_cols) == 2) {
  positive_col <- paste0("prob.", positive_class)
  avg_preds <- all_preds %>%
    group_by(row_ids) %>%
    summarise(
      prob_positive = mean(.data[[positive_col]]),
      truth = first(truth),
      fold_response = names(which.max(table(as.character(response)))),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      response = if (eval_prior_correction) fold_response else
        if_else(prob_positive >= 0.5, positive_class, setdiff(levels(truth), positive_class)),
      response = factor(response, levels = levels(truth)),
      correct = response == truth
    )
} else {
  # Multiclass: take the class with the highest mean predicted probability across folds.
  avg_preds <- all_preds %>%
    group_by(row_ids) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_response = sub("prob\\.", "", names(which.max(colMeans(across(all_of(prob_cols)))))),
      fold_response = names(which.max(table(as.character(response)))),
      truth = first(truth),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      response = if (eval_prior_correction) fold_response else mean_response,
      response = factor(response, levels = levels(truth)),
      correct = response == truth
    )
}

# One prediction per training sample: the one it received in the round where
# it was held out, so the model that made it never saw that sample ("out-of-
# fold"). The sample name is restored from sample_lookup (the task only knows
# integer row ids). Useful for asking which samples or studies the best model
# gets wrong.
readr::write_csv(
  dplyr::left_join(avg_preds, sample_lookup, by = c("row_ids" = "row_id")),
  file.path(metrics_dir, "predictions.csv")
)

# ── Out-of-fold prediction set, every method ──────────────────────────────────
# The outer folds pooled (pool_outer_predictions): every training sample
# predicted by a model that never saw it, for every method, summarised like the
# internal and external test sets (summarise_prediction_set,
# R/tabflux_prediction_helpers.R). No bootstrap — the fold spread above already
# carries the uncertainty. Under LODO the per-group table is lodo_metrics.csv
# seen from the sample side.
# Output: oof_predictions.csv, one row per predicted sample x method, with
# sample name, group, truth, response, probabilities and right/wrong.
oof_preds <- list()
for (m in names(methods)) {
  if (m %in% outer_results$learner_id) oof_preds[[m]] <- pool_outer_predictions(outer_results, m)
}
oof_summary <- summarise_prediction_set(
  oof_preds, measures = bmr_measures, sample_lookup = sample_lookup, group_lookup = group_lookup,
  n_boot = 0, task = task_train, positive_class = positive_class,
  fairness_active = fairness_active, pta_lookup = pta_lookup
)
readr::write_csv(oof_summary$samples, file.path(metrics_dir, "oof_predictions.csv"))

# Per-class recall: which classes each method actually gets, and what it calls
# them instead. Balanced accuracy is the mean of this column, so this table is
# the benchmark number taken apart - worth reading whenever the classes are
# unequal, where a method can score well on plain accuracy by answering with
# the majority class and never predicting the rarest one at all.
if (!is.null(oof_summary$by_class)) {
  cat("\nPer-class recall, pooled out-of-fold predictions:\n")
  print(oof_summary$by_class, row.names = FALSE)
  readr::write_csv(oof_summary$by_class, file.path(metrics_dir, "per_class_recall_oof.csv"))
}

show_and_save_figure(
  plot_prediction_by_class(oof_summary$samples, class_levels = levels(task_train$truth()),
                           title = "Out-of-fold predictions by class and method"),
  "out_of_fold_by_class", save_dir)

# ROC curves (binary tasks): one grey line per outer fold, the pooled folds
# in colour, one panel per method. The fan of grey lines is the fold-to-fold
# spread of the ranking quality; under LODO each line is one group.
if (dataset_attr == "binary") {
  roc_df <- bind_rows(lapply(names(oof_preds), function(m) {
    d <- roc_curves_by_fold(outer_results, m, positive_class)
    d$method <- recode_method_labels(m)
    d
  }))
  print(
    ggplot() +
      geom_path(data = roc_df %>% filter(fold != "pooled"), aes(fpr, tpr, group = fold),
                colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_path(data = roc_df %>% filter(fold == "pooled"), aes(fpr, tpr),
                colour = "dodgerblue4", linewidth = 1.1) +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
      facet_wrap(~method) +
      coord_equal() +
      labs(title = "ROC per outer fold (grey) and pooled (blue)",
           x = "False positive rate", y = "True positive rate") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  )
}

# ── Probability calibration (binary tasks) ─────────────────────────────────────
# The out-of-fold probabilities above come from models that never saw the
# sample's fold, so they are legitimate material for learning a probability
# correction without touching a test set. Platt scaling fits a two-parameter
# S-curve (shift + squeeze) mapping the model's probability to the observed
# frequency of the positive class. The parameters are saved next to the models
# (calibration.json) and applied to the external test set. AUC is unaffected
# (the map is monotone); only the meaning of the 0.5 threshold changes.
platt_cal <- NULL
if (calibration == "platt" && dataset_attr == "binary") {
  cal_p <- pmin(pmax(avg_preds$prob_positive, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  cal_fit <- stats::glm((avg_preds$truth == positive_class) ~ stats::qlogis(cal_p),
                        family = stats::binomial)
  platt_cal <- list(
    intercept = unname(coef(cal_fit)[1]),
    slope = unname(coef(cal_fit)[2])
  )
  # The cut a calibrated probability is compared with: 0.5, or with the
  # class-prior correction the positive class's training frequency (the same
  # rule the raw labels use). raw_threshold is the raw-scale probability at
  # which the calibrated value crosses that cut.
  platt_cal$cut <- if (eval_prior_correction) mean(task_train$truth() == positive_class) else 0.5
  platt_cal$raw_threshold <- stats::plogis((stats::qlogis(platt_cal$cut) - platt_cal$intercept) / platt_cal$slope)
  jsonlite::write_json(
    c(platt_cal, list(model = best_model_id, positive_class = positive_class,
                      fitted_on = "out-of-fold benchmark predictions", n = nrow(avg_preds))),
    file.path(save_dir, "calibration.json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE
  )
  cat(sprintf(
    "\nPlatt calibration (%s, %d out-of-fold samples): intercept %.3f, slope %.3f; decision cut %.3f, raw-scale threshold %.3f.\n",
    best_method, nrow(avg_preds), platt_cal$intercept, platt_cal$slope, platt_cal$cut, platt_cal$raw_threshold
  ))
}

# Calibration curve of the best model's out-of-fold probabilities: predicted
# probability (binned) against the observed positive fraction. On the diagonal
# = calibrated; the dashed line is the Platt correction fitted above, i.e.
# where the same probabilities land after calibration.
if (dataset_attr == "binary" && best_model_id %in% names(oof_preds)) {
  cal_df <- calibration_curve_points(oof_preds[[best_model_id]], positive_class, bins = 10)
  cal_plot <- ggplot(cal_df, aes(x = p_mean, y = obs_frac)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
    geom_line(colour = "dodgerblue4") +
    geom_point(aes(size = n), colour = "dodgerblue4") +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Calibration of out-of-fold P(%s) - %s", positive_class, best_method),
         x = sprintf("Mean predicted P(%s) in bin", positive_class),
         y = sprintf("Observed fraction of %s", positive_class), size = "Samples") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  if (!is.null(platt_cal)) {
    platt_line <- data.frame(p = seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01))
    platt_line$cal <- stats::plogis(platt_cal$intercept + platt_cal$slope * stats::qlogis(platt_line$p))
    cal_plot <- cal_plot + geom_line(data = platt_line, aes(x = p, y = cal),
                                     linetype = "dashed", colour = "tomato3")
  }
  show_and_save_figure(cal_plot, "calibration_curve", save_dir)
}

# Per-class tally of the best model's out-of-fold predictions (right / wrong /
# accuracy), printed for the record. Not used by later chunks: the plots below
# are built from pred_summary instead.
class_errors <- avg_preds %>%
  group_by(truth) %>%
  summarise(
    correct = sum(correct),
    incorrect = n() - sum(correct),
    accuracy = round(mean(correct), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
cat("\nOut-of-fold accuracy per true class (best benchmark model):\n")
print(class_errors)

# Prepare a count + proportion table used by all three prediction plots below.
pred_summary <- avg_preds %>%
  group_by(truth, correct) %>%
  summarise(N = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(truth) %>%
  mutate(prop = N / sum(N)) %>%
  ungroup()

# p1: stacked bar of absolute correct/incorrect counts per true class
p1 <- ggplot(pred_summary, aes(x = truth, y = N, fill = correct, label = N)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  geom_text(position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "dodgerblue3", "FALSE" = "red3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Absolute Counts", x = "True Class", y = "Count", fill = "Correct") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# p2: proportion correct/incorrect — useful when class sizes differ
p2 <- ggplot(pred_summary, aes(x = truth, y = prop, fill = correct, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", prop * 100))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
  geom_text(position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "dodgerblue3", "FALSE" = "red3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Proportion Correct", x = "True Class", y = "Proportion", fill = "Correct") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# p3: true vs predicted class, one point per sample, nudged randomly so
# overlapping samples can be seen — shows confusion patterns at sample level
p3 <- ggplot(avg_preds, aes(x = truth, y = response, color = correct)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.4, width = 0.25, height = 0.25) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "dodgerblue3", "FALSE" = "red3")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "True vs Predicted", x = "True Class", y = "Predicted Class", color = "Correct") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
  )

# Side by side (patchwork): counts, proportions and confusion jitter for the
# best model's cross-validated predictions.
(p1 + p2 + p3) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = paste("Prediction Overview –", best_method),
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
  )
```

#### Prediction

Scores every tuned model on the internal test set reserved in Define Task — samples no model, no feature selection and no tuning has seen. Each method gets the benchmark's metric table, a bootstrap 95 % interval (a test set has no folds, so its samples are resampled instead), a per-group table where groups exist, and a right/wrong-per-class figure. Skipped with `test_split: 0`.

```{r prediction, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Internal test set: score every tuned model on task_test.
# Input: task_test (reserved in the Define Task chunk; NULL when
# evaluation.test_split = 0) and the fitted learners from the Benchmark chunk
# (learners_best), trained on task_train only, so every test sample is new.
# Output: pred_df, one row per method with bench_df's metric columns, read by
# the Performance Comparison plots and the Save Metrics export; pred_ci, the
# bootstrap interval per method x metric; and in metrics_dir
# test_predictions.csv (per sample) and test_metrics_by_group.csv (per group,
# when there is one). All from summarise_prediction_set()
# (R/tabflux_prediction_helpers.R), which also summarises the out-of-fold and
# external sets, so the three tables line up column by column.
pred_df <- NULL
pred_ci <- NULL
test_summary <- NULL
n_boot <- 1000L   # bootstrap resamples for the test-set intervals (enough for a 95 % interval)

if (is.null(task_test)) {
  message(
    "No internal test set (evaluation.test_split = 0): skipping held-out prediction. ",
    "See the outer-fold metrics and, if configured, the external test set."
  )
} else {
# Everything from here to the closing brace at the end of the chunk runs only
# when an internal test set exists (task_test is not NULL). The code inside
# is deliberately not indented, so it reads like the rest of the notebook.

# One mlr3 prediction per method. For each: take the fitted learner from
# learners_best (rebuilt by the Benchmark chunk from memory or from the .rds
# files); if it is missing there, load the tuned learner the Train models
# chunk saved and refit it on task_train (a saved TabPFN carries no live
# model). Then predict the reserved samples.
predictions <- list()
for (method in names(methods)) {
  best_model <- learners_best[[method]]
  if (is.null(best_model)) {
    path <- file.path(save_dir, paste0(method, "_tuned_learner.rds"))
    if (!file.exists(path)) {
      cat("SKIP:", method, "- no tuned learner found in memory or disk\n")
      next
    }
    best_model <- readRDS(path)
    if ("unmarshal" %in% names(best_model)) try(best_model$unmarshal(), silent = TRUE)
    best_model$train(task_train)
  }
  predictions[[method]] <- best_model$predict(task_test)
  if (eval_prior_correction) predictions[[method]] <- apply_prior_correction(predictions[[method]], task_train$truth())
}

# Summarise the prediction set: metrics + bootstrap interval, per-sample
# table, per-group table. group_lookup / pta_lookup are keyed by task row id,
# which the reserved samples kept, so groups and PTA groups resolve directly.
test_summary <- summarise_prediction_set(
  predictions, measures = bmr_measures, sample_lookup = sample_lookup, group_lookup = group_lookup,
  n_boot = n_boot, seed = seed, task = task_test, positive_class = positive_class,
  fairness_active = fairness_active, pta_lookup = pta_lookup
)
# pred_df keeps exactly bench_df's columns (same order) so the comparison and
# export chunks can put the two side by side; the sample count is printed.
pred_df <- test_summary$metrics[, intersect(names(bench_df), names(test_summary$metrics))]
pred_ci <- test_summary$ci
cat(sprintf("\nInternal test set: %d samples\n", task_test$nrow))
print(pred_df %>% select(-learner_id))
cat("\nBootstrap 95 % intervals (balanced accuracy, AUC):\n")
print(pred_ci %>% filter(metric %in% c("balanced accuracy", "auc")) %>%
        select(method, metric, estimate, ci_low, ci_high))

# Right / wrong tally per method, then the per-sample export.
print(test_summary$samples %>% count(method, match) %>%
        group_by(method) %>% mutate(ratio = round(n / sum(n), 2)) %>% ungroup())
readr::write_csv(test_summary$samples, file.path(metrics_dir, "test_predictions.csv"))

# Per-group table (whole groups were reserved under LODO): the internal
# counterpart of the LODO table and of the external per-group table.
if (!is.null(test_summary$by_group)) {
  cat("\nInternal test metrics per group:\n")
  print(test_summary$by_group %>% select(method, group, n, `balanced accuracy`, any_of("auc")))
  readr::write_csv(test_summary$by_group, file.path(metrics_dir, "test_metrics_by_group.csv"))
}

# Per-class recall on the reserved samples, in the same shape as the
# out-of-fold table above, so the two can be read side by side.
if (!is.null(test_summary$by_class)) {
  cat("\nPer-class recall, internal test set:\n")
  print(test_summary$by_class, row.names = FALSE)
  readr::write_csv(test_summary$by_class, file.path(metrics_dir, "per_class_recall_test.csv"))
}

show_and_save_figure(
  plot_prediction_by_class(test_summary$samples, class_levels = task_test$class_names,
                           title = "Internal test predictions by class and method"),
  "internal_test_by_class", save_dir)

}  # end of the if-block skipped when there is no internal test set (task_test NULL)
```

#### Performance Comparison

Benchmark scores (mean over the outer folds, bar of one SD across them) against internal test scores (bar of the bootstrap interval), drawn as dumbbells, one pair per metric and method. A short segment means the model behaves on reserved samples as it did in resampling; a long one with the test point to the left is optimism, or a shift between the two populations. Skipped when there is no internal test set.

```{r performance comparison, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Dumbbells: benchmark (outer-fold mean +/- SD) vs internal test (bootstrap
# interval), per metric and method. Input: bench_df and bench_spread
# (Benchmark chunk), pred_df and pred_ci (Prediction chunk). Output: two
# figures for the report; the numbers are exported by the Save Metrics chunk.
# Skipped when there is no internal test set (pred_df NULL).
if (is.null(pred_df)) {
  message("No internal test metrics: skipping the benchmark-vs-test comparison plots.")
} else {
  dumbbells <- plot_dumbbell(bench_df, bench_spread, pred_df, pred_ci, test_label = "Internal test")
  print(dumbbells$by_method)
  print(dumbbells$by_metric)
}
```

#### Save Metrics

Writes this level's numbers to `metrics/`: the benchmark table, the internal test table when there is one, and a wide and a long version stamped with level, target and sample/feature counts. The long version carries the fold spread for the benchmark rows and the bootstrap interval for the test rows, and is the file `scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R` collects from every level.

```{r save metrics, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Export the performance tables of this run to metrics_dir
# (<save_dir>/metrics, set in the Set Parameters chunk).
# Input: bench_df + bench_spread (Benchmark chunk, outer-fold scores and
# their SD) and pred_df + pred_ci (Prediction chunk, internal test scores and
# bootstrap intervals; NULL when evaluation.test_split = 0).
# Output: benchmark_metrics.csv, test_metrics.csv, performance_metrics_wide/
# long.csv and one .rds bundle. performance_metrics_long.csv is the file
# scripts/run_multi_tax_levels.R reads from every taxonomic-level run to build
# the cross-level comparison; the other files are for manual inspection.
dir.create(metrics_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Tag each frame with a data_split label before stacking. pred_df is NULL when
# no internal test set was reserved; the export then carries the outer-fold
# scores only.
train_metrics_wide <- bench_df %>%
  mutate(data_split = "train_benchmark")   # cross-validated training scores

if (!is.null(pred_df)) {
  # Identify metric columns that exist in both the benchmark and prediction
  # frames (excludes identifiers like "method" and "learner_id").
  metric_cols <- setdiff(intersect(names(bench_df), names(pred_df)), c("method", "learner_id"))
  test_metrics_wide <- pred_df %>%
    mutate(data_split = "test_prediction")   # held-out test scores
} else {
  metric_cols <- setdiff(names(bench_df), c("method", "learner_id"))
  test_metrics_wide <- NULL
}

# Combine train and test rows, then attach run metadata (tax level, target,
# sample/feature counts) so the exported file is self-contained. tax_level
# (feature_level, the display label built in the Import Data chunk) and
# tax_level_key (tax_level_slug, the file-safe version from the Set Parameters
# chunk) are what tell the levels apart once run_multi_tax_levels.R stacks
# the files.
performance_metrics_wide <- bind_rows(train_metrics_wide, test_metrics_wide) %>%
  mutate(
    tax_level     = feature_level,
    tax_level_key = tax_level_slug,
    # target = the NAME of the metadata column being predicted (config
    # dataset.target), not a class label; it lets
    # run_multi_tax_levels.R tell apart runs on different targets. The table
    # has no column called target, so dplyr picks up the global variable.
    target        = target,
    # Use the appropriate task's row/feature count for each split
    n_samples = if_else(
      data_split == "train_benchmark",
      as.integer(task_train$nrow),
      as.integer(if (!is.null(task_test)) task_test$nrow else NA_integer_)
    ),
    n_features = if_else(
      data_split == "train_benchmark",
      as.integer(length(task_train$feature_names)),
      as.integer(if (!is.null(task_test)) length(task_test$feature_names) else NA_integer_)
    )
  ) %>%
  relocate(tax_level, tax_level_key, data_split, target, n_samples, n_features, method, learner_id)

# Long format: one row per (method × split × metric) — easier to filter/plot in
# downstream scripts. Uncertainty travels with it: sd = SD across the outer
# folds (benchmark rows only), ci_low / ci_high = bootstrap 95 % interval
# (test rows only); the other cells are NA.
performance_metrics_long <- performance_metrics_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(metric_cols), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  left_join(bench_spread %>% mutate(data_split = "train_benchmark") %>% select(method, metric, data_split, sd),
            by = c("method", "metric", "data_split"))
if (!is.null(pred_ci)) {
  performance_metrics_long <- performance_metrics_long %>%
    left_join(pred_ci %>% mutate(data_split = "test_prediction") %>% select(method, metric, data_split, ci_low, ci_high),
              by = c("method", "metric", "data_split"))
} else {
  performance_metrics_long$ci_low <- NA_real_
  performance_metrics_long$ci_high <- NA_real_
}

# Export everything: two summary CSVs, combined wide + long CSVs, and an RDS bundle
# so the whole thing can be loaded in one readRDS() call later.
readr::write_csv(bench_df, file.path(metrics_dir, "benchmark_metrics.csv"))
if (!is.null(pred_df)) {
  readr::write_csv(pred_df, file.path(metrics_dir, "test_metrics.csv"))
}
readr::write_csv(performance_metrics_wide, file.path(metrics_dir, "performance_metrics_wide.csv"))
readr::write_csv(performance_metrics_long, file.path(metrics_dir, "performance_metrics_long.csv"))
saveRDS(
  list(
    benchmark_metrics        = bench_df,
    benchmark_spread         = bench_spread,
    test_metrics             = pred_df,   # NULL when no internal test set exists
    test_metrics_ci          = pred_ci,
    performance_metrics_wide = performance_metrics_wide,
    performance_metrics_long = performance_metrics_long
  ),
  file.path(metrics_dir, "performance_metrics.rds")
)

message("Saved metric exports to: ", metrics_dir)
print(performance_metrics_wide)
```

#### External Test Set

Pushes an independent dataset (`input.test_*`) through the trained models. Its counts are aggregated, aligned to the training feature space and normalised with the training settings, so only the biology differs. Every sample gets a quality line — how much of its community the model knows — and, unless none of its reads fall in the taxa the model was trained on, class probabilities. Metrics cover only samples whose label is one of the training classes, overall and per `test_group`. Skipped when no external counts file is configured.

```{r external test, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Predict an independent dataset with every tuned model.
# Input: the three external files from the config (test_counts_path,
# test_taxa_path, test_meta_path, plus test_group for per-group metrics) and the
# fitted learners in learners_best (Benchmark chunk).
# Output: external_predictions.csv, external_test_metrics.csv and
# external_test_metrics_by_group.csv in metrics_dir, plus two figures.
#
# Every sample with at least one read in the model's reference taxa gets a
# prediction; those with none get a QC row and empty predictions (step 3).
# Metrics use only samples labelled with one of the model's classes, so
# controls and extra conditions pass through with probabilities and QC without
# distorting them.
#
# The test data is prepared exactly like the training data:
#   1. aggregate to the same taxonomic rank (same build_feature_matrix code)
#   2. align to the training feature space — features the model knows but the
#      test set lacks become zeros; features the model never saw are dropped
#      and counted (the QC signal for "how foreign is this data?")
#   3. normalize with the same method and pseudocount — per sample, reusing no
#      parameter learned from the training data
#   4. subset to the model's selected features and predict
# The order matters: normalization divides a sample's counts by its read total
# (TSS = total-sum scaling), and CLR also subtracts its mean log-abundance.
# Aligning first computes both over the training taxa; normalizing before
# subsetting keeps them independent of which features survived selection.
if (!external_test_configured) {
  message("No external test set configured (input.test_counts_path is empty); skipping.")
} else {

# ── 1. Read and aggregate ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Same file layout as the training input (Import Data chunk): a counts table
# with features as rows, first column = feature ID, one column per sample; an
# optional taxonomy table keyed by the same feature IDs; a metadata table
# keyed by sample name. build_feature_matrix() (Import Data chunk) turns the
# counts into a samples x features matrix aggregated to the modelled rank,
# exactly as it did for the training data.
ext_counts_dt <- fread(test_counts_path, check.names = FALSE, showProgress = FALSE, integer64 = "double")
ext_counts_df <- as.data.frame(ext_counts_dt)
ext_feature_ids <- make.unique(as.character(ext_counts_df[[1]]))
ext_counts_df[[1]] <- NULL
rownames(ext_counts_df) <- ext_feature_ids

# Taxonomy table: needed to aggregate to a rank (and, at ASV level, for the
# sequence column that makes IDs comparable across datasets). Its rows are
# reordered to match the counts so the two tables line up feature by feature.
ext_taxa_df <- NULL
if (nzchar(test_taxa_path)) {
  ext_taxa_df <- as.data.frame(fread(test_taxa_path, check.names = FALSE, showProgress = FALSE))
  ext_match <- match(ext_feature_ids, make.unique(as.character(ext_taxa_df[[1]])))
  if (anyNA(ext_match)) {
    stop(sprintf("%d external test feature(s) missing from '%s'.",
                 sum(is.na(ext_match)), basename(test_taxa_path)))
  }
  ext_taxa_df <- ext_taxa_df[ext_match, , drop = FALSE]
}

# At ASV level, cross-dataset feature identity only exists through sequences
# (arbitrary IDs are dataset-local, and the hash IDs derive from sequences).
if (!aggregate_requested) {
  ext_has_seq <- !is.null(ext_taxa_df) &&
    any(tolower(names(ext_taxa_df)) == "sequence")
  train_ids_hashed <- all(grepl("^ASV_[0-9a-f]{12}$", feature_name_map$feature_original))
  if (!ext_has_seq || !train_ids_hashed) {
    stop(
      "External test prediction at ASV level needs sequence-based feature IDs ",
      "on BOTH sides (a 'sequence' column in both taxon tables). Without them, ",
      "IDs like 'ASV_12' name different organisms in each dataset and any join ",
      "would silently match unrelated features. Aggregate to a taxonomic rank, ",
      "or provide the sequences."
    )
  }
}

ext_matrix <- build_feature_matrix(
  feature_counts = ext_counts_df,
  feature_ids = ext_feature_ids,
  taxa_info = ext_taxa_df,
  label = "External test"
)

# ── 2. Align to the training feature space ────────────────────────────────────
# The reference is the full list of taxa the model was trained on, before
# feature selection: norm_feat_cols, every feature column the training table
# still had when it was normalized (also written to reference_features.csv).
# Those are sanitized model names, while the external matrix carries original
# taxon names, so translate through feature_name_map (Import Data chunk) before
# matching. align_features_to_reference() (R/tabflux_data_helpers.R) returns the
# aligned matrix plus the read bookkeeping for the QC table below.
reference_map <- feature_name_map[feature_name_map$feature_model %in% norm_feat_cols, ]
alignment <- align_features_to_reference(ext_matrix, reference_map$feature_original)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nExternal test set: %d samples, %d features at the '%s' level.\n",
  nrow(ext_matrix), ncol(ext_matrix), feature_level
))
cat(sprintf(
  "Feature alignment: %d shared with training, %d novel (dropped), %d unseen here (zero-filled).\n",
  ncol(ext_matrix) - length(alignment$novel_features),
  length(alignment$novel_features),
  length(alignment$missing_features)
))

ext_aligned <- alignment$data
# Original names -> the model's sanitized feature names (same order as the reference).
colnames(ext_aligned) <- reference_map$feature_model

# ── 3. QC per sample, then normalize ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Reads here are counted at the modeled rank (reads lost to "unassigned at this
# rank" are already gone, exactly as for the training data).
ext_qc <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(ext_aligned),
  reads_at_rank = alignment$reads_total,
  reads_in_reference = alignment$reads_covered,
  pct_reads_in_reference = round(alignment$pct_reads_covered, 1),
  # Depth far below anything seen in training makes a prediction unreliable
  # however the numbers are scaled, so flag it. Measured on the reads the model
  # can use (inside the reference feature space): a sample full of novel taxa
  # would otherwise look deep enough while the model sees almost none of it.
  # library_sizes = training per-sample read totals (Normalize Abundances
  # chunk), so the threshold is the shallowest training sample.
  below_training_min_depth = alignment$reads_covered < min(library_sizes),
  row.names = NULL
)

# Samples with no reads in the model's reference taxa (reads_in_reference = 0)
# cannot be normalized or predicted: their aligned row is all zeros. Two cases
# end here: no reads at this rank at all, or reads only in taxa the model never
# saw (dropped in step 2). Checking reads_in_reference covers both; checking
# reads_at_rank would let the second case through to normalize_abundance(),
# which then stops the whole chunk. These samples are left out of the
# normalization below and stay in the QC/prediction export with empty
# predictions rather than vanishing.
ext_empty <- ext_qc$Sample[ext_qc$reads_in_reference == 0]
if (length(ext_empty)) {
  message("External sample(s) with no reads in the model's reference taxa ",
          "(none at this rank, or only taxa the model never saw); no prediction possible: ",
          paste(ext_empty, collapse = ", "))
}
ext_usable <- setdiff(rownames(ext_aligned), ext_empty)
ext_norm <- normalize_abundance(
  ext_aligned[ext_usable, , drop = FALSE],
  method = normalization,
  pseudocount = pseudocount
)$data

# ── 4. Metadata: labels and grouping are both optional ────────────────────────
ext_meta_dt <- fread(test_meta_path, check.names = FALSE, showProgress = FALSE)
ext_meta <- as.data.frame(ext_meta_dt)
rownames(ext_meta) <- make.unique(as.character(ext_meta[[1]]))

meta_missing <- setdiff(rownames(ext_aligned), rownames(ext_meta))
if (length(meta_missing)) {
  message("External sample(s) without metadata row: ", paste(meta_missing, collapse = ", "))
}

# Labels are optional: with a target column in the external metadata we can
# score, without it we only predict. class_levels = the training classes
# (tab$target, Define Task chunk); only labels found in this set are
# scoreable, everything else (controls, extra treatments) is prediction-only.
class_levels <- levels(tab$target)
ext_label <- if (target %in% names(ext_meta)) {
  as.character(ext_meta[rownames(ext_aligned), target])
} else {
  message(sprintf("No '%s' column in the external metadata: predictions only, no metrics.", target))
  rep(NA_character_, nrow(ext_aligned))
}
ext_group <- if (nzchar(test_group) && test_group %in% names(ext_meta)) {
  as.character(ext_meta[rownames(ext_aligned), test_group])
} else {
  if (nzchar(test_group)) {
    # A typo here would otherwise just silently produce no per-group output.
    warning(sprintf(
      "input.test_group is '%s' but the external metadata has no such column (available: %s). Per-group metrics are skipped.",
      test_group, paste(names(ext_meta), collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
  rep(NA_character_, nrow(ext_aligned))
}

# Scoreable = the label is one of the classes the model can predict.
ext_info <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(ext_aligned),
  group = ext_group,
  label = ext_label,
  scoreable = !is.na(ext_label) & ext_label %in% class_levels &
    rownames(ext_aligned) %in% ext_usable,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
cat(sprintf(
  "\nSamples: %d total | %d scoreable (label in {%s}) | %d prediction-only\n",
  nrow(ext_info), sum(ext_info$scoreable), paste(class_levels, collapse = ", "),
  sum(!ext_info$scoreable)
))

# ── 5. Predict with every tuned model ─────────────────────────────────────────
external_predictions <- list()
external_metrics <- list()
external_group_metrics <- list()
external_ci <- list()

for (method in names(learners_best)) {
  model <- learners_best[[method]]

  # Probabilities for every usable sample, labeled or not. predict_newdata()
  # runs the full trained pipeline (imputation, scaling, ...) with the values
  # learned on the training data — which columns were kept, the means and
  # standard deviations used for scaling — not values recomputed here.
  # task_train$feature_names = the features that survived selection; ext_norm
  # still holds the full reference list, so subset now, after normalization
  # (see the chunk header for why the order matters).
  newdata <- ext_norm[, task_train$feature_names, drop = FALSE]
  # task = task_train hands mlr3 the training task's column types, class
  # levels and positive class, so the external rows (a plain data frame with
  # no target column) are interpreted exactly like training rows.
  pred_all <- model$predict_newdata(newdata, task = task_train)
  if (eval_prior_correction) pred_all <- apply_prior_correction(pred_all, task_train$truth())
  prob_df <- as.data.frame(pred_all$prob)
  names(prob_df) <- paste0("prob_", names(prob_df))

  # check.names = FALSE keeps the "prob_<class>" column names exactly as
  # built: the default would run them through make.names(), and a class label
  # with a space or hyphen would then no longer match positive_prob_col below.
  external_predictions[[method]] <- data.frame(
    method = method,
    Sample = rownames(newdata),
    response = as.character(pred_all$response),
    prob_df,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  # Metrics on the scoreable subset only, via a proper task so the same
  # scoring helpers as everywhere else apply.
  score_ids <- ext_info$Sample[ext_info$scoreable]
  if (length(score_ids) >= 2) {
    score_tab <- ext_norm[score_ids, task_train$feature_names, drop = FALSE]
    score_tab$target <- factor(ext_info$label[match(score_ids, ext_info$Sample)],
                               levels = class_levels)
    ext_task <- mlr3::as_task_classif(score_tab, target = "target")
    if (dataset_attr == "binary" && positive_class %in% class_levels) {
      ext_task$positive <- positive_class
    }
    pred_scored <- model$predict(ext_task)
    if (eval_prior_correction) pred_scored <- apply_prior_correction(pred_scored, task_train$truth())
    external_metrics[[method]] <- score_prediction_metrics(
      pred_scored, measures = bmr_measures
    ) %>% mutate(method = method, n = length(score_ids))
    # Bootstrap 95 % interval per metric (the external set has no folds):
    # resample its scoreable samples and rescore; see
    # bootstrap_prediction_metrics() in R/tabflux_prediction_helpers.R.
    external_ci[[method]] <- bootstrap_prediction_metrics(
      pred_scored, measures = bmr_measures, n_boot = 1000L, seed = seed
    ) %>% mutate(learner_id = method, method = recode_method_labels(method),
                 metric = label_measure_name(metric))

    # Per-group breakdown (e.g. per site or study): the external counterpart
    # of the LODO per-dataset table.
    score_groups <- ext_info$group[match(score_ids, ext_info$Sample)]
    for (g in sort(unique(stats::na.omit(score_groups)))) {
      g_rows <- which(score_groups == g)
      if (length(g_rows) < 2) next   # a single sample cannot support a metric
      g_pred <- model$predict(ext_task$clone(deep = TRUE)$filter(ext_task$row_ids[g_rows]))
      if (eval_prior_correction) g_pred <- apply_prior_correction(g_pred, task_train$truth())
      external_group_metrics[[paste(method, g)]] <- score_prediction_metrics(
        g_pred, measures = bmr_measures
      ) %>% mutate(method = method, group = g, n = length(g_rows))
    }
  }
}

# ── 6. Exports ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One row per predicted sample x method, with label, QC, and probabilities
# side by side. Samples that could not be predicted (no reads in the reference
# taxa, step 3) are in no method's table, so the full_join with ext_info adds
# each of them once, with method and probabilities NA — they are not repeated
# per method.
external_predictions_df <- bind_rows(external_predictions) %>%
  full_join(ext_info, by = "Sample") %>%
  left_join(ext_qc, by = "Sample") %>%
  mutate(method_label = recode_method_labels(method)) %>%
  arrange(method, group, Sample)

# Apply the Platt correction (fitted in the Benchmark chunk, training data
# only) to the BEST model's external probabilities: an extra calibrated
# probability/response column pair, plus a raw-vs-calibrated balanced-accuracy
# table overall and per group. The other models keep raw values only.
if (!is.null(platt_cal) && exists("best_model_id")) {
  pos_col <- paste0("prob_", positive_class)
  neg_class <- setdiff(class_levels, positive_class)[1]
  best_rows <- !is.na(external_predictions_df$method) &
    external_predictions_df$method == best_model_id & !is.na(external_predictions_df[[pos_col]])
  raw_p <- pmin(pmax(external_predictions_df[[pos_col]][best_rows], 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  cal_p <- stats::plogis(platt_cal$intercept + platt_cal$slope * stats::qlogis(raw_p))
  external_predictions_df[[paste0(pos_col, "_calibrated")]] <- NA_real_
  external_predictions_df[[paste0(pos_col, "_calibrated")]][best_rows] <- cal_p
  external_predictions_df$response_calibrated <- NA_character_
  external_predictions_df$response_calibrated[best_rows] <-
    ifelse(cal_p >= (platt_cal$cut %||% 0.5), positive_class, neg_class)   # same rule as the raw labels

  score_cal <- external_predictions_df[best_rows & external_predictions_df$scoreable, ]
  if (nrow(score_cal) >= 2) {
    bacc_of <- function(resp, truth) {
      mean(c(mean(resp[truth == positive_class] == positive_class),
             mean(resp[truth == neg_class] == neg_class)))
    }
    cal_rows <- list(data.frame(
      group = "OVERALL", n = nrow(score_cal),
      bacc_raw = round(bacc_of(score_cal$response, score_cal$label), 4),
      bacc_calibrated = round(bacc_of(score_cal$response_calibrated, score_cal$label), 4)
    ))
    for (g in sort(unique(stats::na.omit(score_cal$group)))) {
      gi <- score_cal$group == g
      if (sum(gi) < 2) next
      cal_rows[[length(cal_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        group = g, n = sum(gi),
        bacc_raw = round(bacc_of(score_cal$response[gi], score_cal$label[gi]), 4),
        bacc_calibrated = round(bacc_of(score_cal$response_calibrated[gi], score_cal$label[gi]), 4)
      )
    }
    external_calibration <- bind_rows(cal_rows)
    cat(sprintf("\nExternal balanced accuracy, %s, raw vs Platt-calibrated threshold:\n", best_method))
    print(external_calibration)
    readr::write_csv(external_calibration, file.path(metrics_dir, "external_calibration.csv"))
  }
}

readr::write_csv(external_predictions_df, file.path(metrics_dir, "external_predictions.csv"))

# Per-class recall on the external samples that carry a training-set label.
# The helper wants columns named method / truth / response; here the label
# lives in `label`, and the prediction-only rows (controls, extra conditions)
# are dropped by the `scoreable` filter rather than by the helper's own NA
# check, so an unlabelled sample can never be counted as a miss.
external_by_class <- per_class_recall_table(
  external_predictions_df %>%
    filter(scoreable) %>%
    transmute(method, truth = label, response)
)
if (!is.null(external_by_class)) {
  cat("\nPer-class recall, external test set:\n")
  print(external_by_class, row.names = FALSE)
  readr::write_csv(external_by_class, file.path(metrics_dir, "per_class_recall_external.csv"))
}

# Overall external metrics: one row per method, n = scoreable samples, with
# the same readable measure labels as bench_df (label_measure_name in
# R/tabflux_scoring_helpers.R) so the tables can be compared directly.
if (length(external_metrics)) {
  external_metrics_df <- bind_rows(external_metrics) %>%
    rename_with(label_measure_name) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) %>%
    relocate(method, n)
  cat("\nExternal test metrics (scoreable samples):\n")
  print(external_metrics_df)
  readr::write_csv(external_metrics_df, file.path(metrics_dir, "external_test_metrics.csv"))

  external_ci_df <- bind_rows(external_ci) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) %>%
    relocate(method, learner_id, metric)
  cat("\nExternal bootstrap 95 % intervals (balanced accuracy, AUC):\n")
  print(external_ci_df %>% filter(metric %in% c("balanced accuracy", "auc")) %>%
          select(method, metric, estimate, ci_low, ci_high))
  readr::write_csv(external_ci_df, file.path(metrics_dir, "external_test_metrics_ci.csv"))

  # Benchmark vs external dumbbells: the outer-fold mean (+/- SD across
  # folds) against the external score (bootstrap interval), per metric and
  # method — the same figure the Performance Comparison section draws for an
  # internal test set. The external table uses method KEYS in its method
  # column; the plot wants the display labels, hence the relabelling.
  ext_for_plot <- external_metrics_df %>%
    mutate(learner_id = method, method = recode_method_labels(method))
  ext_dumbbells <- plot_dumbbell(bench_df, bench_spread, ext_for_plot, external_ci_df,
                                 test_label = "External test")
  print(ext_dumbbells$by_method)
  print(ext_dumbbells$by_metric)
}

if (length(external_group_metrics)) {
  external_group_metrics_df <- bind_rows(external_group_metrics) %>%
    rename_with(label_measure_name) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) %>%
    relocate(method, group, n)
  cat(sprintf("\nExternal test metrics per %s:\n", test_group))
  print(external_group_metrics_df)
  readr::write_csv(external_group_metrics_df,
                   file.path(metrics_dir, "external_test_metrics_by_group.csv"))

  # Balanced accuracy per group and method — the per-group answer for the
  # external data, mirroring the per-held-out-group figure for the training
  # studies. Chance is 1 / number of classes, taken from the classes the models
  # were trained on (task_train) rather than from whatever this external set
  # happens to contain: a group missing a class is still scored against all of
  # them.
  external_chance <- 1 / length(task_train$class_names)
  print(
    ggplot(external_group_metrics_df,
           aes(x = group, y = `balanced accuracy`, fill = method)) +
      geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = external_chance, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +
      geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("n=%d", n)),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
      labs(title = "External test set: balanced accuracy per group",
           subtitle = sprintf("Dotted grey = chance (%.2f).", external_chance),
           x = test_group, y = "Balanced accuracy", fill = "Method") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  )
}

# Probability strip: where does every sample land on the class axis, including
# the prediction-only ones (controls, extra conditions)? For binary tasks the
# y axis is P(positive class); unscoreable samples are hollow points.
if (dataset_attr == "binary" && nrow(external_predictions_df)) {
  positive_prob_col <- paste0("prob_", positive_class)
  if (positive_prob_col %in% names(external_predictions_df)) {
    print(
      ggplot(
        external_predictions_df %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[positive_prob_col]])),
        aes(x = group, y = .data[[positive_prob_col]],
            color = ifelse(scoreable, label, "not scored"), shape = scoreable)
      ) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = if (eval_prior_correction) mean(task_train$truth() == positive_class) else 0.5,
                   linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +   # where the labels are cut
        scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 1), guide = "none") +
        facet_wrap(~method_label) +
        labs(
          title = sprintf("External test set: P(%s) per sample", positive_class),
          x = test_group, y = sprintf("P(%s)", positive_class), color = "Label"
        ) +
        theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
              plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
    )
  }
}

}  # end of the if-block skipped when no external test set is configured
```

#### Feature Importance

Which taxa the best model uses, and in which direction. `importance.method` picks permutation importance (shuffle one taxon, measure how much the error rises) or SHAP (per-sample contribution of each taxon to the predicted probability). Written to `metrics/`. Skipped with `none`.

```{r importance, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Which taxa drive the best model's call, and in which direction? The model is
# best_model_id, picked in the Benchmark chunk from the cross-validated scores,
# never from the test split.
# Method from importance.method in the config (Set Parameters chunk):
#   "perm" – permutation importance: shuffle one feature, measure the loss
#   "shap" – Shapley values via the iml package, per sample and per class
#   "none" – skip
# Input: task_train (training samples, selected features) and the fitted learner
# (learners_best, or the .rds saved by the Train models chunk).
# Output: plots in the report and CSVs in metrics_dir —
# permutation_importance.csv, or shap_values.csv (per sample x feature x class),
# shap_importance.csv (global ranking) and shap_class_contributions.csv (per
# taxon and class: strength as mean |phi|, and direction, i.e. whether more of
# the taxon goes with a higher or lower probability of the class). Nothing here
# reads them back; they feed downstream interpretation.
#
# The skip is checked first, before the setup below loads (and, for TabPFN or a
# disk-loaded learner, retrains) the model and builds the iml Predictor.
if (importance_method == "none") {
  message("importance.method = 'none': skipping feature importance.")
} else {

# Run feature importance for the best-performing model (chosen in the Benchmark chunk).
method = best_model_id

# Belt-and-braces guard: the Import Data chunk already stops the run when
# `target` is missing from meta_df, so this branch cannot be skipped in a
# normal render. Kept for interactive runs where the import chunk was not
# executed; in that case the chunk silently does nothing.
if (target %in% colnames(meta_df)) {
  # Extract the training features and labels as plain data frames so the iml
  # Predictor can query the model freely without needing the mlr3 task wrapper.
  feature_cols <- task_train$feature_names
  temp_tab  <- task_train$data(cols = feature_cols) %>% as.data.frame()
  temp_tab  <- temp_tab[, feature_cols, drop = FALSE]
  temp_targ <- task_train$data(cols = "target")[["target"]]

  # Load the best learner, in this order: (1) the fitted object in
  # learners_best (Benchmark chunk), (2) the <method>_tuned_learner object the
  # Train models chunk left in the workspace, (3) the saved .rds file. Only
  # the .rds copy is re-trained on task_train here — it may carry the tuned
  # settings without a fitted model; the two in-memory objects are used as
  # they are. (TabPFN is re-trained further down after its settings change.)
  obj_name     <- paste(method, "tuned", "learner", sep = "_")
  learner_path <- file.path(save_dir, paste0(method, "_tuned_learner.rds"))
  imodel <- if (exists("learners_best")) learners_best[[method]] else NULL
  if (is.null(imodel) && exists(obj_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
    imodel <- get(obj_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
  if (is.null(imodel) && file.exists(learner_path)) {
    imodel <- readRDS(learner_path)
    if ("unmarshal" %in% names(imodel)) {
      try(imodel$unmarshal(), silent = TRUE)
    }
    imodel$train(task_train)
  }
  if (is.null(imodel)) {
    stop("No tuned learner available for feature importance: ", method)
  }

  # shap_sample_size (config importance.shap_sample_size, Set Parameters
  # chunk): how many random combinations of the other features iml averages
  # over to estimate each Shapley value. Larger = less noisy estimates,
  # proportionally slower. Only used in the "shap" branch.
  shap_sample_size <- shap_sample_size_default   # feature combinations per Shapley value
  # Which training rows to explain. SHAP costs rows x features x classes x
  # sample_size, so an uncapped training set of a few hundred rows can
  # dominate the whole run; shap_max_rows caps the rows explained. TabPFN gets
  # the tighter cap below.
  shap_row_ids <- seq_len(nrow(temp_tab))
  if (length(shap_row_ids) > shap_max_rows) {
    set.seed(seed)
    shap_row_ids <- sort(sample(shap_row_ids, size = shap_max_rows))
  }
  # Set a learner setting only if the learner has it. Works for both plain
  # learners and pipeline learners, where each setting is named after its
  # step (e.g. classif.tabpfn.device instead of device).
  set_param_if_present <- function(learner, ids, value) {
    hit <- ids[ids %in% learner$param_set$ids()]
    if (length(hit)) {
      learner$param_set$values[[hit[1]]] <- value
    }
    learner
  }
  
  # TabPFN SHAP is extremely slow (hundreds of model predictions per sample).
  # Switch to memory-saving inference, use fewer random feature combinations
  # per Shapley value (tabpfn_shap_sample_size) and explain at most
  # tabpfn_shap_max_rows training rows (both in config importance.*) so the
  # real run time stays manageable. The clone keeps learners_best untouched;
  # the changed settings only take effect after the re-train on task_train.
  if (importance_method == "shap" && identical(method, "tabpfn")) {
    imodel <- imodel$clone(deep = TRUE)
    imodel <- set_param_if_present(imodel, c("device", "classif.tabpfn.device"), "auto")
    imodel <- set_param_if_present(imodel, c("n_jobs", "classif.tabpfn.n_jobs"), 1L)
    imodel <- set_param_if_present(imodel, c("fit_mode", "classif.tabpfn.fit_mode"), "low_memory")
    imodel <- set_param_if_present(imodel, c("inference_precision", "classif.tabpfn.inference_precision"), "auto")
    imodel <- set_param_if_present(imodel, c("memory_saving_mode", "classif.tabpfn.memory_saving_mode"), "auto")
    imodel$train(task_train)
    shap_sample_size <- tabpfn_shap_sample_size
    if (length(shap_row_ids) > tabpfn_shap_max_rows) {
      set.seed(seed)
      shap_row_ids <- sort(sample(shap_row_ids, size = tabpfn_shap_max_rows))
    }
  }

  # A single-row data frame with the same column names, column types and
  # factor levels the training task had; used as a template to rebuild a
  # valid mlr3 task inside the prediction function.
  task_template <- as.data.frame(task_train$data()[1, , drop = FALSE])
  if ("target" %in% names(task_template)) {
    task_template$target <- factor(task_template$target, levels = levels(temp_targ))
  }
  task_roles <- task_train$col_roles  # preserve group/stratum roles when rebuilding tasks

  # iml (behind FeatureImp and Shapley below) treats the model as a black box it
  # queries through a Predictor object: data + labels + a function returning
  # class probabilities for any data frame. iml hands over plain data frames but
  # our learner expects an mlr3 task, so predict.function below stamps iml's
  # newdata onto task_template to restore column names, types and factor levels,
  # wraps it in a task, re-applies the original column roles (e.g. "group"), and
  # returns a plain probability data frame.
  temp_pred = Predictor$new(
    model = imodel,
    data = temp_tab,
    y = temp_targ,
    predict.function = function(model, newdata) {
      newdata <- as.data.frame(newdata)[, feature_cols, drop = FALSE]
      # Copy the template row for every new sample so column types and factor
      # levels stay exactly as in training
      pred_data <- task_template[rep(1, nrow(newdata)), , drop = FALSE]
      pred_data[, feature_cols] <- newdata
      if ("target" %in% names(pred_data)) {
        # Fill target with a dummy level; the actual value is not used during prediction
        pred_data$target <- factor(rep(levels(temp_targ)[1], nrow(pred_data)), levels = levels(temp_targ))
      }
      pred_task <- mlr3::as_task_classif(pred_data, target = "target")
      # Restore non-feature roles (group, stratum, etc.) so the learner doesn't complain
      for (role_name in setdiff(names(task_roles), c("feature", "target"))) {
        role_cols <- setdiff(intersect(task_roles[[role_name]], names(pred_data)), "target")
        if (length(role_cols)) {
          pred_task$set_col_roles(role_cols, role_name)
        }
      }
      as.data.frame(model$predict(pred_task)$prob)
    },
    type = "prob"
  )

  # Parallelise the permutation/SHAP model queries over num_threads background
  # R processes ("multisession"), but keep mlp and tabpfn sequential: they
  # already run multi-threaded (or on the GPU) internally, and adding R
  # workers on top would start more jobs than there are cores and slow
  # everything down.
  future::plan(sequential)
  if (!method %in% c("mlp", "tabpfn"))
    future::plan(future::multisession, workers = num_threads)
  
  if (importance_method == "perm") {
    # Permutation importance: shuffle one feature column at a time, breaking its
    # link to the labels, and measure how much the model's error rises. A large
    # increase = the feature matters. loss = "ce" is iml's classification error
    # (share of misclassified samples, Metrics::ce), NOT cross-entropy: iml
    # turns the probabilities into the most likely class before scoring.
    # compare = "difference" reports shuffled error minus original error.
    # n.repetitions = 100: each feature is shuffled 100 times, importance is the
    # median increase, importance.05/.95 the 5th and 95th percentile (error bars
    # below). Hard-coded, not in the config; lower it if this step is too slow.
    feat_imp = FeatureImp$new(
      temp_pred,
      loss = "ce",
      n.repetitions = 100,
      compare = "difference"
    )
    
    # One row per feature; nothing limits how many features are ranked or
    # plotted. distinct() is only a safety net against duplicated feature
    # rows in iml's results table.
    feat_imp_results <- feat_imp$results %>%
      dplyr::distinct(feature, .keep_all = TRUE)
    
    feat_imp_plot <- ggplot(feat_imp_results, aes(x = reorder(feature, importance), y = importance)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "mediumseagreen") +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = importance.05, ymax = importance.95), width = 0.4) +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(
        title = paste("Permutation importance of", methods[[method]], "model"),
        x = "Feature",
        y = "Importance (increase in classification error)"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.title  = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title  = element_text(size = 12)
      )
    
    show_and_save_figure(feat_imp_plot, paste0("importance_", importance_method), save_dir)
    readr::write_csv(feat_imp_results, file.path(metrics_dir, "permutation_importance.csv"))

  } else if (importance_method == "shap") {
    # Shapley values: phi = how far a feature's value in one sample moved the
    # predicted probability of a class away from the average prediction
    # (positive = towards that class). iml does one sample at a time, hence the
    # loop; mean |phi| per feature then gives a global ranking.
    # shap_row_ids = at most shap_max_rows training rows (tabpfn_shap_max_rows
    # for TabPFN, which is very slow per prediction), chosen above.
    shap_all <- purrr::map_dfr(shap_row_ids, function(i) {
      s <- Shapley$new(
        temp_pred,
        x.interest = temp_tab[i, , drop = FALSE],
        sample.size = shap_sample_size
      )
      s$results %>% dplyr::mutate(sample_id = i)
    })
    
    # Aggregate raw per-sample Shapley values into a global importance score:
    # mean |phi| across all samples and all classes. Higher = feature has a
    # larger average impact on model predictions regardless of direction.
    shap_agg <- shap_all %>%
      dplyr::group_by(feature) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(mean_abs_phi = mean(abs(phi)), .groups = "drop") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(mean_abs_phi))
    # (group_by(feature) already collapses samples and classes into one row
    # per feature, so nothing limits how many features are ranked)
    
    feat_imp_plot <- ggplot(shap_agg, aes(x = reorder(feature, mean_abs_phi), y = mean_abs_phi)) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "royalblue3") +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(
        title = paste("Mean |Shapley values| of", methods[[method]], "model"),
        x = "Feature",
        y = "Mean |Shapley value|"
      ) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.title  = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title  = element_text(size = 12)
      )
    
    show_and_save_figure(feat_imp_plot, paste0("importance_", importance_method), save_dir)

    # Per-sample SHAP export. Two fixes over the plain iml output:
    #  * sample_id from the SHAP loop is a POSITION in the training subset, not
    #    a task row id — translate through task_train$row_ids before joining
    #    sample names, or they are misaligned whenever the training task is a
    #    filtered subset of the full table.
    #  * iml's feature.value shows the value the MODEL saw (normalized), so the
    #    raw read count and the relative abundance are attached as well.
    shap_export <- shap_all %>%
      dplyr::mutate(row_id = task_train$row_ids[sample_id]) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(sample_lookup, by = "row_id")

    # tab_counts = raw counts kept aside in the Normalize Abundances chunk;
    # tab = the normalized table the models were trained on; library_sizes =
    # per-sample read totals from the same chunk. row_ids and sample_lookup
    # (Define Task chunk) translate task row ids back to sample names.
    counts_matrix <- as.matrix(tab_counts[, norm_feat_cols, drop = FALSE])
    model_matrix  <- as.matrix(tab[, norm_feat_cols, drop = FALSE])
    row_pos  <- match(shap_export$row_id, row_ids)                 # row in tab/tab_counts
    feat_pos <- match(shap_export$feature, norm_feat_cols)         # feature column
    shap_export$raw_count   <- counts_matrix[cbind(row_pos, feat_pos)]
    shap_export$proportion  <- shap_export$raw_count / library_sizes[row_pos]
    shap_export$value_model <- model_matrix[cbind(row_pos, feat_pos)]  # what the model saw (normalization applied)

    # ── Which taxa drive each class ─────────────────────────────────────────
    # One row per taxon x class, from the per-sample SHAP values above
    # (shap_class_summary(), R/tabflux_figure_helpers.R):
    #   mean_phi      – signed mean of phi, kept in the table for reference;
    #   mean_abs_phi  – mean |phi|: how far the taxon moves P(class), up or down
    #                   (the strength, and the bar length in the figure);
    #   direction_rho – Spearman correlation (a correlation on ranks) between
    #                   the taxon's value the model saw (value_model) and its
    #                   phi, across the explained samples; NA when either does
    #                   not vary;
    #   direction     – its sign in words: "more of it: higher P(class)",
    #                   "more of it: lower P(class)" or "no variation".
    # Why not the signed mean as the direction: SHAP values are measured
    # against the average prediction, so over the explained samples a taxon's
    # pushes up and down largely cancel. The signed mean is not a direction
    # and hides strong taxa: on the cFMD category run, S. thermophilus on dairy
    # has a signed mean of -0.001 but a mean |phi| of 0.114.
    shap_class_table <- shap_class_summary(shap_export)

    # The figure: the strongest taxa of each class by mean |phi|, coloured by
    # direction. Multi-class: one panel per class. Binary: one panel for the
    # positive class (set in the Preprocess Data chunk), so the colours point
    # the same way as every binary metric.
    class_imp_plot <- plot_shap_by_class(
      shap_class_table,
      method_label = methods[[method]],
      positive_class = if (dataset_attr == "binary") positive_class else NULL
    )
    # Export size grows with the number of panels, two per row: the seven cFMD
    # categories make four rows (10.8 in tall), a binary target one (4.2 in).
    # The default 10 x 6.5 in would squeeze a multi-class figure.
    n_panels <- if (dataset_attr == "binary") 1L else length(unique(shap_class_table$class))
    show_and_save_figure(class_imp_plot, "importance_by_class", save_dir,
                         width = 11, height = 2 + 2.2 * ceiling(n_panels / 2))

    # Exports: per sample (shap_values.csv), global ranking
    # (shap_importance.csv) and per taxon x class (shap_class_contributions.csv,
    # columns feature, class, mean_phi, mean_abs_phi, direction_rho, direction).
    readr::write_csv(shap_export,      file.path(metrics_dir, "shap_values.csv"))
    readr::write_csv(shap_agg,         file.path(metrics_dir, "shap_importance.csv"))
    readr::write_csv(shap_class_table, file.path(metrics_dir, "shap_class_contributions.csv"))
  }
}

# Shut down the worker processes started for the importance calculation, so
# they do not linger after the render (or keep running in an interactive
# session and slow down whatever comes next).
future::plan(sequential)

}  # end of the if-block skipped when importance.method = "none"
```
